steps.text: Welcome to the walkthrough for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33! Despite bouncing off the game when it first released, I tried it again later on and it blew me away. For me this wasn't just a "good" game, it was a ground-breaking one. The story, the soundtrack and the twists and turns are things I thought about months after finishing and the E33 "Sweep" at the game awards also served to cement its place as one of the greats.

The completion itself is fairly chilled out if you play on the lowest difficulty, with combat being more difficult on higher modes dependent on your own ability to dodge and parry. There are no achievements related to difficulty and everything can be obtained in one playthrough. The walkthrough is written with spoilers in mind and I have gone out of my way to try and obscure story elements as much as possible. Part of the joy of this game is figuring out bosses for yourself and feeling super clever when it all clicks. At the same time, I appreciate this might not be for everyone, so each boss has its entire move-set listed out, along with any relevant tips or additional info.

The walkthrough isn't written with just achievements in mind, nor is it a 100% item walkthrough. I wanted to do something in the middle that helps the reader obtain multiple items and skills not linked to achievements but without being overwhelming to the point that every little thing is pointed out. I think I've found a good balance where you will see most of what the game has to offer without going too far off the beaten track. I have tried to pack as much as possible into the guide so that you should rarely need to look elsewhere, if at all, including a separate page which consists of a comprehensive collectible checklist.
With all this being said, it really is a phenomenal experience and I hope you all enjoy it as much as I did.

sections.title: 2. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 General hints and tips

steps.text: There are 55 achievements to collect during your expedition. There are no achievements related to difficulty. The walkthrough is written based on the "normal" or "expeditioner" difficulty as it's known in game. How you play is entirely up to you when it comes to preferred characters, builds and strategies. When it comes to dealing with enemies and bosses, my aim is to give you as much information as I can on what attacks can happen and how they look.
steps.heading: Overview

steps.text: I have tried to keep the WT as spoiler-free as possible because this game is one that should not be spoilt at all. I would strongly advise that you do not scroll past your current spot in the WT though as even location names may spoil things and I can't avoid everything entirely. Whilst this isn't a 100% walkthrough, I will be pointing out some optional items that will help improve your characters and skills such as Pictos, Colours of Lumina, Chroma and weapons. It is up to you whether you collect these but the majority are barely off the beaten path.
There are FIVE MISSABLE achievements in the game:
steps.heading: Achievement Breakdown

steps.text: 1) The Follow the trail achievement is related to collecting all journals in the game. There is one missable journal that requires the "Old Key" item found in the prologue to collect. The item will be pointed out and emphasised in the prologue. Update: This is no longer missable as of the "Thank you" update. If the "Old Key" is not collected in the prologue, it can be found in Act 3 and will be pointed out in the guide.

steps.name: Follow The Trail
steps.description: Find all of the journals from prior expeditions.

steps.text: 2) The Maelle achievement is related to reaching Maelle's final relationship rank. You can be locked out of this if you choose to lie to Maelle instead of telling the truth. This will be emphasised at the time. If you choose to lie, your relationship will not rank up. You can load an earlier save if you mess this one up, provided you realise quickly as the game only uses autosaves and after a while you won't be able to go back far enough.

3) The Connoisseur achievement is related to collecting 33 of the 34 music records in the game. There are 2 missable records so you can miss one but not both. One missable record is in the prologue and the other is obtainable during a certain interaction at camp. Both will be pointed out and emphasised. If you do miss collecting both, you will be unable to get this achievement in your current playthrough.

4) The Peculiar Encounter achievement is related to defeating the Mime enemy in the prologue. This is required anyway for one of the missable records and will be pointed out. If you miss the Mime, you won't be able to get this achievement on your current playthrough but as it is near the start, you can quickly get it on a fresh save if needed.

5) The Professional achievement is related to defeating a boss without taking damage. Technically this is missable as there is only a finite number of bosses in the game. There are a couple of easier chances to get this early on, either by legitimately avoiding every move one of the early bosses does or by leaving one of the optional bosses up until much later in the game then coming back and killing it instantly, unlocking the achievement.

steps.name: Professional
steps.description: Defeat a boss without taking any damage.

steps.text: The rest of the achievements cover a wide range of activities, from passing certain story points to completing side activities, finding lost NPCs, using each character in battle in a certain way and more. There are a number of optional bosses and post-game things to do also but everything other than the above five achievements can be obtained post-game if you miss anything. The WT does not cover the free DLC area as there are no achievements linked to it.
There are quite a few different items in game and it can be a bit daunting at first understanding what everything does. Below is a brief explanation of the main items and abilities in game.
steps.heading: Items Overview

steps.text: Chroma is the games currency and is typically found as a white item pickup. Chroma is used to buy items from merchants such as hairstyles, outfits, pictos, Colour of Lumina, recoats and weapon upgrade materials. If you pick it up as you go, you should easily have enough on hand to always buy what you want. Unless you're going for literally every single item from every merchant, it's unlikely you would ever need to farm this.
steps.heading: Chroma

steps.text: You will be introduced to the Pictos system shortly into the game. Pictos are passive abilities that you can use to create different builds and give your characters different effects. When you loot a new Pictos, it must be equipped on a character. Equipping a Pictos on a character requires Lumina Points and will give that specific character the passive effect. Win 4 battles with the Pictos equipped and it can then be equipped on any character as a passive. This still requires Lumina Points but does not require the Pictos to be equipped. The general way to do it is to always "equip" a new Pictos to a character until you win 4 battles with it. You can then swap it out for another Pictos and learn that one.
steps.heading: Pictos

steps.text: The Colour of Lumina item is used in the upgrade menu to give one of your characters an extra Lumina point. This is typically found as a blue item pickup. As mentioned above when discussing Pictos, Lumina Points are needed to equip different passive effects learnt from Pictos. The effects can require anywhere from 1 to 20 or more Lumina points to use so Colour of Lumina is useful to make sure you can equip many passives on your characters. As with Chroma, for a standard playthrough you will find more than enough Colour of Lumina items to be able to increase your characters Lumina Points comfortably as there are many world pickups and they can be bought from vendors.
steps.heading: Colour of Lumina

steps.text: The Recoat is an item which allows you to respec a character's attribute or skill points. Useful for re-allocating the stats on your character or if you want to try out different skills. These are typically found as red item pickups and can be bought from vendors. You will naturally find more than enough Recoats throughout the game so don't worry about accidentally putting attribute or skill points in the wrong place.
steps.heading: Recoat

steps.text: These are your weapon upgrade materials and come in 5 different forms ranging from standard to grandiose to perfect and more. Each and every weapon in the game can be levelled up to a max level of 33. Every few levels will require the next type of chroma catalyst. This effectively gates you from leveling a weapon too high before the story ends.
steps.heading: Chroma Catalysts

steps.text: Tints come in 3 forms - Energy (AP), Health and Revive. Picking up tint shards will increase the number of each tint you can have, whilst collecting the Shape of Life, Energy and Revive items will increase the potency of the tints. Tints can be used in battle to replenish health, AP or to revive characters.
steps.heading: Tints

steps.text: Your tints will refresh to full every time you rest at a flag. There is a 4th type of tint entitled the Chroma Elixir. This is something you can use outside of battle to replenish your entire party to full health. As with the aforementioned tints, picking up Chroma Elixir Shards will increase the amount you have. These too, are refreshed whilst resting at a flag.
Reminder - There is one missable achievement and two missable items in the prologue.
steps.heading: Prologue - Lumiére

steps.text: Choose your desired difficulty, watch the opening cutscene and let's begin! Following the cutscene, take in the view for a moment, listen to the soothing music and then look to your left. On the small bench in front of you, press when prompted to collect A Flower for Sophie. Turn to your left again and move forward to Maelle. She will sprint away. Follow her, using to run. There are no pickups in this area, so don't worry about missing anything.

When you reach Maelle she will mention grapple hooks. Move to the edge of the platform and press to grapple to the next roof. Continue to follow Maelle, grappling to another two roofs until you reach a bridge. This begins the combat tutorial which explains the basics such as the battle wheel, turn order (timeline), basic attacks and skills as well as the real time dodging and parrying. You will receive a Colour of Lumina for winning.

Back in control, continue to follow Maelle until you reach the edge of a roof with a beam of light. These essentially act as ropes that you can move up and down. Move to this one and press to descend. At the bottom, move to the people in front of you for a cutscene. Back in control you will see you are now Sophie. Pressing will change you back to Gustave and can be used throughout the game to cycle between characters. This has no impact on story and is purely personal taste outside of a couple of niche scenarios.

There are a lot of people to talk to and items to collect in this area now. It is all optional so if you do just want to collect the missable items, skip to the MISSABLE tag below and read from there. If you receive a pop-up asking you if you are ready to go to the harbour, press NO unless you have the missable items as this is a point of no return.

Now, for those who want to see some of the optional parts of this area, speak to the flower stall woman ahead for a short conversation. Dialogue choices in this game generally don't matter outside of one very specific scenario which will be pointed out. Turn left after the conversation and head forward, following the street round to the right until you emerge in a large open area with lots of people. You can speak to the woman and child right in front of you here for some more dialogue if you wish.

Turn right and head forward after the conversation and you should see a white item pickup on your right on top of some pallets. Move behind them to the left and use to climb onto the shorter stack and then run and press again to jump over to collect 125x Chroma. Drop down from here and head right, following the path around. You will see another large street to your right with a statue. Move past this for now and on your right will be what looks like lots of blue stone. There is a bathtub on the ground in front of it. Head to this and a prompt will appear. Choose to [Examine] and you will receive a Colour of Lumina.

Now head back to the street with the statue. On your left, shortly down this path will be a man in a red suit. Speak to him to obtain A Uniform for Richard's Son. Continue down the street until you see the banner with "Expedition" written on it. To the left of this is a woman wearing black. Speak to her and you'll end up in a battle. Just keep attacking the target until your overcharge is at 10/10 then use the overcharge skill to win. You will receive a Colour of Lumina.

Continue to head down the street, between the market stalls until you reach another open area. Speak to the man over by the canvas on the left side to trigger another battle. This is a good way to practice dodging. Dodge all of Sophie's attacks to win and receive a Recoat. Now look to your right and move to the stairs on your left. There will be a rubbish bin on your right. Interact with it a few times to receive a Chroma Catalyst.

Head down the street between more stalls until the area opens up again with a fountain in the middle. This is the final part of this area. If you head forward from the fountain you will receive the pop-up about leaving the area. Looking at the fountain from where you entered this area from, turn right. You will see a stage ahead with what looks like fireworks going off.
steps.heading: MISSABLE

steps.text: Head to the right of the stage in the picture to find the mime. Interact with it to begin a battle.

Whilst I do cover general movesets and give a few tips in how to deal with bosses in this game, part of the fun in my opinion at least, is learning how the fights work yourself. There is a certain joy in figuring out a bosses movesets and how to parry back accordingly.

However, this isn't for everyone so the movesets and any additional information I deem useful are included for every boss just in case. I have tried to keep the guide as spoiler-lite as possible but I would strongly advise that you don't scroll too far ahead in general. There are three achievements related to killing this enemy. He drops a missable item so it's imperative you kill him now. Remember that you can always drop difficulties if struggling and then change it back up later.
Hand to Hand Combo: A simple 3-hit combo. The first two hits are fast, followed by a short delay before hit 3.
steps.heading: Mime - Attacks

steps.text: Strange Combo: A slightly trickier 4-hit combo. The first two hits are quite fast, followed by a short delay before hits 3 and 4.

This may take a few goes whilst you get used to combat. The mime takes virtually no damage unless it is in a broken state so the ideal strategy is to parry/dodge and attack until you do enough damage to "break" it. Build your overcharge to 10/10 and then use it to break the enemy, unlocking the below three achievements.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.name: Overcharge
steps.description: With Gustave, use a fully charged Overcharge that Breaks an enemy.

steps.text: For defeating the mime, you will obtain [Music Record #1/34 - Lumiére]. Now turn around and head to the other side of this area. Left, if you were looking at the fountain. You will see more of that blue rock stuff on the left. There is a white item to pick up here for 125x Chroma.

That's everything for this area so it's time to carry on with the story now. When you are ready, head to the only place we haven't been yet, down to the harbour, opposite the street we came down with the stalls. You will get a pop-up asking you if you want to go the harbour. MISSABLE This is your LAST chance to kill the Mime and collect the music record. If ready, press yes and watch the cutscene.
When back in control you will be in a small area of the harbour. Before doing anything else, let's get the last missable of the prologue. Head down the stairs to see a green, red and blue tent.

You will have a Festival Token automatically from the cutscene. Speak to the woman in the blue tent and exchange the token for the Old Key. You will need this later to obtain a journal and this is the only time you can get it.
steps.heading: MISSABLE

steps.text: There's some more optional stuff to mop up now and some more items to get. If you want to continue on with the story, speak to the three children at the back of this area and then to the woman at the entrance of the area to initiate the cutscene and the end of the prologue.

If you want to item hunt, then let's do it! Opposite the green and red stalls is a ramp leading down to the water. Speak to the boy in red stood near the left pillar to hand over the uniform you got given earlier and receive the Crimson Uniform customization option (you won't be able to use it yet). Now head down the ramp and speak to Maelle for a rematch. Defeat her to receive another Festival Token.

Head back up the ramp and speak to the man at the green tent, trading your festival token for the Weird Pictos. The woman at the red tent gives you a hairstyle cosmetic option for Gustave, again in exchange for a festival token. Personally, I left this one but if you want the third token you need to speak to the man in the white outfit near the blue tent and take his quiz. Answering all 3 questions correctly will give you the last festival token.

With all that done, it's now time to continue the story and finish the prologue. Move to the back of the area from where you entered and speak with the children for a cutscene. Make sure you have obtained the Old Key item from the blue tent; this is your last chance. Now go back to the entrance of this area and speak with the woman to begin a cutscene. This ends the prologue and awards the below achievement.

sections.title: 4. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Act I - Part 1

steps.text: Spring Meadows
steps.heading: Act I - Part I

steps.text: Once back in control after that rollercoaster intro, you find yourself in the first area of the main game, "Spring Meadows". As with the prologue, I'll point out optional items that aren't far off the beaten path, it's up to you whether you collect them. This isn't a 100% guide but it will allow you to have a good stock of pictos, lumina points and recoats so that you can build characters without worry. First things first, turn around and go to the waterfall in front of you. There is a white item to pick up here. Collect it for 180x Chroma.

Turn around and follow the path ahead until you trigger a pop up about Chroma Elixirs and the UI. It's important to remember that Elixirs, like the healing/revive/AP tints, also renew when resting. So, feel free to use them as much as needed. Continue forward until you reach a cutscene and find yourself in a battle where you will learn about Free Aim. Free aim is good for hitting weak spots but there are also many pictos which will enhance your free aim abilities, should you choose to build a character this way. Defeat the enemy for a cutscene. Back in control, continue forwards and grapple up to the next area.

Continue to follow the path and scale the wall via the handholds. Continue onward for another cutscene, after which you will find yourself fighting once more. You'll be introduced to your first new party member and her battle mechanics. After winning the battle, you will receive your first Pictos - "Dodger". You can equip this Pictos now on either party member. An equipped Pictos will only give the passive benefit to that party member. After winning four battles with it equipped, you will master the Pictos. The passive ability it gives can then be added to any character in the party, provided they have the right amount of Lumina points.

I will not be telling you what builds to use, pictos/skills to equip or where to put attribute points. It's entirely up to you and there is no "wrong" way to do it. With that out of the way, we continue. Remember that you can press to swap characters if you wish. Continue following the path until you reach your first Expedition Flag. Resting at a flag will restore all health to your party but will respawn enemies, as well as your tints and elixirs. You can also learn new skills and distribute attribute points at the flags. Have a play around and when ready, back out to continue onward into another battle.

After winning, head up the ramp on your right and loot 180x Chroma. Drop down and turn right. Continue ahead a short distance and you will see another path off to your right. Take this to find the "Critical Burn" pictos. Remember to equip it on someone. Even if you don't think you will ever use a certain pictos, it's still worth equipping on a character for those four battles so that you have it available for all characters if needed. Now, go back to the main path and forward until another enemy jumps down, triggering another battle.

Directly left after the battle there is a path you can go up for some more Chroma if you wish. Either way, head into the building ahead and immediately on your right is a purple item pickup. Collect it for a Chroma Catalyst, an item used to upgrade weapons to level 9. Take the debris ramp upstairs and then go up the rope. Turn right and go down the stairs. Turn around at the bottom and underneath the stairs is an Energy Tint Shard. If you press and look to the bottom right, you will see you now have two of the blue energy tints. Go through the hole in the wall and to the right for 360x Chroma, then head back upstairs and this time leave the building through the open wall on the right. Take in the view, it really is a gorgeous game.

You should see the next flag ahead and to the right. Make sure to rest and assign attribute points/new skills. The main path to continue the story is right from the flag, so we will go left first. With the cliff edge on your right side, follow it around to 180x Chroma, then cross over and head to the wall opposite to find another 180x Chroma. Defeat the enemy on the path here and ahead you will find yet another 180x Chroma. There is a grapple point above you that eventually leads to a Mime enemy. Defeating it awards the baguette outfit for Gustave. The moveset is the exact same as Lumiére and generally every Mime enemy in the game uses this exact moveset.

Once defeated, head back to the flag and rest, allocating any new points. Now we go right and defeat the big enemy ahead. Loot the Colour of Lumina afterward from the tree on the right, then follow the path and climb onto the small ledge. Follow the path around to the left, under the collapsed stone and up the hill. You'll see a tent ahead, approaching it will start a battle. After the fight, there is a rope ahead and before this, a path to the right.

Down the path on the right is an optional boss. Whilst it is possible to fight this boss and get the achievement for defeating a boss without taking damage, it is quite tough at the moment. Personally, I got frustrated fighting this boss at this point, whilst I was still learning dodging/parrying and I found it easier to come back with more hours into the game and with stronger characters that could one-shot it. Note that you can come back at any time you wish to fight it, you don't have to leave it until I do.

Either way, when ready to proceed with the story, go up the rope. At the top, head straight ahead and you will see another ledge below. Collect 720x Chroma on the left side of this. Climb back up and turn left, grappling across the gap. As you round the corner to the left, there is another big enemy to fight. After the battle, go down the path behind where the enemies were to loot 180x Chroma. Now return to the main path and climb up the handholds. Follow the linear path for a cutscene, after which you will obtain you first journal [Journal #1/49 - Expedition 81].

The white NPC in front of you is one of many we will do side-quests for. It is imperative that you DO NOT kill them, when given the option as keeping all of them alive will award you with a whopping 100x Lumina Points in the post-game. You don't void any achievements if you do accidentally kill any, but the Lumina Points is a good reward for not doing so. Rest at the flag and allocate points if you wish, then continue onward. You may have noticed that the flag now has an option to fast travel. This will only ever be fast travel within one area, not the world at large. Head through the tunnel and turn right at the end, following the path all the way around until you can loot the "Dead Energy II" pictos hidden in a barrel. Make sure to equip it! Go back the way you came, past the tunnel you emerged from and straight ahead to the edge where you can loot another pictos - "Burning Shots".

Turn around and head forwards to fight an enemy. After the battle, look to the right, and hidden away is a Colour of Lumina. Looking back ahead, you will see the path splits. This area is just one loop, with an exit at the other end, so it doesn't really matter where you go. We will take the left/upper path to start. Defeat the enemy and loot the Chroma Catalyst behind it. Return to the fork and now go right/down. Defeat the enemy and then loot the Colour of Lumina from under the bridge. After defeating the next enemy, collect the purple item hidden in the barrels to receive a Resin. Take the left path ahead, instead of going up and follow it to the end for a Revive Tint Shard, upping your total to two.

Head up the ramp and rest at the next flag, then fast travel back to "Abandoned Expeditioner Camp". Speak to the white Nevron if you haven't already and give him the resin. You may need to speak to him twice if you didn't previously. When back in control, hold and shoot the lamp he is carrying to light it. Speak to him again and cycle through the dialogue to receive a Healing Tint Shard. Now speak to the Nevron a final time. Cycle through the dialogue and DO NOT pick the option to attack. This completes [Nevron Quest #1/10]. With that dealt with, you can fast travel from the flag back to "The Indigo Tree". When ready, head forward for a cutscene and a boss fight.
Ice Attack: A 3 hit combo that hits a single character, a single character, and then both characters. The best time to counter is shortly after seeing the second ice patch appear on the ground.
steps.heading: Eveque - Attacks

steps.text: Spear Attack: A one-handed 1 hit attack with quite a long wind up, parry just before it connects.
Double Spear Attack: Same as above, just with two spears. It's just one hit, with a long wind-up. Again, parry just before it connects.
Charged Ice Attack: This is the ice attack again but with more hits. The counter is the same, just after the second ice patch appears.

It's entirely possible to do this fight without taking damage given the attacks are quite easy to counter. Again, I will be doing that achievement later but it's completely feasible to learn this boss and do it now if you wish.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: This boss introduces the concept of shields. Each shield take one hit to remove. Free aim works, and attacks with multiple hits will remove a shield per hit. You can shoot Eveque's weak spot through the shield and doing so will remove two shields for the price of one. After doing enough damage, you will see a popup that says, "Eveque feels threatened". Shortly after this message, it will summon two extra enemies.

Focus on them and remove them quickly so you have less attacks to avoid overall, shooting their weak spots to do a good chunk of damage. After you've weakened the boss more, it will create 8 more shields. Gustave's Lumiére Assault is good here as you can remove 5 shields in one go and then use free aim with Lune to get the other 3 off if you have the AP. You will see a message saying that "Eveque is charging up". The boss does this twice before reaching full power. It then performs the charged ice attack described above and then cycles between a few normal attacks before charging again.
For defeating the boss, you will get a cutscene and unlock:

steps.name: Spring Meadows
steps.description: Find your way through Spring Meadows.

steps.text: When back in control, turn around and follow the path to the end for the "Empowering Attack" pictos. Now head back and look out for a rope on your left. Take this down for a Colour of Lumina, then take it back up and continue onward to leave this area and emerge on the world map!

The Continent is the world map for this game. If you look behind you, you will see what looks like a white swirling effect. This signifies the entrance to an area. Pressing will bring up the map. You can see our next objective, Flying Waters, is to the North-East. There are multiple optional areas you can explore right now but the WT continues towards the end of Act I's story before going back to hoover up some goodies. Some locations are too difficult right now and some are locked off entirely until later in the game. When ready, head towards our objective and before long you will be prompted to press to go to camp.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: The camp is an area you can visit whenever you're on the world map. It allows you to speak to your party members for extra story (and later, relationship levels). You can also upgrade weapons, tints and assign Lumina points here when the functions unlock. No camp interactions are missable as you can always catch up later should you miss any. There is ONE interaction that you must do at a certain time for a record but as always, this will be pointed out.
steps.heading: Camp

steps.text: After the cutscene, you are free to roam around the camp. There isn't much to see on this visit other than to interact with the campfire. You can choose to write in Gustave's journal if you wish and then sleep to proceed. When back on the world map, continue to our objective and enter the next area.

Head forward for a cutscene and then turn left and move forward to the edge of the area. Turn left and follow this path to the end for the "SOS Shell" pictos. Head to the back of this area and a message will popup telling you about the paint cage. When facing the cage, turn left 90 degrees and you will see the first lock on the wall in front of you. Shoot it with free aim. Turn left another 90 degrees so you are facing the direction you came from and the second lock will be right in front of you, on the tail of the statue. Finally, turn 90 degrees a third time and the final lock is on the wall here, hidden behind the air bubble and purple corals. Shoot it to open the paint cage, loot the Chroma Elixir Shard and unlock:
steps.heading: Flying Waters

steps.text: Now continue on the main path, to the left of where the cage was, looting 333x Chroma from a body on the left as you go. Emerge into a more open area for a new enemy type to fight. Afterwards, head left and you'll see the main path with lanterns on it. If you go left first, you can follow the path to the end where you can fight two more enemies and loot the "Marking Shots" pictos. Follow the main path now, into an area with lots of mines and will find yourself in a battle. Use free aim against the mine enemies to shoot the mines, deal extra damage and set them on fire. Finish them off with free aim shots as they will dodge normal attacks.

After the battle, take the right path first to fight again, looting the Chroma Catalyst afterwards. Follow the main path, fighting another battle at the bottom of the hill. To the right of the passage is a purple item pickup. You will be ambushed by three of the mine enemies after picking it up. Now go through the passage with the lanterns into another open area. Head behind the structure to loot 665x Chroma. Now go to the entrance for a cutscene. There is a flag to your left after the cutscene if you want to rest up and assign points.

When ready, head up the stairs and then right up another set. At the top, turn left and climb a third set. Go along the corridor until you reach the open door on your right. Enter for a cutscene. When back in control return to the top of the stairs and turn right. Head straight across the landing and jump into the painting on the other side to go through it. Loot the Shape of Life item. Unlike the other tint items you've collected so far, this one isn't automatically applied. This item increases the amount of health revived allies come back with, not the number of revive tints. It needs to be upgraded at camp once we have the ability.

Now return back to the top of the first set of stairs, which lead down to the flag. Run down the corridor in between the left/right sets of stairs. We have a record to get here but it requires a few things first. There are four ornaments in the room that must be interacted with.
The first is to the right as you enter the dining room.
The second is at the back of the room, on the back side of a pillar
Facing the second, turn right and run straight to the wall to find this third ornament.
For the final one, look to the left of the fireplace.
With all four ornaments interacted with, a trap door opens next to the 4th one. Crawl through and smash the boxes with to loot [Record #2/34 - Nocturne pour un masque de tristesse].

Now go back to the flag and you will be able to assign Maelle's attribute points and skills (don't forget to equip learnt pictos on her too!). It may be worth speaking to the NPC by the entrance first so you get a sense of how she works in combat before picking skills but it's up to you. After you've spoken to the NPC and completed Maelle's battle tutorial, leave the manor for a cutscene. You will get a popup afterwards telling you about how Merchants work. There is a unique mechanic in this game where some merchants can be fought in order to unlock an extra item to buy.

Try it now by speaking to this one. You will be prompted to select one character and then will find yourself in a one on one battle with the merchant. Defeat it to unlock the "Exposing Attack" pictos in the Merchant inventory. As a general rule of thumb, I always try to buy all of a Merchant's wares outside of cosmetics. This just means I never miss a pictos and am always fully stocked on useful items, although this can be a bit pricey in the early game.

Once you're ready to proceed, head forward past the merchant to a flag. It's unlikely you'll need anything but you may as well rest anyway. Head down the path past the flag, looting a Chroma Catalyst on your right as you go. You will emerge in another large open area. First things first, we have our second Nevron quest to do. The enemies ahead drop a weapon for Maelle, so are worth fighting. Afterwards, head left. An enemy will jump out. Defeat it, then turn to your right where you will see another enemy roaming. Remember the path through the ship to your left as this continues the story. For now though, defeat the enemy pacing ahead and then continue straight on until you see an opening in the shell ahead.

To the left of this, climb onto the low platform to loot a Recoat. You can then jump to the next platform along and follow the series of handholds and grapples to the end of a high path where the "Augmented Aim" pictos is located. Now return to the opening in the shell and go through. Shortly inside you will find our Nevron. Interact with it and choose to [Examine], NOT [Attack] to learn it needs a mine. Head to its right to see a series of platforms. Jump across straight and then to the right to pull up onto a bigger island. Go straight ahead to another circular platform on your right. You will see the purple item pickup in the distance.

It's not super obvious but jump from this platform to the spiky area on the right and then jump across to the item. Loot it and drop down ahead of you. Then just run back to the shell tunnel and interact with the Nevron again and give it the mine to receive a new weapon for Lune. I always speak to them again to make sure but this completes [Nevron Quest #2/10]. Now you can return to the path through the ship that we ignored earlier. You will see a large enemy ahead that looks like it is forging something. You can run past it if you really want but it drops a weapon for Gustave and you can loot 2x Chroma Catalyst from behind the anvil.

Continue on to reach the next flag. Rest and sort skills/pictos as necessary, then hug and follow the right wall around to loot the "Staggering Attack" pictos. Now go to the left wall opposite the flag and follow this round to 333x Chroma. Continue following the wall and an enemy will jump out. This is the same as the one you just fought at the forge. After the battle, go to the wall that the enemy burst from and turn left to loot the "Rewarding Mark" pictos. Turn around from this and ahead you'll see more lanterns. Go to them and head forwards. You will hear a growl. If you look to your right, there is an area where you can drop down. Grapple across the gap in this reddish area and follow the path out to a large area with some mines. You should see the paint cage across from you. As with the first one we did, there are three "locks" in this area that need to be shot with free aim.
Grapple across to your left and turn to the right. You can see Lock #1 across from you
Turn left and grapple across the next gap. Turn around and Lock #2 will be on the mine directly in front of you.

Climb up the platform opposite the mine and jump across the circular pillars to reach a path uphill. Loot a Colour of Lumina at the top. Drop off this ledge and head to the left. You'll see the paint cage ahead and another big enemy wandering around. Lock #3 is immediately to the right of the paint cage.

Defeat the enemy, shoot the third lock and loot a Revive Tint Shard, increasing your total to three. Now backtrack to where you dropped down and climb back up. Shortly along the path, on your right, is [Journal #2/49 - Expedition 68]. Continue forward into an open area with a giant Nevron in the distance. Turn right and you will see handholds ahead. There is an optional Mime fight if you go through the corals to the left, before the handholds. It drops a haircut for Maelle and 2x Chroma Catalysts. You can also loot a Colour of Lumina from the area behind it.

Either way, climb the handholds when ready. You'll see the path split, with the left leading upwards and the right through some coral. Go left first and rest at the flag. Now, the right path you ignored leads to an optional boss. It does drop an item you will eventually need for a Nevron quest but there are other bosses that do. I found this boss tough my first time through but it's totally doable. It's just up to your personal skill and whether you want to learn it now or go for it later. It also drops a weapon for Gustave and a pictos.

Eat: On its first turn, the boss will always eat one party member, this cannot be dodged or avoided. Breaking the boss will cause the boss to spit the party member back out. The boss will then eat another party member a few turns later.
steps.heading: Bourgeon - Attacks

steps.text: Miasma Spit: The boss spits out four globs of Miasma. Characters hit become exhausted, stopping them from gaining AP. There is a nice rhythm to this and you only need to parry the final glob to perform a counter.
3 Hit Combo: This is just three quick hits back to back. No delays to throw you off.
5 Hit Combo: This was the hardest to time for me. it's two quick hits followed by a pause and then three hits back to back.

This boss caused me a lot of trouble the first time, if nothing else just because he has a lot of health and higher difficulties hit way harder. He will ALWAYS eat one party member shortly into the fight and they will remain out of action until the boss is broken. If there is a character you feel you can't play without, you can always restart the fight if they are eaten as it is random who is eaten on each attempt. Just like the mimes, he only has a couple of attacks and once you learn them, you will blitz him. The miasma spit is the easiest move to parry and you can sometimes have him do this repeatedly. I believe there is also a 4 hit combo variant but I didn't personally see it in my run.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: When ready to carry on, look at the area past the flag to find that the path splits. There is an optional boss to the left, the story continues to the right. I've listed both paths so it's up to where you go. The optional boss guards a pictos and it drops a weapon for Lune. If not interested in this, just read on from story path below.

Take the left path ahead and you'll see handholds. Climb them and defeat the enemy at the top. Run up the incline here and turn left. Ahead of you, across a gap, you will see more handholds. You can grapple over here. Once across, run around the building and loot a Chroma Catalyst at the end. Head down the path to the left of the item and you will see a grapple point below. Head down here to find the optional boss.
steps.heading: Optional Boss Path

steps.text: Tricky Shot: This one is a bait. You will see two orbs fly out from the boss. Ignore them! He will physically attack you with this trumpet first. Dodge/parry this, then do the orbs.
steps.heading: Chromatic Troubadour - Attacks

steps.text: Trumpet Concerto: This is a 3 hit attack with the trumpet. There is a fairly long wind-up before the first hit and then between each attack.

Chromatic bosses are just suped up versions of regular enemies. We skipped one earlier as it's a good candidate for the no damage achievement. This guy isn't too bad but the moves are annoying. In the end, I actually found the tricky shot easier once I was aware of the bait. The concerto caught me off guard quite a few times with the delays and slow hits. Loot the "Energising Break" pictos from behind the boss and then return to the flag.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Take the right path and follow it to another flag. Odd right? Boss battle ahead. Rest up and sort skills as necessary. Check Gustave's weapon. You may still have Cruleram equipped. If you do, swap it out for something as the boss is resistant to ice.
steps.heading: Story Path

steps.text: Jump Attack: Every person I've seen play this fight, including me, has the initial reaction to try and jump counter this. I think it's just because it says "Goblu Jumps" and you've just learnt jump counters. Just dodge/parry normally though. It's 3 bounces back to back with a short delay.
steps.heading: Goblu - Attacks

steps.text: 2/4 Hit Combo: When the popup says "Goblu performs a combo", it will either be this or the 4 hit one. The attack is a bit of a bait as it will hit much later than you think it should and it will likely throw you off. The 4 hit version only seems to be towards the tail end of the fight, after Goblu has summoned more flowers.

Grow Flowers: Goblu will grow 4 flowers. Shoot the orbs with free aim. They can be shot, even though your reticle may not go red. If you don't shoot the flowers, he will absorb them and regain shields. Later on in the fight, he will grow too many flowers for you to kill. It's up to you what you do then. You can either full focus the boss or use some AP on free aim shots to destroy some of the flowers.
Crush: This only appears to happen towards the end of the fight but a message will appear that says "Goblu is about to crush...". This is a big, one hit attack with a long wind-up.

This fight mostly just challenges you on what you've learnt so far, combining shields, jump counters and everything else. The fight will start with Goblu jumping at you. Don't try and counter with jumps of your own, just dodge/parry. If you parry all 3 bounces, the expedition will counter and break both his shields. For this boss and others with shields onwards, Maelle's "Breaking Rules" ability is a godsend as it removes ALL shields an enemy has in one turn and rewards you with AP per shield destroyed.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: You will receive a Shape of Health from defeating Goblu, something we can use soon to upgrade the potency of health tints. Leave this area and you will automatically be in the camp, following a cutscene. This completes Flying Waters and unlocks:

steps.name: Flying Waters
steps.description: Find your way through Flying Waters.

steps.text: When back in control, you will find yourself in front of the Curator. He will always be here at camp and offers a range of services. Speak to him to see that he can upgrade weapons or expedition resources. Go to weapons first. There will be a few popups telling you how this works. If you've played any souls-like games before, it will be very familiar. Attribute points scale with certain weapons and weapons themselves can be upgraded up to certain levels with the use of various items. I'm not going to tell you what to upgrade or not, just be aware that you can buy upgrade materials from most merchants and even past this, most of them can be farmed. Upgrade any weapon now to unlock:
steps.heading: Camp

steps.text: Now back go out and this time choose to upgrade expedition resources. The Upgrade Lumina section will use your Colours of Lumina to give a character of your choice an extra Lumina point. This, in turn, allows you to equip more pictos to them. Colours of Lumina are plentiful in the game. There are plenty to pick up in the open world, most merchants sell a number of them and if all else fails, you can farm them. So again, spend at your leisure. Give any character a Lumina point now to unlock:

Finally, at the bottom is the Upgrade Tints section. You should already be able to upgrade the healing and revive tints. Unlike the shard items which are applied automatically and increase the number of tints you can carry, the Shape items must be used here. This will increase the potency of the tints, healing your characters for more health and reviving them with more health. Upgrade both tints now. When done with the curator, leave this cave to be back at the campfire. The characters don't have much to say at this point so interact with the fire. Choose to write in the journal if you wish and then choose to check up on the others. This starts a cutscene and unlocks:

steps.name: Curious
steps.description: Witness an optional scene at camp.

steps.text: Rest at the fire to return to the world map. Open the map with and you will see our next destination is right ahead. Go to it and enter the Ancient Sanctuary.

Rest at the flag ahead and just past this you will see a strange little ball like creature. These are Petanks and I personally find them extremely irritating. They are mostly optional so it's up to you if you want to bother with them. Essentially you need to "herd" them onto a certain space on the floor which is indicated with their colour.
steps.heading: Ancient Sanctuary

steps.text: You can then fight the Petank and defeat it for rewards. They will escape if not defeated quick enough. The one here doesn't drop anything special - just Chroma, Colour of Lumina, etc. so I chose to leave it. If you do choose to fight it, Maelle's "Breaking Rules" is again, a godsend as it removes all shields in one turn. This stops you using all your AP removing them.

Whatever you decide, to the left of the Petank's spot you can loot the "Energising Jump" pictos. Now go back to the main path and follow the river first, not the ramp to the right. You emerge in an open area with a chasm below. Turn right and you will see some handholds on the wall. Use this to climb down and loot the "Burning Mark" pictos. Climb back up and now take the ramp to the right. Follow this path all the way around. You can speak to the NPC here if you wish. Continue following the path for a cutscene, after which you will end up in a battle.
Club Attack: The popup will say that it is "swinging its dead partner". The windup for this attack is hilariously long and it will hit much, much later than you think it will.
steps.heading: Robust Sakapatate - Attacks

steps.text: Shield Slam: The enemy swipes its shield, hitting ALL party members. Try not to dodge too early, it has a bit of a windup again.
4-Hit Combo: The enemy will attack with two fast punches first then a jump counter and then another punch. There are no delays with this combo.

Shield Counter: It will "raise its shield" and will counterattack on its next turn. This seems faster to me than the shield slam above. As soon as you see it with the shield to its side, you should be dodging. I haven't found a way to stop this attack from happening, regardless of whether you attack the boss or not, it seems to counter.
Body Slam: On defeat, the enemy will stagger left to right and then slam into the party. Wait until it's close as its very easy to dodge too early here. Around the 3rd/4th step is about right.

The enemy will get the first move so don't put down that controller for the cutscene! You can use free aim to hit the glowing white spot in its shoulder. If you see a popup at the top of the screen saying that "it is raising its shield", be prepared to try and dodge its attack on the next turn or it will break and stun the whole team, dealing high damage. This is the last time that I'll recommend Maelle's "Breaking Rules" ability but it is just invaluable as many enemies have shields in this game and removing them all in one turn is so powerful. Other than the moves doing high damage, it is a standard enemy and doesn't have boss levels of health. It is weak to fire so spamming Lune's "Immolation" and Maelle's "Spark" will help. On death, it will perform the body slam attack above.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: You won't be thrilled to know that the above enemy is a standard enemy in this area, along with a couple of other variants. As with everything else in this game though, once it clicks, it clicks. After the cutscene, there is a flag ahead you can rest at. Proceed forward into another open area where the path splits. Go right first, under the fallen tree and then take a right again. There is a hole here that you can crouch under. Take a right again and then go to the right side of the pillar head for a dead-end and 965x Chroma.

Now take the left side of the pillar. Run up the ramp to the left and at the back of this area, on the left wall, are some handholds. The pacing enemy here drops a weapon for Lune. Kill or skip the enemy then climb the handholds. Follow the path at the start all the way to the end to obtain the "Energising Start" pictos. Drop back down from this area and look to your left. There is a tunnel marked by a lantern. Go into here and at the split in the path take a left. Defeat the enemy and then loot the "Attack Lifesteal" pictos. Take the other path and go up the rope. Loot the Colour of Lumina at the end. Drop down here to be back at the start of this area. Rest at the flag to your left and then fast travel to "Sanctuary Maze."

Return to where we crawled through the gap (right at the split, under the tree and then right). This time go left after crawling through. Loot a Revive Tint Shard from the wooden hut in the middle here. There is a Mime you can fight around the other side of the hut if you wish. As usual, it just gives mostly cosmetics - in this case an outfit and haircut for Lune.

Once ready, face back the way you came from. The left path takes us back to the crawlspace, so let's go right. Loot the Colour of Lumina and then drop down. Turn left and smash the boxes at the end of this dead end for 483x Chroma. Now go the other way to a fork. The left path will take you back to the flag if you wish to rest. Go right to the area with the blue crystal figures. Defeat the enemy and then take the left path lit with torches. There will be some dialogue. Keep following the path to another split. Take the left path and go the only possible way until you see a purple item. Loot it for a Healing Tint Shard.

Take the path to the right of the item to reach another open area. Defeat the enemy and then take the left path. You will see [Journal #3/49 - Expedition 63] ahead. There is a paint cage nearby but we can destroy all of the locks from here. From the journal, facing the middle structure in the area, turn left and look up for Lock #1.
Now go to the right side of the structure and destroy the crates in the image below for Lock #2.
For the final lock, look left from the crates and you can see Lock #3 partially hidden behind some trees.

With the locks destroyed, leave this area to the open area where you fought the enemy and take the next path left, between the two statues and through the trees. Carefully walk along the tree branch and take the rope down. Climb onto the platform to your left that a statue is holding up and then jump from platform to platform, following the path until you reach the item where the paint cage was. Loot the Chroma Elixir Shard and then drop back down. Once again, head to the open area where you fought the enemy and this time head straight on, following the path lit by blue lanterns, until you reach the next flag.
After resting, carry onward to reach another large open area and a cutscene that ends with another boss battle.

Club Attack: Similar to what you've seen already. The popup will say that "it attacks with its dead partner". This is just a simple 3-hit combo. No delays, just two quick hits followed by a jump counter.
steps.heading: Ultimate Sakapatate - Attacks

steps.text: Slam: Again, similar to the standard enemies you've fought already. This is just a 1 hit slam with the club. I chose to dodge this due to the windup throwing me off.

Shield Slam Cannons: After the boss "takes the fight seriously", it will raise its shield and attack whoever next hits it. This is immediately followed by 3 bursts of cannon fire which will hit all party members and cause them to burn.
Electric Thingies: When the popup says that the boss "reaches its full potential", it will cast 3 electric bolts. This is the exact same as the standard enemies you've fought.

This guy isn't so bad, I actually found the standard enemies more annoying in this area and I was just glad to be done with these guys in general. Fire still works wonders here. Keep an eye out for when the popup says that the boss is "taking the fight seriously" as this will be followed by the Shield Slam Cannons move above. When you break him, the shoulder weak-spot will be exposed. Destroy this quickly as it will destroy his shield arm. This stops him from shield slamming or firing cannons again, making the rest of the fight trivial as he can only do the club attack or electric thingies from now on. Unlike the other enemies in this area, he doesn't crash into the party on death.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Defeating the boss will give you a cutscene as well as unlock the below achievement for completing this area:

steps.name: Ancient Sanctuary
steps.description: Find your way through Ancient Sanctuary.

steps.text: We're not quite done here yet though as there are goodies to collect nearby. When back in control after the cutscene, run up the slight incline to the right and on your left is an Energy Tint Shard. Crawl through the gap to the right of this and loot the "Stun Boost" pictos at the end. Now go back to the boss area and leave via the path to the right, taking you back to the world map.

This is a very brief visit to the world map but for the sake of consistency I'm writing it as its own section. You will already see the swirling portal ahead that leads to our next area, the Gestral Village. To the right of this is a Colour of Lumina. You can press if you wish to go to the camp and upgrade weapons or add Lumina points. Other than that, that's it! Go into the Gestral Village portal now.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: There is a LOT of optional stuff here. I'll do the story and collectible stuff first and then list some optional bits afterwards for those that want them. Rest at the flag ahead and sort out the usual stuff before heading into the village proper. Enter the building straight ahead marked as "Chief House" and speak to the NPC at the back of the room. When given the option, choose to look around first as it's easier to give directions from here rather than from the arena.
steps.heading: Gestral Village

steps.text: Leave the chief's building and turn around so you are facing it. To the left you will see a sign marked for "Arena". Follow this to reach another arena sign pointing to the right. Follow it again to a third sign. Go to the LEFT of this one, down the narrow path and loot [Journal #4/49 - Expedition 52]. Now go to the right of the sign and the arena will be on your right, along with a flag. Rest if you want and then speak to the yellow Gestral to the right of the arena entrance, to register.

You can only choose one character for the fights. Make sure to choose Maelle for the final fight against "The Stranger" as you get a weapon specific to the character you pick. Maelle's weapon will likely see you all the way through to endgame as long as you keep on top of upgrading it. I won't do any tactics for the arena as the fights are all very easy. Don't be afraid to heal if you need to but you should really have no issue here. There will be a cutscene after winning the final battle, after which you will be asked if you want to play Sciel's tutorial. I'd recommend doing so because like all characters in this game, she has a unique mechanic.

Following the tutorial, speak to Golgra again to receive the password for the next area. It's now up to you what to do. I'd recommend at least following the optional route just to get the Shape of Energy from the manor. With regards to party members, you now have 4 but only 3 can play at a time. You can add/remove party members at any time outside of combat by pressing when on the character menu. Make sure you assign skills, attribute points and pictos to Sciel as well!

First things first, you can challenge Golgra here with any character to a duel. Winning will award them with a weapon. Personally, I didn't bother with this as Maelle's is the best one and you already have that now. Leave the chief's building and this time turn left. You will see a path to the left, and an arch to the right. Take the path left and take the right path at the fork. You will be in an open area with two Gestrals sat down at a table in front of you. Look to the right of them to see a sign that says "Turn Back". Go through the arch next to this and enter the door at the end to find yourself in the Manor.
steps.heading: Optional

steps.text: There are three items in this kitchen that you need to interact with, similar to the ornaments from earlier. The first is the middle saucepan on the right wall. The second is the statue bust to the right of the saucepans. The third is a candlestick on the table at the left side of the room, near the door in the back left. Face the candlestick and turn left, then go to the far wall. Destroy the barrels and drop through the now open hole in the floor. Go through the hole in the wall, past the stairs and in the back left corner you can destroy some crates for the Shape of Energy. You can also destroy some more boxes at the wall opposite this to crawl through a gap and obtain a new hairstyle for Maelle on the right.

When done, go up the stairs in the room where you looted the Shape of Energy and exit the door at the top to be back in the kitchen. Go through the other door here to be back at the flag. Leave the manor. Now we're going to go grab a few pictos from various merchants in the village.

Make your way back to the Chief's building and look to the left when facing it to see a sign for "Bazar". Speak to the first Gestral on the left, behind the counter for some dialogue and eventually the store. Fighting this merchant will unlock a purchasable weapon for Gustave. It's up to you what you buy from any of these merchants. I tried to get as many pictos as I could for variety but didn't buy the weapon for instance. You can always come back to any of these vendors later anyway.

Talk to this merchant again if you obtained the "Weird Pictos" in the prologue and he will change it into the "Augmented Aim" pictos. Turn right from this merchant and follow the path through the bazar. You will soon see a giant Gestral with green hair. Opposite him, to your immediate left is a wooden ramp. Follow it up in a spiral and destroy the boxes at the top. Keep following the path and destroying boxes. At the very end, you will see a white item. Loot it for 610x Chroma. Go back the way you came and at the bottom of the ramp take a left and go down the path here. Cycle through the dialogue to fight another battle.

This unlocks another merchant who sells the usual items, the "Healing Mark" pictos and a weapon for Maelle. There is just one more pictos I want to grab now. Head back to the arena area and when facing the arena building, turn left. Move forward, past the flag on your right and go left through the opening next to the arena sign on the left. Follow the path in the only direction you can until reach a short Gestral with a path behind him adorned with purple torches. Head to the building back here and interact with the door.

Select "Yes" when given the option and then, "I don't care". You will receive the "Roulette" pictos. This pictos is extremely powerful as it makes it so any attack can be either double or half damage. Some characters, like Maelle in virtuoso stance will do extreme damage if the double effect procs. I personally did not equip this pictos until the endgame but it's definitely worth picking up.
We're now done with pictos gathering in the Gestral Village. There is still more stuff to explore and Gestrals to talk to so feel free to keep exploring if you wish.
Once done with the optional stuff or if you choose to continue without, leave the village the way you came in. You will unlock the below achievement for completing this area:

steps.name: Gestral Village
steps.description: Find your way through the Gestral Village.

steps.text: You will find yourself put back into the camp on leaving the village. Make sure to speak to the curator in the cave and upgrade your tints/weapons. Other than this, there isn't much to do. You can speak to the characters but we don't have relationship levels yet so there isn't much dialogue. Interact with the campfire and write in the journal, then check up on the others for a scene. All that's left then is to go to sleep for another cutscene.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Back on the world map, we will again just proceed to the next objective. As usual, you are free to explore as much or as little as you wish. To your left, the gate has been opened so you can access the rest of the continent without having to run back through the Sanctuary Maze. Head through there now and you'll see what looks like a face in the distance. Head here to see a small Gestral standing out front. Speak to it and it will return to your camp. This is [Lost Gestral #1/9]. You can speak to an NPC at camp who will give you rewards for each one you find. Proceed into the spiral portal behind where the Gestral was to enter Esquie's Nest.

This is quite a short area thankfully after the Sanctuary Maze and as usual, there are some goodies to get. Head forward along the only path to see a flag on the left. Rest if you wish and then speak to the Gestral for a cutscene. When back in control, turn right and you should see a crawlspace to the right of the Gestral. Go through it for a Colour of Lumina. You can also loot 653x Chroma at the end of the path behind the Gestral.
steps.heading: Esquie's Nest

steps.text: Now head up the ramp to arrive in a large, colourful room. If you look down to your right, you will see a Mime. This one drops an outfit and haircut for Sciel. If you look down to your left, there is a Petank you can herd into its spot and then kill. These generally just drop standard upgrade materials, so I never bothered with them. Both sides can climb back up to the bridge via handholds on the bridge itself.

Once you've defeated one, both or neither, head to the far end of the bridge and through the tunnel beyond to reach another open area adorned with braziers. Climb the stairs to the first landing and follow the path along the left side to find an item. Loot it for 1,305x Chroma. Now go up the stairs again for a cutscene. When back in control, head the way you are now facing and follow the path until you reach a grapple point. Turn right on landing and follow this path to the end for a Colour of Lumina. Now go the other way for a flag. Rest up and then proceed forward for a cutscene, after which you will find yourself in a boss battle.

This boss only has one move, the ice attack. It will one-shot your characters, so watch the pulse from the boss and get ready to parry just after the second one. Otherwise, just damage the boss down. You will get another cutscene afterwards. When back in control, go to the rope ahead. Follow the path to the right and loot another 1,305x Chroma to your left. Continue following the path, climbing up at the end. You can jump to the ledge ahead for another Colour of Lumina if you wish. Either way, return to Esquie at the top of the stairs for a cutscene. You will unlock the two achievements below for finishing this area and unlocking Esquie:

steps.name: Esquie's Nest
steps.description: Find your way through Esquie's Nest.

steps.text: Back in control, head to the fallen pillar in front of you and grapple from it to a new ledge. Follow the path until it leads down and you can make a right to a small camp area. Amongst the tents here is [Journal #5/49 - Expedition 66]. Continue along the path and grapple again. Loot the item at the end for the "Energising Start III" pictos and then drop down. You are now back at the entrance to this area. The next main area we will visit is the last of Act I so now we will begin with the Act I clean-up followed by finishing off the story here. Leave this area back to the world map.

sections.title: 5. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Act I - Part 2

steps.text: First things first, Esquie. You will gain more abilities for Esquie throughout the story that give you access to more of the map. At the moment, all he can do is smash through rubble. Riding him is faster than walking/sprinting though which is one reason I left the collectible stuff until now. As with everything else in this game, if there is an area or activity you really don't want to do right now, you can always come back later. Just remember that your counters will be different to mine.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: First up, we will go to the "Yellow Harvest" side-area. Where some side-areas are literally just one room with the collectible in the middle, this one is more akin to an optional dungeon. Summon Esquie with and hold to sprint. Make your way to the location below.

On entering, there is a flag straight ahead. After resting, look to the right to find a wall with handholds. Climb up and drop down at the top. Follow the linear path past a destroyed shed and some tents. Once on the other side of a cave, you will find yourself in an open area with enemies. Defeat the enemy in front of you and then make your way over to the two in the back right and defeat them. Hop up the white ledge and follow the path to the right of the grapple to find another flag.
steps.heading: Yellow Harvest

steps.text: Look to the right of the flag to see another large area with a statue in the middle. Make your way to the right first and you will see a ramp going up. Take this path all the way and climb up twice at the end. Straight ahead of you is [Journal #6/49 - Expedition 38]. Continue straight on past the journal and look up at the end to find a grapple point.

Up here is a merchant you can battle for the "Teamwork" pictos. As the description is hidden unless you unlock it, this pictos increases damage by 10% whilst all characters are alive. It's up to you whether you go for it. Buy what you want from the merchant and then drop down to the area below, noting that you don't take fall damage in this game. Return back to the open area with the statue and again go right, this time ignoring the ramp and going past it to the left. Directly in front of you, near the enemy patrolling ahead, is [Journal #7/49 - Expedition 44]. Look to the right of the journal to see a passage in the wall. There is an optional Mime through here. This one drops a hairstyle for Maelle.

Continue following the main path from the journal and you'll see another ramp on your left. Head up this and grapple at the top to reach the roof of the building. Follow another ramp upwards and across another few grapple points, handholds and steps, eventually reaching a flag at a split in the path. Take the left path from the flag to find [Journal #8/49 - Expedition 59]. Take the right path from the flag now for a cutscene and a boss fight.
Earth Ground Pound: Similar to Eveque's attack but Earth. Parry just before the traveling Earth hits you.
steps.heading: Glaise - Attacks

steps.text: Jump Slam: When the popup says "Glaise Attacks", he will jump into the air and slam the ground, hitting all three characters. There is a delay on this and you can easily try to parry too early. Give him a second or two after he jumps and then hit it.
Earthquakes: After the popup says "Glaise prepares for a powerful blow", he will use this on his next turn. This is 3 hit combo with a short delay between each attack. It hits the whole party.

The boss will get the first turn, try and counter what you can for some easy shield removal. This boss seemed to get stuck in a cycle for me where all it would cast was the jump slam over and over. As this is relatively easy to counter once you get the feel for it, I just constantly parried him and he was dead in a couple of turns. If this attack connects it will either kill your team or drop people low so feel free to dodge for the easier timing if you want to play it safe. Nothing special about this boss to be honest though, it shouldn't give you much trouble.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Back in control after the boss fight, turn around to face the entrance. There is another path to the left that leads to a Chromatic boss fight. The enemy is one you won't have seen yet and they will one-shot your characters. It's entirely doable if you learn their moves and counter accordingly. I left it at this point as it only drops a weapon for Lune and some upgrade materials but if you want to have a go there is no reason not to.
Whether you kill it or not, return to this area and look at the pirate ship. Turn to your right and go under the stone arch. Follow this path to exit the area and return to the Continent.

Look to your right and interact with the object to form a bridge leading back to the rest of the map. Turn around and go straight ahead to another swirling portal for the "Lost Woods". There is nothing in this area apart from [Record #3/34 - Aline's Glasshouse]. Loot it and exit back to the Continent. Cross over the bridge we made and at the other side look to your left to see some destroyed buildings. In between them is [Journal #9/49 - Expedition 62]. Head to the location in the image below to reach the Gestral Beach side area.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: There are a few Gestral Beaches throughout the game, each containing a mini-game of sorts such as obstacle courses, parkour and racing. Fair warning, they can be annoying. However, they are needed for an achievement so we're going to have to do them. Speak to the Gestral ahead for some context and then move behind him. There is a log in the water. This is the start of the course. It is linear so you can't really get lost but the parkour can be iffy as this isn't a game designed around it and if you fall off you have to restart. I'll outline below how I did it but your mileage may vary. Some people suggest playing as Lune here because she glides but I actually found this harder so stuck with Maelle as she has the smaller character model.
steps.heading: Gestral Beach

steps.text: The most annoying part of this course to me was actually the first jump as you will roll on landing due to jumping from height. This will most likely be the cause of a lot of restarts at first. The rest of the log section is fine, just don't rush it. Sprint and jump over the gaps but without a roll you'll be fine. The spinning platforms are more disorienting than difficult as I found even if you hit the spokes when jumping over, you'll still land on the platform most of the time.

After this it's just a running jump from one flat platform to the next and then another to the moving platform when its close. Take one more running jump from the moving platform at the end of its route, being careful to align yourself with the middle of the platform below so you don't roll off. Speak to the Gestral for your "rewards" and then return to the entrance by jumping into the water. This is [Gestral Game #1/5]. Leave the area and return to the Continent. Directly opposite where we come out is the Hidden Gestral Arena. This side area is entirely optional and consists of different 1v1 fights that award pictos. I will outline it below, along with what each pictos does so you can decide if it's worth the time or not.

There is a flag straight ahead here that you can use to tinker with things between battles. For reference, I was level 19 when I did this and used Maelle for all my fights as she was already doing 9,999 openers for me at this point thanks to the Medalum weapon we received from the Gestral Village. Proceed the only way you can and speak to the Gestral to choose your fighter and opponent. Below is each enemy and what pictos they give for defeating them. There is nothing special about any of these enemies and they all have basic moves that are easy to counter. The final fight against Julien could catch you off guard because of the 3 hit combo he does but it shouldn't take you long to smash through these encounters.
steps.heading: Hidden Gestral Arena

steps.text: Matthieu the Colossus: "Last Stand Critical" - 100% critical chance while fighting alone.
Bertrand Big Hands: "Accelerating Last Stand" - Gain Rush if fighting alone
Dominique Giant Feet: "Protecting Last Stand" - Gain Shell if fighting alone
Julien Tiny Head: "Solo Fighter" and "Empowering Last Stand" - 50% more damage when fighting alone + Gain powerful if fighting alone.
Head to the location on the image below to find a merchant.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Buy [Record #4/34 - Goblu] from him as well as anything else you fancy. Facing the merchant straight on, turn around and you will see a group of enemies ahead to the right. Run past or defeat these and on the right is an entrance to the Small Bourgeon side-area. Enter here.

Rest at the flag if needed then move forward into a large room. On the left side is a giant, dormant enemy like the one we fought earlier. Take the path to the left of it and loot [Journal #10/49 - Expedition 53]. Now go back to the giant enemy and speak to the small white version of it underneath. Cycle through its dialogue and then, provided you killed the bourgeon enemy back in Flying Waters, you will be able to give it the Bourgeon skin when speaking to it again.
steps.heading: The Small Bourgeon

steps.text: Leave this area back to the Continent and then re-enter it again to see the Nevron has now grown. Speak to it, and then turn around after the dialogue to see a purple item has appeared. Loot the Colour of Lumina. Speak to the Nevron again and cycle through the dialogue, making sure NOT to select the option to attack, then leave. This completes [Nevron Quest #3/10]. We're done here so again, return to the Continent.

Back on the Continent, turn right and activate the switch ahead, forming another bridge. Move to the blue crystals ahead and re-enter Spring Meadows. We're going to go and get the achievement for killing a boss with no damage now that we are sufficiently levelled.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Move ahead and take the rope on the left down back to where we fought the Eveque boss. Go to the flag and then fast travel to "Grand Meadow". We're going back to the Chromatic boss we skipped earlier. Take the path right from the flag and under the fallen stone pillar like last time. At the top of the hill, take a right before the rope and you will see the green tinted enemy ahead. This is the Chromatic Lancelier. Make sure to get a first strike on it and then shoot its weak spot on your first turn. This should remove at least 1/4 of health. I then defeated it with Maelle given she starts in Virutose stance, provided Medalum is equipped. At the very most, the enemy might get one move off but I find this doubtful if you are anything around level 15+. Defeating the enemy without taking damage will unlock:
steps.heading: Spring Meadows

steps.name: Professional
steps.description: Defeat a boss without taking any damage.

steps.text: Now return to the flag, fast travel to the "Indigo Tree" and then make your way back out to the Continent.

We're almost done with our collectible gathering now. Back on the world map, cross the bridge directly ahead and turn right. There is an area with red trees ahead and some breakable rocks you can now smash through with Esquie. Loot the Colour of Lumina on the right and then enter the "Ancient Gestral City" side-area. There is nothing to do here apart from loot [Record #5/34 - Lights of the Past] and then leave.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Make your way to the location in the image below, you will need to cross back over the bridge we took from the Small Bourgeon first.

Enter the "Twilight Quarry" side-area and loot [Record #6/34 - Un 33 Decembre A Lumiére]. Leave the area. Smash back through the rocks and take a right, passing Esquie's nest on your right. There is another merchant here that sells some cosmetics should you want them. Smash more rocks to the right. The ramp ahead leads to the next main story area. First though, go to the right of it and you will see another Bourgeon enemy. This will also drop a Bourgeon skin if you didn't kill the one in Flying Waters. We need to kill this one either way as there is a Lost Gestral hiding behind it.

The fight itself is the same as the one in Flying Waters, except it is accompanied by two normal enemies at the start. Kill those first and then focus on the big guy. I won't go through the moves again but you can use the information on the previous page if needed. Just be extra careful of when the popup says that the enemy is about to do a "Crushing Combo" as this is a whopping 6 hit attack. When the boss is defeated, move forward and take a right to see [Lost Gestral #2/9]. You can also take the left path to the cliff edge and loot the "Healing Parry" pictos.

With this final task done, we can now return to the ramp we passed and go up it. When you try and enter the area, Maelle will say she is tired. Press to go to the camp, which will start a cutscene. After the cutscene, take the path between the two lanterns ahead to find a Gestral. Speak to him a couple of times and he will reward you for returning the lost gestrals to him.
