As you have rescued two so far, you will get two haircuts. Spend some time upgrading weapons and adding Lumina points as necessary. Interact with the campfire, write in the journal and then rest for another cutscene. You can now head into the Stone Wave Cliffs.

Follow the linear path until you trigger a cutscene. When back in control, keep heading forward, the only way you can, until you see a flag ahead. Just to the left is 790x Chroma. Rest if needed and then continue. Follow the right wall in this area until you reach a rope. Take it up and loot [Journal #11/49 - Expedition 78]. Turn left from the journal and you'll see a paint cage ahead. For the first lock, walk around the back of the cage itself and you should be able to see this on the wall behind. You might need to be in front of the cage, aiming past it in order to hit it.
steps.heading: Stone Wave Cliffs

steps.text: Climb the rope to the right of the cage and straight in front of you, slightly above, is the second lock.
Now walk straight until you reach the wall ahead. Turn around and look up to your left for the final lock.

Loot the Delaram weapon for Gustave. Return to the previous area and defeat the enemy here. Looking at the path onward through the wreckage, turn left and follow the wall round to some more wreckage. Inside is the "Breaking Counter" pictos. Return to the wreckage and go through it, grappling across the gap ahead. There is a Colour of Lumina right next to you as you land. In this new open area, take the left path around the edge of the area. Defeat the enemy ahead and then loot [Journal #12/49 - Expedition 56] from behind it. Cross the nearby bridge and turn left. Near the cliff edge to the left, in a little hut, is a Colour of Lumina.

Climb the platforms opposite this, and loot the "First Strike" pictos after you've defeated the enemies. Drop back down and grapple across the gap to the right. There is 790x Chroma on the right to loot here. Take the left path to the next flag. After resting, take the path to the left of the flag. Defeat the enemies here and then loot the Healing Tint Shard. Go back past the flag and at the bottom of the slope is an Energy Tint Shard also! Turn around from the shard and follow the path over the bridge to the left. Take the left path at the split and stick to the left. On the cliff edge ahead is [Journal #13/49 - Expedition 50].

Turn around from the journal and climb the broken stairs. Grapple over to loot 3,160x Chroma. Grapple again and loot another 1,580x Chroma behind you as you land. Climb the handholds at the end of this path and then head left. You will see some lanterns ahead. Take the long path underneath these, grappling across a large gap. Look to the right of the rope, around the corner, to loot 790x Chroma. Take the rope up and rest at the flag at the top.

Follow the path down past the flag and through the gap in the fence on the right to loot 790x Chroma. Head around to the back of the hut and follow the path here, crawling through a hole in the rock to eventually reach a merchant. There is a prompt at the edge of the path here that opens a shortcut to the area below. Fighting the merchant unlocks a weapon for Sciel in the merchant's stock. On your way back to the hut, stick to the left side and you will see a purple item. Loot it for a Polished Chroma Catalyst.

Back in the area with the hut, head back to the original slope we came down from the flag and go straight across it, dropping off the other side. There is another Polished Chroma Catalyst here. Now take the path ahead, sticking to the left and you will see a paint cage at the top of a slope. Go right up to the cage and turn around. You will see the first lock ahead, attached to the side of some wooden pallets.
Turn left 90 degrees from this, and directly across from you, is the second lock.
Finally, turn 180 degrees and look up and to the left. The final lock is here.

Loot the weapon for Maelle from the cage. If you look out across the area, you will see some more lanterns ahead. This is the way we need to go. Make your way over there and follow the path up the hill and over some handholds. You will see a white Nevron here. This is another quest. Speak to him and cycle through his dialogue before taking the tunnel to the right of the Nevron and resting at the flag.

Head right from the flag, and grapple across the gap. We have three quest items to collect here for the quest Nevron, so will do this first. Go down the rope ahead. In one direction you should see a giant enemy and towards the left wall, a blue crystal. This is Crystal #1 needed for the quest.

Run up to it hit, press to break it, and loot. From the crystal, turn around and head to the other side of the room, near the water. Follow the water along, past the submerged building and follow the wall right. There will be two paths, a slope going upwards and a path to the right of it.

To the left of the slope is a Colour of Lumina. Take the right path, past the slope and loot a second Colour of Lumina straight ahead. Now turn around and take the left path. You will see Crystal #2 just ahead.

Approach it to reveal an enemy. Defeat the enemy to obtain the crystal. Remember the rope ahead as we will come back to it after dealing with the Nevron quest. After defeating the enemy, return to the slope and stick to the left side. You will see Crystal #3 around the corner.

Loot it and return to the quest Nevron. Talk to it, cycle through the dialogue, again making sure NOT to attack, and then loot the "Auto Shell" pictos. Speak to the Nevron one more time to make sure, completing [Nevron Quest #4/10].

Now you can either continue with the story path or take the rope I told you to remember about for an optional boss. The boss drops the "Perilous Parry" pictos which gives you +1AP for a successful parry BUT your damage received is doubled. You can also enter the Manor behind the boss but there is only an outfit item here. To continue with the story path, from re-entering the area via the rope from above, stay to the left until you find a path adorned with red flowers and lanterns. Take this path upwards to the top, where it splits. The right path leads to a short platforming segment where you can loot the "Breaking Shots" pictos. Grab it or not, then take the left path.

Grapple across, loot the Colour of Lumina to the right of the rope and then take it up. The next flag is at the top. Rest as necessary and then turn around from the flag to see a grapple ahead. Take this one, followed by another and you will reach another flag in a destroyed building. Go through the door to the left of the flag and down the stairs. Follow the left wall here, past the area with the enemy and around the corner. Keep following the left wall, into another ruined building. Go upstairs all the way and when you are back outside, turn around and take the handholds to the left of the gap in the wall you came out of. At the bottom here is a Revive Tint Shard.

Climb back up, defeat the enemy and then loot the Recoat from the back right of the roof. Look left to spot another grapple in the distance. Take it and loot the "Enfeebling Mark" pictos. Grapple back across and return downstairs, back through the destroyed building. Now take the grapple we ignored earlier. Follow the path the only way you can and ahead to the right, you will see a purple item. Climb the ledge here to loot a Colour of Lumina. Return to the path, climb up and cross over the rubble bridge. You will see a blue item ahead, behind an enemy. This is the "Healing Tint Energy" pictos. Take the rope ahead and go through two doorways. Look behind you after the second, and climb some more handholds to the right of the doorframe. Jump the small gap at the top and loot a weapon for Lune.

That's everything collected here. Leave this building via the stairs, not the rope and grapple back across to the flag. Rest up, check pictos and assign points because the boss is ahead. When ready, go into the cave for a cutscene.
Jump Attack: This is quite delayed so you may get baited into dodging early at first. If it hits, it will put "Defenceless" on your character. This increases damage taken by 25%.
steps.heading: The Lampmaster - Attacks - Phase 1

steps.text: Lamp Shot: There will be a popup saying that the Lampmaster is "turning all the lamps off in the cave". This is followed by the boss shooting four white orbs at the party. You should parry just before they hit, it's faster than you think though. Essentially as soon as you see the shot, you should be ready to parry.

Lamp Power: When the popup says the Lampmaster "uses the power of its lamps to attack", there will be one hit to dodge/parry. The damage of this attack is amplified by how many lamps are still active. There is a sound cue "ping" that indicates when to parry this.

Disruption: When the popup says the Lampmaster "tries to disrupt the aim" of a party member, it is about to do a 3 hit combo. If the boss hits the party member, they will be disrupted and free aim will be harder to control.

Dark Explosion: The boss does a single attack on a party member. It can be a little hard to see because of the already dark cave. He does a little jump and then you want to parry just after this. If the attack hits your character, they will be afflicted by "Exhausted", which stops AP gain.
Light Ball: The popup will say that the Lampmaster is going to "throw a ball of light" at the party. This is a simple jump counter.
steps.heading: Attacks - Phase 2

steps.text: Lamp Trial: Four lamps will flash green in a certain order. If you hit the lamps in the order they lit up whilst in free aim, you will cancel out the powerful attack below.

Powerful Attack: The boss will only cast this if you fail the lamp trial, either by hitting the lamps in the wrong order or by not hitting them in time. The popup will say that the Lampmaster is going to attack with a "giant sword of light". Thankfully, this attack is actually easy to parry. It's slow and very predictable but if you do miss it, will do a tonne of party damage and may outright kill characters on higher difficulties.

Flying Combo: This is a 4 hit combo with long wind-up times. I found this the most annoying of phase 2 but thankfully only had to deal with it once. It will afflict a character with disruption if the majority of the combo connects.

The first thing to note with this boss is that shooting the lamps in free aim, DOES do damage to him as well as reduces the damage of certain abilities. Whilst you shouldn't burn all your AP destroying them, tactically think on each characters turn if you can destroy any. Note that the lamps you need to destroy are the square ones floating near him, NOT the ones he is carrying and they only take one hit to destroy. Attempting to shoot the carried ones will just deal damage to the boss.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: When you deplete the boss's health, a brief cutscene will start, after which you will find yourself in phase 2. If you die in phase 2, you will restart from phase 1 so you want to try and save as many healing and revive tints as you can for phase 2. Personally, I found phase 2 easier as the lamp trial is always easy to complete provided you're paying attention and the light ball attack is an easy jump counter. Even the "powerful attack" that only happens when failing the lamp trial is an easy counter. If you reach phase 2 in good health, with healing items then you'll likely have no issue. Phase 1 is definitely the more annoying as it has more abilities that are hard to counter in part due to the dark cave. Persevere, learn the patterns, dodge over parry if you have to and you will soon be victorious.
After the boss fight, you will find yourself in a series of cutscenes, at the end of which you will be in camp. You will also unlock the below achievement for finishing this area:

steps.name: Stone Wave Cliffs
steps.description: Find your way through Stone Wave Cliffs.

steps.text: This marks the end of Act I. Onwards to Act II!

sections.title: 6. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Act II - Part 1

steps.text: Camp
steps.heading: Act II - Part I

steps.text: Once back in control at camp, we have a few things to do. First of all, let's do the bits we know. Speak to the curator and assign any more Lumina points you wish, as well as upgrade weapons and tints. If you rest at the flag here, you can assign attribute points and skills to Verso, though you may want to wait until you've done a battle or two and have a feel for him first. Relationship levels with each character will now become a thing, although in this camp interaction you can only gain a level with Esquie.

There is an achievement tied to getting to max relationship rank with each character. You can't really "miss" a level as you can speak with a character multiple times in one camp session and catch up if you're behind. The dialogue choices in these relationship interactions don't matter apart from one specific one with Maelle and this will be heavily emphasised. You can speak with the other characters now if you wish but make sure you speak to Esquie and choose to spend time with him. After the dialogue, you will be Relationship Level 1. When ready, interact with the fire and go to sleep for another cutscene, after which you will be back on the Continent.

Esquie now has the swim ability so there is a lot of the map you can explore. As usual, if you want to go and look for yourself, there is no reason not to. We will do one quick backtrack though before carrying on with the story. Turn around when back in control, summon Esquie and swim to the merchant across from you. Behind him is a swirling portal. Enter it to return to the "Stone Wave Cliffs".
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Follow the linear path here back into the cave where you fought the Lampmaster. In the middle of the room, you can loot [Record #7/34 - Gustave]. On your way back out, grab the "Defensive Mode" pictos from the right side if you missed it. Back on the Continent, get back into the water and swim North, towards your objective. You will see lots of wrecked ships and a big gate ahead, with a swirling portal. Enter this to reach our next story location, "Forgotten Battlefield", where you will immediately enter a cutscene.

The cutscene ends with you in battle and introduces you to the gradient counter mechanic, as well as how Verso plays. Gradient attacks from enemies are always shown with that grey wash of the screen and are countered with . Normal parries will not work on them and gradient counters will not work on normal enemy attacks. If you are parrying a lot and are good at timings and counters, Verso will be incredibly powerful as you'll have him at A/S rank more. Check your party after this battle, swap in/out who you want and then continue forward along the linear path until you reach the first flag.
steps.heading: Forgotten Battlefield

steps.text: After resting, move onward to find yourself at the start of a large open battlefield. I'm sure my routing here will not be the most efficient but I tried to do it in a way that was easy to follow along with, without needing loads of pictures. Look to your right, at the start of the area, and you should see a short wooden ramp. Head up this and up it again to the left. At the top, on the right, is a Polished Chroma Catalyst.

Return to the main path and follow it down and to the right. You will be at a roundabout of sorts, with various paths leading off of it. First, head to the right, moving counter-clockwise around it. Take the first path to the right and loot 988x Chroma from the right side at the end. Drop down into the trench below. Turn left and run straight into the next trench ahead, ignoring the paths to the left and right. Loot the "Energising Start IV" pictos from the end of the trench. Turn around and now take the right path back up until you are back at the roundabout. Turn right and follow the right edge to an enemy. You are now above the trench where you just looted the pictos. Keep following this right edge and you will see a ramp going up to your left ahead. Drop off the ramp to the right and loot a Revive Tint Shard from the trench below, bringing your total to 6! Follow this trench to the end and return to the ramp. At the top of the ramp is a flag you can rest at.

Go back down the ramp now and climb the ledges to the left, following the only path you can until you reach another flag. Take the handholds to the left of the flag and then follow the path again, the only way you can, down a short flight of steps. Defeat the enemy ahead and pass through the archway. Turn right and take the stairs up, taking the right path at the top to loot a Colour of Lumina. Now go out onto the balcony. On the left end, when facing out towards the battlefield, you can loot the "Energising Death" pictos.

Return back down the short stairs and turn right. Defeat the enemies at the bottom of the stairs for a Colour of Lumina. Now return to the flag and fast travel to the main gate. Return once again to the roundabout area, we have one more path to explore before carrying on with the main story route. This time take a left on the roundabout and follow the path to the left and down. There is another split in the path ahead. Take the right path first and loot the Colour of Lumina at the end.

Return to the split and take the left path. You will see a purple item pickup in the back left corner ahead. Loot this for a Colour of Lumina. Go under the large arch opposite the item and up the stairs. Defeat the enemies here and then go through the doors/windows to the left to find a Recoat. Take the path behind where the enemies you just fought were, and go to the bottom of the ramp. Turn around and you will see another purple item to your right. This is a Healing Tint Shard, which should take your total to 5. Now take the ramp up, defeat the enemy and loot the "Sweet Kill" pictos from behind them.

We've now got everything we want to get here. Head back to the ramp and drop off it to the right. We're now back at the split path. Take the right path here back up, and keep going straight, past the wrecked boat to your left. You will see a ramp ahead. This is the one we took earlier that leads to a flag. Take it, rest at the flag and then drop down through the gap in the fence to the left of it. Before moving down the path, there is a very easy to miss Energy Tint Shard here.

The main path is to the left side in the image. To the right of it, barely visible, in the corner, are some breakable crates. Break these for the shard. Now follow the main path until you reach the woman ahead. There are multiple paths here. Take the right path first. Turn left, before the purple item and loot [Journal #14/49 - Expedition 41]. Now take the purple item for a Colour of Lumina. Take the path straight to the end and follow it round the corner.
The enemy ahead is an optional Chromatic boss. It drops the usual slew of upgrade materials, a weapon for Sciel and the "Energising Parry" pictos which gives +1 AP for every successful parry.
Fire Explosion: The popup will say that the boss is "charging a fire explosion". There will be two "pulses" first and then the attack goes off. Easy to time, just dodge/parry on the 3rd.
steps.heading: Chromatic Luster - Attacks

steps.text: Fast Combo: As the name suggests. The first one has a bit of a lead in, and then the other two are back to back.

Fury Unleashed: You may remember this attack from the Flying Waves area. The boss will charge through random party members, up to four times. The sweet spot is to parry just a split second after he hunches his arms back between each charge.
Absorb Burns: The boss will absorb burn stacks off of your characters to heal itself. You will accrue burn stacks from being hit by the boss.

Mechanically, this boss is very simple but it can easily one-shot party members if they are hit by even a single attack, at least on higher difficulties. The boss will absorb ANY fire attacks and will heal, so you may want to look at Maelle/Lune's skills before fighting this guy. The fire explosion is a very easy parry that gives nice damage in return. I mostly just applied mark on the boss here with Sciel and Verso, then used Percee with Maelle as even in defensive stance, it does high damage.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: With the boss defeated, return the way you came and take the first left path. Look to your left at what appears to be a dead end, to see a rope. Climb it and loot the "Empowering Tint" pictos. Now make your way back to the woman where all the paths split. Facing the woman head on, turn to your left 90 degrees and you will see a flag. Take the path to the right of the flag and as it turns to the left, you will see a purple item. Loot it for a Colour of Lumina.

You can continue past the flag for a Petank and some Chroma if you want to be thorough. Otherwise, rest at the flag and then take the only path we haven't, the one behind the woman. Take the left path when it splits and break the crates here to destroy Lock #1 of a nearby paint cage. Now take the right back and then the first left turn. The cage itself is ahead on the left here and to the right of it are more crates. Break these to destroy Lock #2. Finally, when facing the cage turn around. Above you, on top of a wall back the way you came, is Lock #3. Loot the Chroma Elixir Shard from the cage.

Now take the remaining left path into an open area. You should be able to see [Journal #15/49 - Expedition 57] just ahead. Take the stairs ahead of where you looted the journal and climb the rope to reach a merchant. You will see that he sells a pictos called "Inverted Affinity". Inverted is a status effect that means you can't be healed, as you will take damage if healing is applied. Fighting the merchant will unlock an outfit for Maelle in the merchant shop if you win.
Drop down from here and follow the path to the right, under the archway. Rest at the flag and then cross the bridge for a cutscene. It's boss time!
Swiping Combo: A slow, 4 hit attack that is quite easily timed. It is one hit, one jump and then two more hits.
steps.heading: Dualliste - Attacks - Phase 1

steps.text: Expedition Attack: The popup will say that "Dualliste attacks the expedition". This attack hits all party members. The boss will twirl its sword and then plunge it into the ground. Parry just before the sword hits the ground.

Dualliste Combo: The popup will say "Dualliste performs a combo". This is a 5 hit combo with harder timing than the swiping combo above as there is a wind-up before the first hit and a short delay between each subsequent one.

Swift Attack: The popup will say "Dualliste attacks swiftly". This is a 3 hit combo that, despite its name, isn't that swift. As with the Dualliste combo, there is a wind-up before the first hit and each subsequent one.
Expedition Attack: Do not be fooled by this. In phase 2, there are TWO hits. Parry the first as usual and then listen for the "ping" sound cue, indicating a second parry.
steps.heading: Dualliste - Attacks - Phase 2

steps.text: Inversion: Dualliste applies the inverted status effect to the party. This cannot be avoided. Characters affected by inversion cannot be healed so make sure not to accidentally use healing tints on anyone.

Dualliste Combo: This is an amped-up version of the phase 1 Dualliste combo. This now comprises of a whopping EIGHT hits finished off with a ninth, gradient attack. Remember to counter the gradient with . The combo itself is quite slow but you can quickly get caught out if you miss 1-2 hits.
Swift Attack: This is a much longer attack than its phase 1 counterpart but thankfully is still quite slow. There is one hit, followed by TWO jumps back to back, followed by THREE more parries.

Stormblood: The boss summons multiple blood clones of itself to attack you, followed by attacking itself. The clones are a little hard to see because of the arena darkness. There will be a clone attacking from the left, right and middle, followed by the boss performing a stab move. There is a really long windup at the start and a long delay between each.

This boss tends to be the first big step up for many due to the slew of abilities and how many hits they all consist of. This is a two phase fight so as with the Lampmaster, you want to try and save your revive tints until phase two. At this point I was using Sciel, Verso and Maelle. I essentially just kept applying foretell/burn/mark and then using Maelle for the heavy hitting attacks.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: This boss is purely just learning what and how to avoid each combo. Once you are through 3/4 of the boss health in p2, he will affect everyone with inversion. DO NOT heal your party or they will take damage from this. An important note about the 9 hit combo is you can miss all eight but if you hit the gradient counter at the end, you will still counter. Due to this, it may be easier to dodge everything until the gradient as dodging has a more lenient window than parrying, then parry the gradient attack at the end for a good counter. Note that if someone dies with inverted, you CAN revive them. They will not have inversion after being revived.

When back in control, find your way to the interactable orb and use it to form a rope. It's a little hard to see in this area. There is another orb at the top. Before using it, crawl through the gap to the left of it for a Colour of Lumina. Now take the rope, followed by the grapple point. Follow the path the only way you can, past the remnants of the bridge and round a corner to the left where the music will change. When the path splits here, take a right and then go left at the top to find the "Revive Tint Energy" pictos. Turn around and follow the path ahead and to the left, round a corner. You will see a red tree ahead. Approach it for a cutscene.
After the cutscene, go straight ahead and return to the world map. For completing this area, you will unlock:

steps.name: Forgotten Battlefield
steps.description: Find your way through Forgotten Battlefield.

steps.text: Make sure to do all the busywork first, upgrade weapons and assign Lumina points. This time round you can speak to all party members and increase relationship levels. Speak to Lune and Sciel and choose to spend time with each to reach Relationship Level 1 with them. Spend time with Esquie for Relationship Level 2. Check up on the others (do it twice for two optional scenes), and write in the journal at the campfire, then choose to sleep. You will automatically reach Relationship Level 1 with Maelle.
steps.heading: Camp

steps.text: Back in control after the cutscene, press to check the map. You will see that you are now on the other side of the Forgotten Battlefield. Our next story destination, Monoco's Station lies to the North-West and is a simple run over.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: This is a similar area to the Gestral Village in that it is more like a hub of sorts than a dungeon. On entering, move ahead and rest at the flag if needed. Follow the path the only way you can until it opens up. Head under the big archway to the right and turn left before the flag. Go behind the trains here to find 2,180x Chroma at the end. Rest at the flag so you get it as a fast travel point and then move past it for a cutscene, after which you will find yourself in a battle.
steps.heading: Monoco's Station

steps.text: Standard Attack: Monoco uses his base attack. A one hit attack with a little windup.
steps.heading: Monoco - Attacks

steps.text: Dual Attack: Same as above but with two hits rather than one. The second hit comes in fast after the first despite what the animation may look like.
Relentless Combo: Monoco takes on the form of a Nevron and performs a 6 hit combo. A few hits of this connecting will outright kill you and it's pretty fast.

Unlike Sciel's fight earlier, this is a bit more serious. His attacks will decimate you if you don't have many points in vitality and he doesn't have an insubstantial amount of health either. The standard attack and dual attack are both fairly easy parries once you've seen them but absolutely dodge the relentless combo unless you are confident you can parry it successfully as it hurts a lot and its very fast.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Back in control after the cutscene, we must now go and fight another Nevron to protect the station. Turn around and loot the Colour of Lumina here, then rest at the flag on the way back to the arch. Head through it for another cutscene and another battle. This battle will also introduce you to how gradient attacks work. These are very powerful attacks that are generated by spending AP across characters. Using one does NOT take a turn up. Keep an eye on your gradient charges as the game isn't great at informing you that you have them.
Earthquakes: The popup will say that the boss "creates earthquakes". This is an easy 3 jump counters back to back. Don't jump the second you see the symbol or you will be too early.
steps.heading: Stalact - Attacks

steps.text: Combo Attack: A 4 hit combo. There is quite a long windup on the first hit and there is a delay between each.
Explosion: After "heating up", the boss will explode in a couple of turns.

This is more an intro to gradient attacks than anything. The boss doesn't have much health and is a normal enemy in the next area anyway. The fight opens with the earthquakes move so be ready to jump straight away. After doing enough damage, the boss will "heat up" and gain six shields. Destroy them quickly and kill the boss before it can do the explosion attack above.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: You will unlock the below achievement during the cutscene, as Monoco will now join the party, becoming the final party member:

You will be prompted to play Monoco's tutorial. As with Sciel, I'd recommend doing this to see how he works. There is an achievement linked to Monoco for learning all of his skills. Monoco MUST be in the party when you kill an enemy that drops a skill. Monoco does not need to have the killing blow or to even be alive, but he must be one of the three party members fighting. There are multiple ways you can tackle gaining skills. A number are available now if you want to backtrack through previous areas, or you can just permanently have Monoco in your party and never worry about missing anything.

Guide wise, I will be pointing out enemies as we go that give Monoco skills but I won't be going out of my way to get them as almost all of them can be obtained in a single post-game area. A lot will come down to how much you play Monoco. I didn't have him in the active party much so not having skills wasn't an issue. If you think you will play him more, it may be worth doing some backtracking first.

In terms of mechanics, Monoco is quite simple. You want to try and have a spread of skills so that you have one for each mask type. This means that provided you have the AP, you can always cast a move that corresponds with the wheels current mask.
With Monoco's tutorial complete, you will unlock the below achievement for completing this short area:

steps.name: Monoco's Station
steps.description: Find your way through Monoco's Station.

steps.text: Turn around when back in control and you will see that the station where the flag is, is now packed with NPCs. Most of them can be spoken to for goodies if you wish. Head to the back of this area, where we first fought Monoco, and take a left. Cross over the train tracks and on the left here is [Journal #16/49 - Expedition 65]. Cross back over the tracks and go all the way back to the large cavern where we fought the Stalact. With the archway behind you, go straight ahead here, across the room and up the slope. Exit out to the Continent.

Check your map again to get your bearings. As with the Forgotten Battlefield, we are now on the other side of the Monoco's Station area, with our next destination, Old Lumiére to the North-West. You will see a group of enemies ahead. Have Monoco in the party here to unlock the [Monoco Skill - Cultist Slashes]. Now head onward to your destination and enter Old Lumiére.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Head down the hill and take the rope down. Rest at the flag ahead and spend some time here assigning points and pictos to any party members that you haven't used in a while as the party will be split shortly and everyone will get a go. There is a merchant opposite the flag. Defeating him will unlock a weapon for Sciel in his inventory. Note that this merchant sells a Revive Tint Shard for a measly 1,000x Chroma. Definitely worth the investment.
steps.heading: Old Lumiére

steps.text: Proceed down the only path you can for a cutscene, after which your party will consist of Sciel, Monoco and Lune. There is another flag ahead if you didn't assign stuff and now need to. Take the path to the left of the flag until it opens up and you can see a path left and right. Defeat the enemies here first for [Monoco Skill - Chevaliére Thrusts] and [Monoco Skill - Chevaliére Piercing]. Now take the right path, defeat the enemies and follow the path up. At the top, look to your left for a red item. Loot this for a weapon for Monoco.

Now return to the fork and take the left path, grappling twice to reach the area below. Look ahead and see a gap you can crawl under, do so and loot 4,990x Chroma. Crawl back through, and take the path up the hill. You will drop down ahead and then reach a turning to the left. Instead of taking this, drop off the platform to the right and loot the "Time Tint" pictos below. Now return to the corner and take the left path. There are some ledges you can climb up shortly on the right where there is an enemy guarding a Colour of Lumina.

Continue to follow the main path until you reach a cutscene, after which, you will be in control of Maelle and Verso. First off, head to the destroyed wall on the right side of this area and look behind it for a sneaky Colour of Lumina. Follow the path down to the next flag, and then continue to follow it down the hill until you again reach a more open area. Look to the right, and move through the archway to the right of the big sword in the ground.

As soon as you pass through the arch, look to your right. You will see what looks like a crane ahead. Move to the edge here and drop down onto the pipe to loot the Polished Chroma Catalyst. Now drop through the hole in the pipe and turn around. Open the gate here using the old key you looted way back in the prologue. Here is [Journal #17/49 - Fracture Survivor]. Activate the orb at the end of the pipe and use the rope to return topside. Climb up the ledges and this time go right, away from the arch.

The path again splits. Take the left path to loot 2,495x Chroma, then take the right path. You will reach two enemies that are stationary. Defeat them and a cutscene ensues, after which you will be left with just Maelle. Look right to see a grapple point. Follow the path to the right and around to it, then use it to reach the platform above where you can loot a Colour of Lumina. Turn left and drop back down to the main path.

Follow it the only way you again, defeating an enemy and grappling over a gap in the bridge. After the grapple, take the archway to the left and loot the "Auto Rush" pictos that the enemies are guarding. Continue on the main path as it bends to the right and you will see a destroyed building ahead. Take a left here, climb up the ledge and follow the balcony around to loot a Polished Chroma Catalyst. Return to the main path and follow it, grappling over another gap to arrive at a large open area with the manor in the distance. Rest at the flag and then look to your left.

You will see a gap in the wall ahead. Go through it, turn right and loot 2,495x Chroma from near the gate at the end. Head back to the gap and move past it. Look to your right and go to the door that is at the back here, at an angle. Interact with it to enter the Manor.

You will be in a bathroom. Look immediately right and loot [Record #8/34 - Renoir]. Open the doors here to enter the bedroom and look right. Loot [Journal #18/49 - Renoir]. Exit via the other doors here and leave the manor. Back in Old Lumiére, rest at the flag if you need to or didn't before. Approach the manor itself this time to start a cutscene, after which you will be facing another boss!

Chroma Burst: The popup will say that the boss "gathers an incredible amount of chroma". This an attack that hits your whole party and it requires a gradient counter. There is a LONG wind-up to this. The camera will zoom out slowly before going back in for the pulse. This is when to parry. There is also an audio cue for this attack. Below 50% this attack will be 3 pulses not 1. The first two pulses require normal parries and the 3rd requires the gradient counter.
steps.heading: ??? - Attacks

steps.text: Ranged Attack: The popup will say that the boss "attacks from a distance". This is a 4 hit combo with various delays. It is fairly obvious when to parry. This will get beefed up sub 50% and have more hits.

Vanish: The boss will attempt to gommage a character, removing them from the battle entirely. This attack requires a gradient counter. The boss will summon a black orb and then jump, you need to counter shortly after the jump, before he hits the orb.

Melee Combo: Probably the easiest attack of them all to parry. This is a 5 hit combo. The first four attacks are quite quick and well telegraphed. There is a short delay before the 5th and final one. There is a 6th hit after 50% which will stun a character if it connects.
Chroma Pool: Very easy. This is just a simple jump counter.

Gather Petals: At around 50% health, the boss will summon these petals. Free aim will not be enough here, so you need to destroy them physically. Absolutely prioritise these as they will heal the boss basically to full health.

Summon Masks: Sub 50%, the boss will summon masks. Giant masks appear in the sky that tilt and then hit. Just after they tilt, you want to parry. There are 6 hits and then all 3 masks will tilt together for the final hit. If the final hit connects with the party, it will inflict everyone with exhausted.

Chroma Waves: Sub 50%, the boss will cast this ability. He will pulse 5 times, with you needing to parry just before he pulses. The first four are pretty quick with there being a delay before the 5th.

This is another fun boss fight with an epic music score and a whole array of moves. To further complicate things, a few of his abilities gain more hits sub 50%, similar to how Dualliste's combos got longer. One thing to note is that your party will automatically be Lune, Maelle and Verso. However, should you die, you will get to choose who to take. As for the fight itself, this is a one phase fight, so feel free to go ham on tints without worry.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: At 50%, he will use the summon mirrors move mentioned above. The fight can be a struggle if the boss successfully vanishes a character, so play close attention to this move. The Chroma Burst will decimate your party if it connects, so prioritise avoiding this at all costs. Remember to keep an eye on your gradient charges and unleash a gradient move when at one charge. It doesn't cost a character their turn and does a lot of damage, the game just isn't great at notifying you of it. If you break the boss around 50%, you will delay him from casting the petals move until he is no longer stunned.
Defeating the boss will automatically start a cutscene during which you will unlock the below achievement for completing Old Lumiére:

steps.name: Old Lumière
steps.description: Find your way through Old Lumière.

steps.text: After the cutscene ends, you will be back at camp.

You automatically have [Journal #19/49 - Expedition 58]. Technically you looted this at the end of Lune/Sciel/Monoco's section earlier but this is the first time you can actually listen to it. As usual, upgrade weapons/tints and add Lumina points, then it's relationship time. You may be ahead on relationship levels here if you camped at all previously. You can't go past the current cap but if you have already got some of these characters levelled, it's totally fine. As usual, none of the dialogue choices matter.
steps.heading: Camp

steps.text: Spend time with Monoco twice to get to level 2.
Spend time with Esquie twice to get to level 4 - This unlocks a new gradient attack for Verso.
Spend time with Sciel twice to get to level 3.
Spend time with Lune twice to get to level 3.
Spend time with Maelle twice to get to level 3.
With all of that done, write in the journal if you wish and check up on the others for another optional scene. Go to sleep.

Just like when we finished with Stone Wave Cliffs, we are going to do a little backtracking here quickly. Esquie also has a new ability that allows you to swim through and break the coral reefs. The expedition escape ability is also useful to quickly return to the Continent from any flag. Turn around and re-enter Old Lumiére.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: You will start off where the manor was before you fought the boss, with the flag ahead of you. Look to the left from the flag and you will see a path sloping up in the distance. Take this and slide down the rope to the right at the top. Defeat the enemy here, loot 4,990x Chroma from the chair and then loot [Journal #20/49 - Expedition 42]. It can be a little hard to see, it is right next to the sword implanted in the ground.
steps.heading: Old Lumiére

steps.text: Climb the rope back up and go back down the slope. Follow the edge of the area to the left until you reach another slope. On the wall to the right is Lock #1 for the upcoming paint cage.
A few steps ahead, you will see the paint cage and to the right of it, attached to a chunk of wall, is lock #2.
Finally, approach the cage and look to the cliff behind it for lock #3.
Loot a new weapon for Lune from the cage and return to the Continent. That's all here for now.

Now time to continue to the next story area. Open the map and you will see two red destinations this time. Whilst you can go to either first, the left is easier and the order that most do it in. Mount Esquie, smash through the reef ahead and swim all the way to the red destination on the left. The entrance to this area is straight ahead as you approach the island.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Follow the path ahead the only way you can. When you see the giant face ahead, look to the right and loot a Colour of Lumina. Take the narrow path to the left of the face until you reach a cutscene and a flag. Back in control you are actually free to go wherever here. The path past the merchant you can see ahead leads to the boss who can be fought right now if you wish. The other paths lead to mini bosses that when defeated, make the actual boss fight easier, plus there's collectibles in each of them.
steps.heading: Visages

steps.text: First of all, let's go to the merchant and fight him. Defeating him unlocks access to a weapon for Sciel. Note that this merchant also sells 5x Resplendent Chroma Catalysts. These allow you to upgrade weapons to level 19!

Return to the flag and face the path you came in from. Take the path to the right of it. The scenery will shift to green from red and there will be a short scene once you enter the mouth ahead. In the new area, follow the path ahead until you see two enemies. Put Monoco in your party here as they give the [Monoco Skill - Moissonneuse Vendance]. Head through the tunnel to the right of where the enemies were to arrive at a flag.

From the flag, follow the right wall up a short hill. Loot a Healing Tint Shard on the right. Make sure Monoco is still in your party and then defeat the big enemy opposite the shard to obtain [Monoco Skill - Contortionniste Blast]. Still with Monoco in your party, go back down the slope and defeat the enemies here to obtain [Monoco Skill - Chapelier Slash]. Let's reorient. With the flag behind you, and the slope we went up to the right, there are two more paths to take. Take the left path now and look to the left when you reach what looks like a weapon stuck in the ground. Loot 2,940x Chroma. Follow the path past the weapon and turn left at the end of the path to see a journal and some enemies.

There is another skill to get here as this group of enemies gives you [Monoco Skill - Boucheclier Fortify]. Now loot [Journal #21/49 - Expedition 69]. That is all Monoco skills for this side area so feel free to swap him out now. If you turn right from the journal and follow the left wall all the way round, you will find a Mime here. This one drops an outfit and haircut for Verso. Now return back to the area near the flag and go down the middle path. You will see a giant mask in front of you, don't approach it yet as it starts a battle.

Look to the right in this area to see some enemies and a slope leading up. Defeat the enemies and loot the Resplendent Chroma Catalyst to the right of where they were. Then climb the slope and loot the "Confident Fighter" pictos from the right corner here. Drop down from here and go straight across this area to find a path behind a tree. Defeat the enemy and then loot the weapon for Verso. Rest at the flag again if needed to heal up, and then approach the giant mask.

When asked the question, respond with A) Joy. This will trigger a boss fight. I haven't created a section for this as the "boss" is just a slightly stronger normal enemy. The boss will do a long combo attack that is a good number of hits, I found it easier to just dodge. Defeat the two normal enemies first and then go for the boss. The mask will heal the boss every turn so you need to try and parry as much as possible to get free damage from counters. Buff your characters if you can and go for the most damaging abilities possible. On harder difficulties you can get stuck in a loop where you can't outdamage the heal. Remember, every turn that you heal or revive someone is lost damage on the boss.

I reached level 33 upon killing the boss. You might already be there by now but if not, you should be close and will get it within Visages. You will unlock the below achievement once you reach level 33:

With the boss defeated, you will find yourself back at the flag we first arrived at in this area. That's one path down, two to go before the main boss of this area. Rest up as needed and then take the next path along, in the back left corner. Follow the path until you reach another mask and are again teleported. Take the only direction you can, defeat the enemy and arrive at the next flag. This time we will follow the wall to the left from the flag to loot a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Keep following this left edge and you will eventually see a platform ahead with an enemy on it. This is a Chromatic boss. There is also the "Glass Cannon" pictos you can loot from the platform without fighting. The boss drops the usual upgrade materials as well as a skill for Monoco. Note that you do not need to kill the chromatic enemy just for the skill, it can be obtained off any normal enemy of the same type.

Nevron Arm Combo: The popup will say that the boss "attacks with a nevron arm combo". This is a 4 hit combo. It goes windup -> Hit 1 -> Hit 2 -> Windup -> Hit 3 -> Hit 4. There is also an 8 hit combo that consists of the 4 hit combo, followed by another windup, then 2 more hits and then another 2 straight after without a windup. Best advice is just to be ready for the 8 but if you get the 4 then great.
steps.heading: Chromatic Ramasseur - Attacks

steps.text: Mortal Hit: The boss does one long windup attack. Unlike the regular version of the enemy, this can just be normal parried, it doesn't require a gradient counter.

If you're not too hot on parries, you might struggle here as you will not get an attack unless you parry and counter successfully. This is a gimmick that other bosses use later so there is no way round it really. After a few rounds of countering, you will break the boss and it's time to go big damage. Note that if you don't kill the boss within the stun window, it will begin chain attacking again, in which case you need to again parry until you break it. I had all but Maelle dead when I did this and it took me a long to kill it. But you also won't get a chance to revive characters until you break it. It's an annoying boss. Unfortunately, there isn't much in the way of strategy here as your only option is to parry everything. He tends to cycle moves and never repeats twice. If you get an 8 hit combo, the next nevron arm attack will be 4 and vice versa.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: With the boss dead, return to the main area here. With the flag behind you, take the middle path, just like we did in the Joy Vale. You will see another giant mask ahead. Just like in the previous area, take the path to the right. There is a slope directly ahead and another slope to the left. Take the slope ahead and turn right at the top. Defeat the enemies here and then loot the Energy Tint Shard.

Now take the slope we ignored. Defeat the enemies then continue all the way up, climbing a ledge at the top and looting [Journal #22/49 - Expedition 39]. Go back and rest at the flag if needed and then approach the giant mask. This time choose "Sadness" and another boss battle will begin. This is a similar situation to the one we just did, with two regular enemies and a "boss" version of another enemy. The mask this time puts exhaust on a party member each turn, which means no AP gain. You can clear it off but it will be reapplied. Annoying but to me at least it wasn't as arduous as dealing with it constantly healing the boss. The boss itself can only be hit by free aim attacks or parries as it counts as a flying enemy. Kill the two regular enemies and then, same as last time, turn your attention to the boss. You shouldn't have too much issue here. Note that you can use energy tints for AP and then spam free aim to kill the Boss.

Again, with the boss defeated, you find yourself back in the starting area for Visages. Rest at the flag and then take the only path we haven't yet, in the back right corner to the right of the merchant (not the one opposite him). Exact same deal here. Follow the path until you reach a mask and are teleported. Then head to the flag. This area is laid out in a similar manner to the others. You will already be able to see the giant mask down the path to the right.

Head towards the mask, and look to the right. There is a cave entrance here and to the left of it, a slope. Go into the cave first where the path will split. Take the right path and open the door here to enter the Manor. Pan the camera slightly left here and you will see the purple item. Loot it for [Record #9/34 - Verso]. Open the door to the left of this and loot [Journal #23/49 - Unknown]. Leave via the other door here and exit the manor.

Back in the cave, take the other path this time, defeat the enemies and loot the "Double Burn" pictos. Leave the cave and now take the slope to the right, looting a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst at the top. Now go back down the slope and stand with the cave to your back. Just like in the first area we came to, there is a path opposite. Cross over to it, defeat the enemy and loot the "Powered Attack" pictos. Look to the right of the path leading back to see a rope. Take it up and follow the ledge around to another group of enemies. Defeat them and loot the Revive Tint Shard they were guarding. Drop down from here and return to the flag to rest before approaching the giant mask one more time.

This time round choose "Anger". This is in a similar vein to the two you've done already. This is the easiest of the three as the "boss" this time just gets given an extra turn now and then by the mask. This essentially just make this boss fight a normal fight. You should have no issues at all here. After defeating the "boss", you will again be back in the main hub for this area. It's now time to take the path opposite the merchant. Follow the path the only way you can and you will eventually reach another flag. Check pictos and skills here, then move on for a cutscene and the main boss of this area.
Determination Mask: This is just a simple 3 hit combo. A long windup for the first hit, parrying just before it slams into the ground followed by a jump counter and another parry.
steps.heading: Visages - Phase 1 - Attacks

steps.text: Anxiety Mask: This is a 2 hit combo with sound cues. Parry when you hear the ping. If the attack connects, your characters will become afflicted with the exhaust effect.

Doubt Mask: This is a 5 hit combo. I personally found this one hard to parry just because it's hard to really gauge when the massive boss will hit you. Each hit is also delayed which makes timing difficult. Your mileage may vary but I dodged this one.

Peace Mask: This is a 4 hit combo. Every attack that connects will give the boss one shield. This is a quick combo with all four attacks back to back. Again, I found this difficult to gauge as there is no telegraphed move really. I almost always missed the first one but then got in rhythm for the others.
Confidence Mask: This is just one attack but if it connects, the boss will heal for around 9/10K. The Mask will rise up then slam down.
Swing Combo: A 3 hit combo. There is a little windup before the first hit. Hits 2 and 3 follow quick.
steps.heading: Mask Keeper - Phase 2 - Attacks

steps.text: Storm Attack: The popup will say that the boss "attacks like a storm". This is just a 4 hit combo. Hist 1-3 are quite quick and then there is a delay before hit 4.
Long Swing: This is a 6 hit combo

Defensive Aura: After the boss activates this, every hit that connects will give him a shield. This is no issue with certain skills but if you have no way to easily remove shield, 100% dodge if needed rather than parry.
Vehement Attack: This is a 6 hit combo
Chaotic Combo: This is an 8 hit combo
Fire Sword: The boss will set fire to his sword and then do a 3 hit combo ending with a gradient counter

This is two bosses, although it is fought as one fight so I have listed it in phases. The Visages stage has a lot of moves to learn and can take a while for everything to click. As with the other 2 phase bosses we've fought, you want to try and hold onto tints as long as you can. For boss one, your attacks will be focused on the mirror, which will produce different themed masks, each with their own attacks. The first boss looks intimidating but the attacks are actually pretty easy to learn. As we defeated all of the giant masks at the end of the optional paths, the boss will be unable to call masks in this phase.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Try not to lose your cool here as whilst there are lots of 6 and 8 hit combos, you can instinctively dodge them as they are all quite easy to gauge.
Defeating the boss will start another cutscene. You will unlock the below achievement for defeating the first axon:
After another cutscene you will be back at camp.

You know the drill by now. Upgrade your weapons, assign Lumina points etc. There is a MISSABLE scene during this camp. Make sure you choose to check up on the others at the fire. If you have been doing this every time we've been at camp, you should get the scene we need right away where Verso plays the piano. You will receive [Record #10/34 - Lettre á Maelle]. If you don't get this scene straight away, don't panic. You should be able to choose to check up on the others until you're caught up. There will be a warning when we head for the end of Act II and a reminder to do this again if you don't do it here. But you're here already...so you might as well. Supposedly you have until the end of Act II to get it, just make sure you get it now and then it's done.
steps.heading: Camp

steps.text: Speak to Sciel once to reach level 4. This unlocks a new gradient attack for Sciel.
Speak to Lune once to reach level 4. This unlocks a new gradient attack for Lune.
Speak to Malle once to reach level 4. This unlock a new gradient attack for Maelle.
Speak to Monoco once to reach level 3.
If you didn't do it above, check up on the others for the missable record and then sleep.
Nothing much to do here other than check the map for the next red destination to the east. Swim to this island and enter "Siréne".
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: This is another chunky area, much like Visages, although it's just one pretty linear path this time. Head straight ahead to start a cutscene. Back in control, move onto the platform ahead and interact with it to get it moving. Head the only way you can at the bottom and take the first right you see. Follow this passage to the end and loot a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Return to the previous area and continue on, down the steps and forward to the next flag.
steps.heading: Siréne

steps.text: Put Monoco in your party if he isn't already as we can get a skill ticked off ahead. Defeating the first group of enemies ahead up the right stairs will give [Monoco Skill - Ballet Charm]. Continue forward, the only way you can to see another group of enemies. Defeat them and then look to the balcony on the right. Here is [Journal #24/49 - Expedition 55]. Move to the edge of this balcony to loot a Colour of Lumina.

Go into the opening opposite this balcony and turn left to see a rope. Take it down and turn right into a room. There is an enemy on the right and a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst on the left. Leave this room and look right where you will see a grapple point. Follow the path downstairs and you will end up back outside with one of those moving platforms ahead. Look to the left here for a paint cage. Locks 1 and 2 should be visible to its left and behind it.
To find lock #3, turn around and you will see some rubble ahead. Look behind this for the lock.

Loot the "Shield Affinity" pictos and then take the moving platform. When you arrive at a new platform, look to the left here for a Chromatic boss. This one drops a weapon for Verso. You can also loot the "Effective Heal" pictos from behind the boss without fighting if you wish.

Stab Attack: Just like with the normal enemy variant. The boss stabs itself, generating shields before swinging at you. This is an extended combo compared to the original, with two hits, one jump and then FOUR more hits. It feels like the same timing as the normal enemy so you shouldn't have too much trouble here.
steps.heading: Chromatic Greatsword Cultist - Attacks

steps.text: Jump Attack: This is identical to the normal enemy version. It's a bit of a windup but very easy to time.

This is one of the easier chromatic bosses by far. Just make sure you can remove shields easily and you are laughing with this one. Both attacks are very easy to time and parry so you will be full of AP constantly.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: I got [Monoco Skill - Cultist Blood] here but as with the previous chromatic boss, there is no need to fight it just for this as you can get it an endgame area later. With the boss out of the way, head the only other way on this platform. There is a purple item near a destroyed pillar, loot it for a Colour of Lumina. Go to the end of this area and loot the "Greater Shell" pictos after defeating the enemies here. Look to the right of the pictos to see some handholds blending in with the red fabric. Climb these and loot a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst from inside the cave at the top.

Leave the cave through the other opening and go right to the edge of this balcony where you will see an orb you can interact with to deploy a rope. This is right back at the start of the area. Follow the path until you reach one of the first flags we rested at. Rest if you need to then and continue on, this time going past the passage to the left all the way to the end where you will see another moving platform. At the other end, proceed forward into a large room. Taking the passage straight ahead will lead to a Petank that drops the usual hoard of upgrade materials. Tackle it if you want and then go right from this large room.

You will be in another big room with multiple paths. Put Monoco in your party if you don't already have him and drop off the ledge here to the bottom of the room. Defeat the enemy here for [Monoco Skill - Bénisseur Mortar]. Loot the "Auto Regen" pictos also and then find the ramp leading up at the edge of the room. At the first fork take a right, defeat the enemy and then go through the doorway behind. Move down the stairs in the next room. Instead of taking the path ahead, keep following the edge round to the left for a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Now take the main path to arrive at yet another moving platform.

Once at your destination, follow the edge of the room to the right where you will see a door to the Manor ahead. Inside, use free aim and shoot the large mirror on the right wall to open a passage. Climb through and then drop down to loot a Shape of Health. Follow the path out and leave the manor. Back in the Siréne area, move ahead past the fading man and loot a Colour of Lumina on the left. Go into the next passage and ignore the grapple for now, instead take the path to the right. Climb the ledge at the end and loot the "Protecting Death" pictos.

Return to the grapple and cross the gap. Follow the path all the way around this pillar for another Colour of Lumina. Again, cross the gap with the grapple. Take the left path, defeat the two enemies and loot the Resplendent Chroma Catalyst, then drop down off the balcony. To the left here is a Mime that drops a haircut for Lune. If you don't want to bother with it, move down the short steps ahead and then into the room on the left for the next flag.

Move into the next room with the giant creature. Interacting with it, you will be given a choice to fight it or leave it. Similar to Visages, if you leave it, the main boss will be affected. It may seem like you get something extra for leaving it because the characters comment on it not being hostile but you don't. Having said that, all it does to the main fight is add shields so it's really up to you if you want to fight it or not. It drops the "Anti-Charm" pictos and a weapon for Maelle.
Curse: The boss curses your entire party, killing them at the end of 8 turns. This cannot be dodged or parried.
steps.heading: Tisseur - Attacks

steps.text: Combo Attack: This is a fairly fast 5 hit combo comprised of two hits, two jumps and then another hit. There is a bit of windup before the first attack and then it's pretty much all back to back.
Smash: This is just a 1 hit attack where the boss smacks its hands together.
Weave: The boss weaves together an enemy and throws it at the party. This is just one hit
Swipe Combo: This is three back to back jump counters and then a normal hit

Bear in mind that with the curse, if a character dies and is revived, the curse is gone. The boss will cast curse again, but you don't have strictly 8 turns. You have to do a good amount of damage to the boss to kill it within strictly 8 turns and you will quickly fall behind if you have to heal/revive.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: After the battle, face the doorway we came from and pan to the left. You should see a purple item. Loot the Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Now look to the right of the doorway leading back to the flag. There are some ledges here you can climb. At the top, look up for Lock #1 attached to what looks like a spool of yarn.
Follow the path you're on all the way around to the paint cage and then look ahead to see lock #2
Follow this path right to the end and then look up and to your right for lock #3

Turn back to face where the paint cage was, and just before it, on the ledge with vases and pots, is a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Loot the Revive Tint Shard from the paint cage and then go back to rest at the flag if you fought Tisseur. Return to the boss room once more and look in the back right corner for a grapple point. Follow the path the only way you can until you reach a rope. Take this down, rest at the flag, and prepare for another boss!
Tail Slam: Quite an easy 3 hit combo. The tail swipes twice and then from above once. The final hit will have an audio cue.
steps.heading: Glissando - Attacks

steps.text: Head Smash: Another easy to time 2 hit combo. The boss slams its head into the group twice. There is a bit of a delay but you can sense this one pretty easily.
Enchant: The boss will try to charm one of your characters.
Summon Ballet: The boss will summon three of the ballet enemies you have fought in this area. This is a really simple 3 jump counter attack.
Gobble Up: The boss eats a party member, removing them from the battle.

This is more than likely one of the easiest bosses you've fought in a while. All of its attacks are easily dodged or parried and it's well telegraphed. If you killed Tisseur, definitely equip the anti-charm pictos, removing the boss's ability to charm one or all of your characters, depending who you have it equipped on. The boss has a deceptively large amount of health but it's a simple fight.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: After the fight, go rest at the flag and then, facing where the boss was, look to the right. There is a path back here. Loot the purple item for an Energy Tint Shard and then use the rope ahead. Follow this short path round to a grapple point and follow the path the only way you can. After crouching through a gap, look to the left for the "Healing Fire" pictos. Turn around and grapple across the gap ahead, looting the 1,763x Chroma ahead. The stairs going up here take us back to the boss we just defeated but we're not quite ready yet. Look back towards where you grappled from, opposite the Chroma pickup. There is a destroyed pillar here, move to its right side and climb the handholds.

Climb across them and then follow a short path to deploy another rope. Take this down to see a Petank ahead. Run past it, going up the stairs behind and go forwards. To the left of the Petank pad is a merchant. Defeat him to unlock access to a weapon for Maelle. Now backtrack to the boss room and this time take the stairs down opposite the flag to a moving platform. At the other end, turn around and you will see [Journal #25/49 - Expedition 67] waiting for you across the gap. Run around and loot it, then climb the stairs and rest at the flag. Check on your pictos and attribute points as the main boss for this area lies ahead. When ready, head through the tunnel beyond the flag for a cutscene, after which, you will be facing off against the final boss for this area.
Glissando Dance: Two Glissando's will appear either side of the boss and will slam into the party one after another. This is quite easily timed.
steps.heading: Siréne - Attacks

steps.text: Dress Attack: 3 hit combo. The boss will fire parts of its dress at you. The dress comes in quite fast but the timing itself isn't too bad once you know what to look for.

Ballet Charm: Same as the boss we just fought, a ballet enemy will fire an orb at a character. It pulses along to you. You want to parry just before it hits. Note that if this move is cast after the final act, there will be sets of orbs to dodge. The timing is the same for both.
Seduce: The boss will attempt to charm a character. This is a gradient attack.

Grand Ballet: This is a very flashy move but nothing happens until the ballet enemies are lined up in front of you. They will then take turns to charge through you from the right. This is a 5 hit combo.

Final Act: This is a souped up version of the grand ballet. Again, despite the flashy appearance, you are safe until the ballet enemies are in front. This time around you have to jump counter and then dodge/parry, jump and dodge, jump and dodge. After the 3rd dodge/parry, the boss throws a chunk of the building down at you to also avoid.
Ground Smash: A 3 hit combo where the boss slams the platform. Can be hard to see the first hit because of the camera and dark setting.
Ground Shake: Very easy, 3 jump counters back to back.

This boss has a lot of flashy moves that have long animations before anything happens. The boss itself isn't too hard. It just looks worse than it is. Read the moves above and bear in mind that the grand ballet particularly has a lot of dead time where the boss doesn't do anything. You are only in danger once the ballet enemies are in front of you. If you didn't kill the Tisseur enemy earlier on, the boss will have an extra move that will generate shields. It's not the end of the world, and assuming you are running at least one anti-shield ability, it is barely an inconvenience.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: For defeating the second axon, you will get a cutscene as well as the below achievement:
You will end up back in camp, where we have another round of relationship building to do before continuing onward to the second half of Act II.

sections.title: 7. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Act II - Part 2

steps.text: Camp
steps.heading: Act II - Part II

steps.text: Before our backtracking quest commences, we have the camp to deal with. Do the usual upgrading of weapons and Lumina points, making sure to assign new tints also. If you didn't collect the missable record yet outlined on the previous page during the optional camp scene, we are beginning to close in on the end of Act II. Make sure you get it!

Speak to Lune, Maelle and Sciel once each to get to level 5 with all of them. Speak to Monoco once to get to level 4 and unlock a new gradient attack for him. Note that you must beat Monoco in the duel to level up his relationship further. Interact with the campfire, write in the journal and then sleep for a cutscene.

We're now going to go back to side-areas as well as merchants on the world map to hoover up some goodies. As mentioned, I'm leaving Monoco skills until the post-game as there is a post-game dungeon where you can get virtually all of them. First things first, go to the world map location in the image below and enter the "Sinister Cave" located here.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: There is a flag right in front of you as you start. Move past it, through the tunnel and hug the right wall when you exit. Keep following it until you reach a slope with a grapple point at the top. There is a Chromatic boss down the path to the left of the ramp which drops a weapon for Maelle. Should you wish to fight it, the moveset is below.
steps.heading: Sinister Cave

steps.text: Relentless Combo: This is a 6 hit combo. If you just fought Monoco at camp, this is identical. The attacks are all fairly fast and timing is tricky.
steps.heading: Chromatic Chalier - Attacks

steps.text: Swiping Combo: A 3 hit combo. There is a jump counter first, then two more physical hits. This is a good deal easier to time than the above combo.
Punching Combo: A 3 hit combo. It has an awkward animation but once you've seen it once, this is the easiest of the three to parry.

With the boss dead, return to the ramp and this time use the grapple at the top. Once up, turn around and grapple again. Stick to the right edge and follow it until you reach a lamp on the ground. Follow the path down to the left of this until you reach a square hole in the ground. Face the wall in front of you and drop down. Loot [Record #11/34 - Nocturne pour Lumiére]. Drop off this little ledge here and go left to find yourself back at the entrance. Rest at the flag if you need to and then return to the Continent.
It's been a while but it's time for another Gestral Beach minigame. Head to the below location on the map.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: This one felt like the easiest of the bunch to me. It's essentially just a timed platforming course. You must reach the end in 38 seconds for it to count towards the achievement. Look to the right upon entering and speak to the Gestral here to begin. The course itself is quite simple and with a few cut corners, you will ace it in no time. Climb the platforms at the start, make sure to always be running and try to angle yourself at the corners to the next platform so you are landing and jumping again immediately, spamming to lift yourself up.
steps.heading: Gestral Beach

steps.text: When jumping across the spinning wheels, try to jump near the edge so you don't roll on landing as this wastes time. Once you reach the handholds, go right as it's a shorter route. Beating the 38-second time will award you with some upgrade materials and an outfit for Verso. One of the rewards is a Grandiose Chroma Catalyst. [Gestral Game #2/5].
Now go to the below location to find a merchant. Buy [Record #12/34 - Robe De Jour].
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Proceed to the below location for [Lost Gestral #3/9]. Note that you can interact with him and leave without fighting the enemies.
Continuing our world map tour, go to the below location where you will find a Chromatic Boss and a journal.
You can loot [Journal #26/49 - Expedition 43] from here without fighting the boss. If you want to fight it, the moves are below. The boss drops a weapon for Verso.

Dark Projectiles: The boss fires a projectile at one character, then a second and then 3 at the same time. There is a delay on this, as the projectile kind of flies backwards first before homing on a character. Do not be baited into parrying early.
steps.heading: Chromatic Reaper Cultist - Attacks

steps.text: 7 Hit Combo: The popup will just say the boss attacks. The first few attacks are delayed and the rest are pretty fast back to back. I parried the slow ones and dodged the fast ones.

Every time that the boss connects an attack, that character will receive a stack of "blight". Chances are this is your first time encountering this. It is a nasty effect that reduces a character's overall HP by 10% per stack. I.E If every attack in the 7 hit combo connects with the same character, they will be left with 70% less HP at the end. It is very difficult to hit this boss through normal attacks so you are stuck with either parry countering or doing what you can with free aim.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Hitting the orbs with free aim DOES do damage so my advice is to go for this first and then try to parry everything the boss throws at you. If a character dies with the blight effect and are revived, they will still have it unless you have used items which remove it another way. The long and short of this boss is that since the 7 hit combo will target multiple characters anyway, blight is unavoidable without learning the patterns and parrying.

Once dealt with, go to the below location to find [Lost Gestral #4/9]. It is found behind the mimes here, near some pots. The two mimes have the same moves as always, it's just that there are two of them now. They drop a hairstyle for Sciel and one for Lune.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: With that small batch of collectibles done, it's time to break things up with a side-dungeon, stopping off at a Gestral Beach on the way. Head south from the island where we just found the gestral and cross over land to reach the location below.

Fair warning, this one annoyed me a lot. This is essentially just a climbing challenge. The kicker though is that if you fall off at any point, you will likely fall back to the start and it is not a short climb. There are also some very annoying parts with jumps onto tiny ledges. A general rule of thumb is to always take your hand off the sticks when climbing and always spam . For most of the trickier jumps you don't want to be running either, simply get to the very edge and jump normally.
steps.heading: Gestral Beach

steps.text: Just before you reach the ship, there is a very small box-like object to jump to. This took me more tries than I'd like to admit. The best advice I can offer is to get as close to the edge of the object you are stood on and then tap forwards whilst spamming . Once you get it down the first time, it just kind of clicks after that. I found it easiest again with Maelle due to the smaller character model.

Once you've grappled across to the ship there are two paths you can take. Look to the back of the ship, and climb onto the tarp. Then jump across to the floating pot, not the lower. This is recommended as the easier route as the other route consists of smaller objects and the pots are just easier. Once you are on the next platform, look to your right and you will see a table to jump to. DO NOT run and jump to this. You will fall or overshoot. Just again, go to the edge and take a normal jump. You can run and jump the next gap.

From here, the challenge is fairly self-explanatory with no more branching paths or overly difficult bits. Just take your time. If you try and rush or get cocky, chances are you will fall and it is a long climb back up. Reach the top and speak to the gestrals up here to complete [Gestral Game #3/5].

At this point I decided to continue with the main story. Whilst there are certainly more collectibles that you can grab now, the post-game ability to fly around the map is just faster than running and swimming is now. Time for the Monolith itself. Head there now for a cutscene.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Following the cutscene, you will be on a small island with a merchant. Look nearby to find [Journal #27/49 - Expedition 40]. Approach the Monolith again, this time entering a new area for another cutscene. There is nothing to do here other than proceed down the only path you can. You will find yourself in another battle, after which you will be in another cutscene and will unlock the below achievement for reaching the Monolith:

This is a long area that takes you through bits from all the zones you've been in previously. On higher difficulties, I found this area to be a bit of a step up in difficulty also. We are nearing the end of Act II and I will point out when the final flag is so that you can still get the missable record if needed. Follow the path a short way until you find the first flag. Continue along the path, crossing over several grapples until you end up in a grassy area, reminiscent of the first area we found ourselves in way back in Act I. You may want to have Monoco in your party throughout this whole area as there are a lot of skills to pick up but it's up to you. You can always return later and get them, or grab them from the endgame area.
steps.heading: Inside the Monolith

steps.text: This first group of enemies by the water will drop [Monoco Skill - Lancelier Impale]. Loot the Colour of Lumina they were guarding and continue to the next flag. Turn around from the flag and go back the way you came, looking to the right before the picture frame for a path with a rope at the end. Attack the big enemy and win the battle for [Monoco Skill - Abbest Wind] and [Monoco Skill - Portier Crash].

Go down the next rope. You will see a paint cage ahead. Defeat the enemies here first so that you don't get interrupted whilst looking for the locks. With the enemies gone, face the rope. Look up and to the right of the rope to find Lock #1. Now take the path to your right and round the corner here, to the left, is Lock #2. Finally, go to the other side of this area where you will see another rope. Turn around so this rope is behind you and you will see Lock #3 ahead.
