Loot the Revive Tint Shard from where the cage was and then climb up the rope we haven't been up yet. Grapple across to end up back in the area by the flag. Take the path sloping down ahead and to the left, hugging the left edge and dropping down to loot a Colour of Lumina. The big enemy here is indeed identical to the very first boss we faced back in Act I, and it even has the same moveset. Defeat it with Monoco in the party to obtain [Monoco Skill - Évéque Spear]. There is another Colour of Lumina at the back of this area, where you fought the boss. Follow this path around the area until you see a stationary enemy ahead with two swords.

Defeat this enemy to obtain [Monoco Skill - Clair Enfeeble]. Carry on, down the path behind where the enemy was and climb the short ledge for another black and white scene. The path onwards is to the left and will transition to be like the "Flying Waters" area. Hug the left wall and defeat the large enemy ahead for a whopping three Monoco skills - [Monoco Skill - Bruler Bash], [Monoco Skill - Démineur Thunder] and [Monoco Skill - Cruler Barrier]. Keep hugging the left wall and you will reach a merchant.

Defeat the merchant to unlock access to the "Energising Cleanse" pictos in its inventory. This pictos dispels the first negative status effect received and the character gains 2 AP. Go back through the narrow passage and take the path ahead and to the left. Follow this and eventually you will reach the next flag.
Again, follow the left edge in this area until you reach a path going upwards between some seaweed.

Go to the edge of the platform at the top and grapple down to face a Chromatic boss. This is the chromatic variant of the big Bourgeon enemies you fought a few times near the start of the game. It drops a weapon for Sciel. it's also guarding the "Stay Marked" pictos. I haven't included a moveset section for this boss as it is literally identical to the Bourgeon's you have fought before. With the Bourgeon taken care of, grapple back up and go back down the slope to the main area.

Look around near here for one of the small mine -carrying enemies and fight it. You will obtain [Monoco Skill - Luster Slicer]. Now go past the slope we took to reach the grapples and you will see another one of those enemies with two swords ahead. Defeat this one to obtain [Monoco Skill - Obscur Sword]. Again, follow the path behind where the enemy was until you reach the next flag.

This area is a rehash of the area leading up to the Gestral Village which means our old friends, the Sakapatate's are back. Keep Monoco in your party as we have more skills coming up. Go past the two Gestral statues and loot the Colour of Lumina back here. Now take the path between the statues and defeat the first enemies you come across to gain two Monoco Skills - [Monoco Skill - Sakapatate Estoc] and [Monoco Skill - Sakapatate Slam]. Look to the left as you climb the slope for another Colour of Lumina. Defeat the next group of enemies ahead for yet more Monoco Skills. The Ultimate Sakapatate, like Eveque previously is just the same boss you fought before, so I won't cover mechanics again.

Wining this battle awards [Monoco Skill - Sakapatate Explosion] and [Monoco Skill - Sakapatate Fire]. If you look directly behind the statue in the middle of this area, you can loot 2,130x Chroma. Turn around from the chroma and take the path ahead. Take the left path here and look to the right to see the next double sword enemy, indicating the way forward. Defeat this one and proceed until you reach the next flag.

Take the stairs up and look near the edge at the top for a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Look to the left and above you to grapple upwards and loot 4,260x Chroma ahead. Keep following the path until you see some enemies ahead. Look to the right of these to see another group of enemies. Defeat these and loot another 2,130x Chroma. Now defeat the other set of enemies and look to your right to see a windmill with a petank nearby. As usual, I don't bother with the petank but there is a Colour of Lumina behind the left side of the windmill.

Continue to follow the main path now and loot 4,260x Chroma ahead. To the left there is a rope, at the bottom of which is a Mime, accompanied by two of the double sword enemies you've been fighting throughout this area. The Mime drops a haircut for Maelle. The fight is no different to how you normally deal with mimes and you should be well used to their attacks by now. Defeat the two normal enemies and then focus on the mime.

Take the right path now from where you looted the Chroma and again, make sure Monoco is in your party if you took him out as the next group of enemies drops [Monoco Skill - Hexga Crush]. With the enemies defeated, look behind the stone pillar to the right of where they were for the "Weakness Gain" pictos. Now take the path through the wreckage out of here and follow the grapples to the next flag.

Head up the ramp past the flag and drop off to the right at the top to loot a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Defeat the first enemies here for the only Monoco Skill in this part of the area - [Monoco Skill - Troubadour Trumpet]. Drop down off this ledge and head to the left where you will see a rope ahead. Loot the 2,130x Chroma and then drop off down below. Follow the path to the left here to encounter your next double sword enemy.

After the battle move on and look to your left. At the top of a slope that leads back the way you came is a Colour of Lumina. Now take the path ahead and to the left. You will reach a gravestone. Turn left from this and enter the door here to go to the Manor. Look to the left straight away here and loot the purple item to obtain [Record #13/34 - L'amour D'une Mere]. Search the right side of the room for [Journal #28/49 - Aline]. Leave the manor by going down the stairs at the back of this room and returning to the front doors.

Back where the grave is, take the other path this time and use the grapples to reach the next flag. Head through the arch and keep going straight until the colour returns. Put Monoco back in your party if you swapped him out and fight the enemies on the right side here to obtain [Monoco Skill - Danseuse Waltz]. Look at the edge here for 4,260x Chroma. You can fight the big enemy down the other path if you want, though he only drops some Resplendent Chroma Catalysts. There is also a paint cage behind him that has the "Empowering Parry" pictos. There is a merchant up the wall to the bosses right that I don't think you can reach without defeating him. However, if you head up the main slope in this area and turn around at the top, you can take the path on the right down to him. The WT assumes you fight the boss and approach the merchant from here.
Punches: The boss punches fast 3 times. After the first hit, the other two come almost instantly.
steps.heading: Gargant - Attacks

steps.text: Empowered Punches: Same as above, except there are now 6 punches. The last few are delayed.
Freeze: The boss freezes a character. This has a similar animation to Francois, the turtle boss. Wait till just as the 3rd pulse goes out, then parry.
Yell: The boss fires one projectile at a character. There is a good windup.
Arm Swing: 4 hits that go for the whole party.

The boss will switch stances between fire and ice so be careful what attacks you use. After the boss uses snowstorm, the empowered punches attack will happen. If freeze connects with a character you won't be able to use them again until they take damage and the effect breaks.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: After you've beaten the boss, look opposite the flaming tree and go to this edge to find a grapple. Right in front of you here on the right wall is Lock #1. Move ahead to the cage and then go to the right, all the way to the edge of this platform. Turn around again and look left to find Lock #2 in the image below.
Now look above the cage itself to see Lock #3.

Loot the pictos and grapple back across. Climb the wall opposite you to find a merchant. Defeating him unlocks access to two items this time, the "Greater Defenceless" pictos which adds 15% to defenceless damage amplification and a weapon for Sciel. He also sells a Healing Tint Shard. Continue up the hill here to see your favourite new enemy is waiting just ahead. Win this battle for another [Monoco skill - Braseleur Smash]. Enter the tunnel here and continue straight, grappling across the gap at the end. Talk to the boy here to take the train to the final part of this long area.

Rest at the flag and then fight the first enemies ahead for [Monoco Skill - Chevaliére Ice]. This is the last Monoco Skill in this entire area now so you are safe to put your party back to something else for the rest of this act if you wish. Go left around this area. The second left will have a Recoat tucked away. Take the main path ahead now, crossing over the grapple points. At the top, take the left path and the middle one. Note that there are the usual Lumina items and stuff scattered around here but I find the enemies here tiresome to deal with so apart from stuff that is in front of us or things like journals, I skip in this part.

Taking the middle path, go all the way to the end here and then look to the right. Take the path here, loot the Colour of Lumina and then grapple across twice. Defeat the enemies here and then loot [Journal #29/49 - Expedition 70] as well as the Colour of Lumina behind it. Now return back across the grapples and take the path ahead to see two of your sword-wielding friends. Defeat them and then proceed forward to the flag. Check Lumina and skills as there is a big fight ahead. When you're ready, head past the flag for a cutscene which ends in a boss fight.

Vanish - The boss will attempt to vanish a character, removing them from the fight permanently. This is a 2 hit combo. The first hit is parried as the boss jumps and the second hit needs a gradient counter.
steps.heading: ??? - Phase 1 - Attacks

steps.text: Chroma Pool - A simple jump counterattack
Chroma Wave - This is the same as the Old Lumiére version. Parry each time the attack "bursts".
Melee Combo - A 6 hit melee combo. The first 3 hits are fast and the last 3 have a small delay that is easily telegraphed.
Large Chroma - 3 hit combo. 2 normal parries then a gradient
Ranged Attack - 4 hit combo, quite delayed

Tail Attack - This requires a gradient counter and will probably either outright wipe your party out or do serious dmg if it hits. I found this one hard to counter also. Don't wait too long trying to bait it out.
steps.heading: Phase 2 - Attacks

steps.text: Launch Attack - The creature will do a normal hit very quickly and then propel itself into you for a jump counter. The first hit is again, quite hard to see but it is right at the start of the attack.
Roar Attack - A 3 hit combo that is quite to parry. The creature will stand on its hind legs and shoot 3 times. As the creature begins to come down each time is when to parry.
Claw Attack - Another quite easy one. The creature will attack 3 times with its claws. As with the roar attack this can be timed as it begins to swipe down.

This is the big one. The boss retains some of the moves you saw back in Old Lumiére and gains some new ones. This is a 2 phase fight, with the 2nd phase starting when you get the boss to around half health. If the boss manages to banish a character, it may be worth just restarting the fight if you are near the beginning as you won't get them back. The fight gets very chaotic in phase 2 when the boss becomes enraged as he will attack twice.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Back in control after the cutscene, proceed forward and you will enter a new area with another flag ahead. Not rest for the wicked I'm afraid, rest up, check lumina's and prepare yourself for another, arguably harder boss fight. MISSABLE This is the last Act II flag. This is your LAST chance to get the missable record by watching the optional scene at camp. Do not go to the next boss unless you have this. When ready, head to the top of the slope to start another cutscene, ending in your next boss. Absolutely make sure you have a character that can break shields.
Void Meteors - The boss summons 7 spikes that will pulse and fire one at a time.
steps.heading: ??? - Phase 1 - Attacks

steps.text: Gradient Attack - This is just a 1 hit gradient that requires a gradient counter. The timing seems quite lenient on this one.

Chroma Waves - Similar to the previous bosses chroma attack, this is two back to back quick hits then two slower ones. It doesn't have the identifiable pulse that the other version did but it's still quite easy to get the hang of.
Chroma Orb - 5 hit combo. It pulses and must be parried for each
Rock Throw - The boss throws three spiked rocks from the monolith.
Brush of Light - Easy 3 hit combo. It has a slow windup but is very obvious when to parry.
steps.heading: Phase 2 - Attacks

steps.text: Swipe attack - 5 hit combo. The boss will soar into the air and swipe left to right and back a couple of times before launching more attacks. Again, this is quite easily telegraphed but there are big delays between each. Make sure to count the hits out so you know you are done.

Reality Tear - This is a very flashy move but it's not hard to counter. After the wall has been ripped open, 5 bolts of light will shoot out, one at a time. Just parry before they hit you. They are quite slow moving, it's just easy to be struck in awe at the move itself and miss them.

Unleash - A whopping 8 hit combo. The boss will approach a character and "set up" by twirling her paintbrush a few times. The first 3 attacks are back to back, followed by a pause before 4+5. Hits 6 and 7 are both quite slow. The final 8th hit will hit the whole party.

Ranged Attack - The boss will "attack from afar". This is a jump counter followed by 3 more bolts fired at you that need to be parried. It's easily telegraphed again, just don't drop your guard after the first jump counter.

Curse - At 50% health, the boss will curse all characters so they die in two turns and will gain 9 shields. There will also be two orbs near the boss. Destroying these in free aim will give your character another turn to live per orb hit and will remove a shield from the boss. The orbs will respawn every few turns so you can keep your characters going a little longer. If a character dies from the curse, they can be revived but will again have two turns to live.

You will unlock the below achievement for defeating the boss and then will watch a number of cutscenes. When back in control in the Manor, make your way to the room with the canvases in and interact with the person here. Go through the dialogue and there will be some more cutscenes after which you will finally end up in Lumiére. This signifies the start of Act III and will continue on the next page.
Lumiére
steps.heading: Act III

steps.text: Take the only path you can take until you find the curator and start another cutscene, unlocking the below achievement:

After more cutscenes you will be back at camp. You will need to speak to each party member here. There is no relationship building in this version of the camp, it is just for story purposes. Once you have spoken to everyone, go to the campfire and choose to check up on the others, followed by starting the greatest expedition in history. There will be another cutscene, after which you will find yourself on the world map with Esquie, a "final objective" and the ability to fly.
steps.heading: Camp

steps.text: Before we continue with anything, a note about the plan now. You're basically now free to do whatever you want. You can continue with the story and finish it by returning to Lumiére, or you can do as much or as little of the postgame as you want. Personally, I recommend just finishing the story so that it isn't too easy. Some people recommend finishing relationships first but I found some of them very difficult at this point and they don't affect the outcome of the game. Bear in mind, that if you do chase relationships yourself, you will eventually be given a choice when speaking to Maelle (spoilers for it below). You MUST choose to tell Maelle the TRUTH. If you don't, your relationship level won't go up and you will miss the achievement on this playthrough.
I will point out in the when I do this part but if you go exploring on your own and pop it early, do bear this in mind. The specifics are below.

When speaking to Maelle after completing the Reacher side-area and fighting Alicia, there will be a cutscene at camp where she asks Verso if he could have saved Gustave. You MUST tell the truth here to advance the relationship and unlock the achievement. If you lie, the relationship will not go up.

Press to go back to Camp again. Now make sure to equip the "Painted Power" pictos on one of the characters you use. This allows you to damage above 9,999. After the usual four battles, you can equip this to everyone, and should do. Now sort out any attribute points, tints and Lumina points by speaking to Maelle, and then go to Esquie. Some of the relationships require you going to areas and fighting bosses to continue them, but not Esquie or Sciel.

Speak to Esquie. You get nothing for reaching level 5. Speaking to him again will eventually put you in a battle with Francois. This is the same fight as when you fought him back in Act I, just with only Verso this time and will unlock the ability to swim underwater when defeated. Keep speaking to Esquie until you reach level 7, maxing out the relationship and unlocking the below two achievements, as well as Verso's final gradient attack:

Now speak to Sciel twice. Reaching level 6 will unlock [Record #14/34 - Sciel], as well as outfits for Verso and Sciel. Reaching level 7 will unlock Sciel's final gradient attack as well as the below achievement for maxing the relationship:

That's all we're going to do with relationships for now as Lune, Maelle and Monoco's require going to other areas and fighting some bosses. Just remember, if you choose to go after Maelle's relationship now, you MUST tell the truth when prompted. With those two relationships out of the way, we are ready to go back to Lumiére. Rest at the campfire and, when back on the Continent, mount Esquie then take off with . Look at the map and fly to Lumiére for a cutscene, after which you will be on the docks.

Put Monoco in your party if you don't already have him and proceed ahead. Head forward to the stairs and look to the right of and behind the flag for a Colour of Lumina. Proceed up the stairs and fight the enemy at the top and on the left to obtain [Monoco Skill - Aberration Light]. You can now swap Monoco back out if you wish as there are no more skills for a while. Turn around and face the stairs. Look to the right for a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Now follow this wall round to the right for another Colour of Lumina.
steps.heading: Lumiére

steps.text: Head to the stalls ahead and stay to the left side, going straight and looting 2,450x Chroma near a bin at the end. Cross over to the other side from where we are to find another bin opposite this one. Interact with it for some short dialogue and a Perfect Chroma Catalyst. Now continue onwards and climb the rope. Turn right at the top and follow this path all the way you can until you end up in the exact spot where the game started. Loot the "Energising Powerful" pictos and take the path back until you reach the flag. Note that you can now upgrade weapons, tints and Lumina points from the flag also, nice!

The "Challenges" section is just modifiers. I found no use for them personally but if you do find yourself too over-leveled, either for the story here or for other areas, the enemy life multiplier is useful. You can also unequip the Painted Power pictos if you want to cap your damage. After resting, head forward and take the rope down to the large circular area. On landing, look to the right to see a purple item pickup. Defeat the enemies ahead and then go to the item for a Colour of Lumina. That last set of enemies was the 4th battle for me and this unlocked Painted Power for everyone. Make sure you equip this on every character, including the ones you don't have in your party!

From the item, continue around to the next group of three enemies, ignoring the path to the right for now. After defeating them, you should see another purple item ahead and to the left, near the edge of the statue in the middle of the area. Loot this for a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Now take the path that we skipped, with the two enemies at the end. Defeat them and then look to the right as you move ahead. There is another purple item down a path to the right that is another Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Take the main path ahead until you reach the boy. Look to the middle of the area, where the tree is and loot the "Charging Stun" pictos from its base.

Orient yourself so the flag is ahead of you, then look left for another purple item. This is yet another Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Return to the flag and rest up, the continue down the path ahead and take the left path at the split. Look to the left ahead for 2,450x Chroma next to some rubble. Follow the path to an enemy, then move down the short stairs and loot a Colour of Lumina. Take the left path here and follow it out to a more open area with a big enemy ahead. This is a chromatic boss and cannot be skipped as far as I know. Move down the short stairs and look to your left to see a lone enemy guarding a purple item. Win the battle and then loot the Colour of Lumina it was guarding.
Head to the stairs leading down to the boss but instead go left and loot another Colour of Lumina. Put Monoco back in your party as this boss drops a skill and then begin the battle.
Jump Attack - This is a jump counter followed immediately by a gradient counter.
steps.heading: Chromatic Echassier - Attacks

steps.text: Blight Absorb - The boss absorbs all blight stacks, including those on dead characters, healing relative to the amount of stacks.
2 Hit Combo - A drawn-out, 2-hit combo. Be patient and wait until the attack is about to connect before parrying.

Long Combo - The popup will just say the boss attacks, but this is a long, 7-hit combo in an effort to apply blight. The attacks come quick and are well telegraphed. Dodge/parry as much as you can to avoid stacks.

This boss is all about the blight. If you take too many blight stacks not only will your characters health be reduced by an absurd amount, but the boss will heal based off of how many stacks you have. The boss's abilities are all well telegraphed, you just have to be careful not to take too many hits, thus stacking up the blight. For the longer combos, it can be better just to dodge if not confident. For the jump attack, the gradient counter is literally straight away, do not wait with it like other gradients. There is also an opportunity for a quick achievement here. Unequip Painted Power from your characters and keep using abilities until you reach 3 gradient charges.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Without painted power, the boss will not fall over quick and as the attacks are all fairly easy to avoid, this is a good place to get it done. Bear in mind that not all characters will actually have a level 3 gradient ability as this point though. Once at 3 charges, use a level 3 gradient attack on the boss to unlock:

With the achievement unlocked, you can press and then reload the latest save to restart the battle. If you don't get it here, worry not. In the post-game, you can do this on most enemies by just taking off painted power and wailing on them until you get the three charges. This is just a good time as the boss is in the way anyway and its attack pattern is simple.

You will obtain [Monoco Skill - Échassier Stabs] for defeating the boss. Look to the left ahead and loot a Colour of Lumina, then grapple across the platforms. Look left after the ramp uphill and loot another Colour of Lumina from near the boat. Approach the Opera House but don't enter yet. You can loot 2,450x Chroma from the left side at the bottom of the stairs. Take the stairs up and then turn right. Take the path all the way to the end here and interact when prompted, then ask Esquie to bring the item to the surface for [Journal #30/49 - Expedition 60]. Enter the Opera House and take the stairs to the right, where you can loot yet another Colour of Lumina from the top.

Now take the main path through into the Opera Hall and to the left of the piano is a flag to rest at. Look to the right ahead and loot [Record #15/34 - Lumiére]. Note that this is a duplicate of the one that the Mime dropped in the prologue. It still counts as one of the 34 but it is the same, hence being able to miss 1 of the 2 missable records. Continue on to find yourself outside again. Grapple across twice and you will eventually reach some enemies.

Defeat them and then move ahead and look left. There is a purple item here that can be looted for a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. From the item, look right and you will see a group of enemies ahead to the left. Ignore these for now and instead head straight across to find another group. Defeat these and loot the "Healing Stun" pictos they were guarding. Continue on and defeat another two enemies ahead, then loot the Colour of Lumina.

Carry on and take the right path, down the sloped roof and grapple across the gap. As you land, you should see the item to your left. Loot it for a Colour of Lumina and then proceed ahead, past the boy. Continue down the slope and grapple across at the end, heading left first for another Resplendent Chroma Catalyst. Take the other path and look to the left, near some boxes for 2,450x Chroma. Speak to the merchant here and fight him to unlock access to the "Full Strength" pictos which gives 25% increased damage whilst at full health.

When finished with the merchant, continue on to the next flag. There are some items in the area ahead but it's mostly the usual fare. If you want to explore, you can, it's not a very large area. Take the main path through the gardens towards the tower in the background. The large enemy ahead is a boss and also has a Monoco skill. I did not use Monoco at this point as he was under-leveled for me and this boss can be a pain. The boss respawns at the flag if you rest after killing it so it's up to you whether you kill it now with Monoco or later. This enemy also appears in the post-game area where we collect most of the Monoco skills so you can wait until then also if you wish.

Kick - This attack is really hard to see. It targets one character, the boss turns around and then kicks them, like a horse. After enough tries I ended up doing this off feel alone but it can be frustrating to start with. As soon as the boss has turned, it's about to kick so be ready to dodge/parry and hope.
steps.heading: Creation - Attacks

steps.text: Melee Combo - This is a 5 hit combo that is quite slow. As with the kick attack, because of the way the boss is designed, it can be hard to tell what part of it is actually attacking you.
Tail Swipe - A slow, 3 hit combo where the boss hits the party with its tail. It alternates which way it spins and there is quite a delay between each.

Void Orbs - The boss will "rise up into the air" and gain 6 shields plus 4 void orbs. DO NOT free aim these orbs, you take damage from hitting them. The orbs will pulse and explode every turn. This is your standard parry as it pulses type attack. The orb will pulse once, parry just as it goes off.
Energy Attack - I'm unsure why this attack is called what it is as this just feels like another melee combo. The boss will swing round a bit and each time its head is about to hit you, parry.
Flying Combo - This is a 6 hit attack that looks similar to the melee combo, combined with the tail swipe. The 3rd hit will be a jump counter and the final one will require a gradient counter.

This is one of the few bosses in the game that I just did not enjoy, mostly as it's hard to tell when the boss will hit you due to its bulky design. The boss starts accompanied by two of the enemies you've no doubt seen a lot in this area. Focus them one at a time with your strongest attacks to get them out of the way. There are several aspects of this fight that are annoying. The main boss will apply inverted to all party members so you can't heal, and all of the enemies have attacks which apply blight. Removing them from the fight fast gives you some breathing room. The boss itself is just very chunky and the inverted status makes things difficult. Note that if a character dies and is revived, they will still have inverted BUT will be at full health or close to it from the revive tint.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: With the boss defeated, only one enemy remains. Head forward, up the steps and rest at the flag. Make sure you have everything equipped that you need and then move forward for a cutscene, after which, the final battle begins.
Black Hole - Very simple. There is a distinct sound cue for this as the hole expands. When you hear the cue, parry.
steps.heading: ??? - Phase 1 - 100% - 50% - Attacks

steps.text: Void Cross - The boss will "slice" a cross pattern. The camera will zoom out and then surge inward. You want to parry just before the camera zooms back in.

2 Hit Combo - The screen will say "??? Attacks". This is a very simple jump counter coupled with a very difficult normal attack. After you jump, the boss will bring the paintbrush down past his head. This is when you want to parry. It is tricky to time.
5 Hit Combo - A well telegraphed attack. There is a long wind-up before the first hit, followed by some quick hits in succession and then a long delay before the final one.
Visages - Shields the boss. This doesn't really affect you as it is assumed at this point you can easily remove shields.
steps.heading: ??? - Phase 1 - Sub 50% - Attacks

steps.text: Reacher - Buffs the boss with Powerful or Rush.
Hauler - Throws a chunk of building at you. As the rubble starts heading towards you, parry just before it connect. It is fast.
Sirene - Once the bosses health bar is empty, Siréne will heal the boss to full and the second phase will start.
Dessendre Canvas - At the start of Phase 2, the boss will summon the Dessendre Family Canvas and enter it. When he returns, he will be buffed with Powerful, Shell and Rush.
steps.heading: ??? - Phase 2 - Attacks

steps.text: Frenetic Attack - A very fast 8 hit combo that ends with a gradient counter
Swift Attack - Another quick multi hit attack. As with the Frenetic attack, it's easy to tell what is happening although the boss does delay some hits.
Void Meteors - The boss summons 5 meteors that will attack the party one at a time. Similar to the Paintress void spikes, parry just before they hit.

There are two phases, with the second phase beginning once the boss's health is depleted so try and save your tints, etc. for that phase. In Phase 1, the boss will summon the axons at around 50% health, hence splitting the attacks above. Most of them just buff him but the hauler can decimate you if the rubble hits. Phase 2's combo attacks are very fast and heavy hitting so try and play defensively. There is no shame in dodging instead of parrying, particularly as some of the delayed attacks are hard to time. You will get faster at phase 1 whilst learning phase 2 and it is entirely possible to skip most of the axons' abilities if you damage the boss to 0 fast enough.
steps.heading: Additional Info

steps.text: During the cutscenes you will unlock the below achievement for reaching the end, although you're not quite done yet:

When the cutscenes finish, you have limited control. Speak to the NPC ahead and eventually you will be given a choice. There are no achievements affected by this, so choose what feels right for you. This is followed by a short battle and some more cutscenes, tying up the story. You can "lose" this battle but there is no penalty other than just restarting it. I didn't feel it was necessary to run through all of the abilities here as even on the hardest difficulty, the battles felt quite manageable at this point. With the main story finished, only the post-game remains and we have rather a lot to do. I've split the post-game into two separate pages purely as there is a lot of content and it felt tidier than having it all on one page.

sections.title: 9. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Post Game - Part 1

steps.text: Following the climax of the story, you will return to the main menu. Reload your last save and you will be back where we fought the Creation boss in Lumiére. With the story done we still have a lot of things left to do, such as Gestral games, relationships, collectibles and end-game bosses. As a disclaimer, I wrote the WT on my first playthrough of the postgame. Due to this, there is some back and forth traveling, especially with collectibles. There are undoubtedly routes through the postgame that are more efficient than this. However, it didn't overly bother me at the time as with Esquie flying it doesn't exactly take ages. I just wanted to acknowledge this now so readers are aware. For completing the game, you will also automatically have received [Record #16/34 - Our Drafts Collide].
steps.heading: Postgame - Part I

steps.text: As an additional note, the final super-boss in the game will require every party member to be suitably leveled. This means every single one. Not just the ones you play with mainly. They don't have to be level capped, but they do have to be suitably ready. You may want to swap around your characters a bit more than previously. Alternatively, you can wait until right at the end and then go back and just grind out levels for the characters you lack. It's entirely up to you but I wanted to mention it now so it is in your head. The mechanics of the boss mean that everyone will have to play.

In terms of post-game stuff, the first thing I chose to do was get the Gestral Games out of the way. We have already done the parkour, the climb and the race games so all that remains are two more. I didn't particularly enjoy these and just wanted them done. Go to the location on the map below:
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: This Gestral Beach is home to the volleyball minigame. Speak to the Gestral here. There are three levels to complete but for the achievement you only need to do the first two. You can try the third if you wish but I felt that it wasn't worth the trouble personally as this minigame felt janky at best and downright horrible at worst. The aim of the game is to punt back the gestrals that the enemy on the raft opposite throws at you, thus breaking his raft.

You want to hit as they cross over to your side, at the peak of their journey over. It will not work if you leave it till just before they hit, you need to punt them back way earlier than you might think. If you miss one, chances are you miss the next also because of the cooldown on the ability. The easy version gives the opponent the same amount of hit points on their raft as you and there is a short space of time between each gestral thrown. The medium version needed for the achievement gives the enemy more hitpoints than you and the gestrals come in pretty much back to back.

There isn't too much help I can give here other than to say you can always come back later if it annoys you too much. For beating the easy and normal versions of the minigame you will unlock a Resplendent Chroma Catalyst and an outfit for Lune. If you really want to try the hard version, all you get for it is an outfit for Sciel. Personally, I don't think it's worth the frustration but if you go for it, good luck!
With that game won, we only have one left [Gestral Game #4/5]. Return to the Continent and head to the location below for the final Gestral Beach:

On entering this beach area, look to the right and loot [Journal #31/49 - Expedition 37] from next to the torch ahead. Now approach the giant climbing wall. I found this game no less frustrating than most of the others but your mileage may vary. There are three "lanes" with fireballs shooting down them. The aim is to climb to the top of the wall whilst swapping between lanes to avoid being hit. Being hit sends you back to the start. The best advice for this one is to take your time, especially near the top. Wait until you see which lanes are unsafe next and climb accordingly. One important note is that you can only climb onto the top from the middle lane.

The first time I got to the top, I was in the right lane and didn't understand why I couldn't get up. I promptly got knocked back to the start and was not impressed. The patterns on the wall can be free at points, essentially allowing you to climb a good chunk up the wall without having to move. Just keep a look out, especially nearer the top. Once you reach the top you will unlock an outfit for Maelle and, if you've completed all the other games you will unlock the below achievement [Gestral Game #5/5]:

steps.name: Gestral Games
steps.description: Win all of the Gestral games.

steps.text: The next thing on the list for me was locating the remaining Lost Gestrals as they are all available on the world map and it gets another achievement ticked off. We should have 4/9 already. Head to the location below for [Lost Gestral #5/9].
For [Lost Gestral #6/9], head to the location below:
For [Lost Gestral #7/9], head to the location below. This one is very high up in the air, on a platform in the clouds:
For [Lost Gestral #8/9], head to the location below. There are enemies here but you can speak to the Gestral whilst mounted on Esquie:
Finally, for [Lost Gestral #9/9], head to this location:
For rescuing all 9 Lost Gestrals, you will unlock the below achievement:

steps.name: Lost Gestrals
steps.description: Find all of the Lost Gestrals.

steps.text: Now go to Camp and speak to Sastro by taking the path to the right of Esquie and then the first left. You will have to spam through the dialogue a bit as we are getting all rewards at once. Among other things, you will get the "Paint Break" skill which allows you to press and break the blue paint spikes. You've probably seen them throughout your travels. Most of the time they contain a bit of chroma or the odd Colour of Lumina so I didn't rush to get this unlocked. You can break the one next to Sastro here for another Colour of Lumina.

With the Gestral related achievements done, it's time to finish off our relationships, starting with Maelle. Spend time with her at camp whilst we are here to learn that she wants to see Alicia. Head to the location below and enter "The Reacher".

Go forward upon entering the area to start a cutscene just before you reach the flag. After the cutscene, do anything you need to at the flag and then head forward and grapple over the gap, followed by taking the rope up. You can break the blue paint spike ahead now that you have the ability and take the rope up behind it to a Colour of Lumina.
steps.heading: The Reacher

steps.text: Continue on the main path ahead to find the first enemies for this area. Put Monoco in your party to obtain [Monoco Skill - Orphelin Cheers]. After fighting the second group, ignore the grapple you see on the left for the moment and continue following the ramp down. Loot the Colour of Lumina from the crate here and then return to the grapple, crossing over two of them to reach the next area. Continue on, looking to the right as you move until you see a white item. Loot this for 3,128x Chroma. Climb down the rope ahead or drop down and turn around.

There are two paths here. Take the right one first, where the enemies are. Defeat them and loot the "Draining Cleanse" pictos. Now take the short left path to loot 6,255x Chroma. With both paths looted, continue on the main path forward. You will eventually reach a hot air balloon. Before taking it, turn around so it's behind you and you will see a purple item ahead, take it for a Colour of Lumina. Now step onto the hot air balloon platform and interact with it to reach the next section.

There is a flag ahead to rest at if needed, after which you should grapple across the gap ahead. The enemies ahead are the normal versions of the chromatic boss you fought in Lumiére. Defeat them and then take the slope upward and turn right at the top. You will see a blue item and a rope ahead. Take the right path before the rope here and loot 3,128x Chroma from some boxes. Return to the rope. Jump across the wooden boards to loot the "Longer Shell" pictos. Either jump back across or drop down and take the rope back up.

Now continue taking the slope up and follow the path to another hot air balloon. Before taking it, look left under the scaffolds to see some handholds. Take these up and then grapple across at the end. Follow the wall here around to the right, climbing the ledge and following it again to loot 6,255x Chroma. Now take the only path you can until see the Fading Man. Take the grapple to the right of the man, followed by another at the bottom of the ramp. Defeat the enemies ahead and then loot the "Charging Counter" pictos.

Head back the way you come and look right for an opening that you can crawl through. On the other side, look left and drop down to the platform. Loot the "Charging Attack" pictos and then make your way back to the hot air balloon, again taking it to the next section. There is another flag ahead. Rest as needed and then take the ramp down. There are a few separate paths here. First, head to the right and loot the Colour of Lumina hidden back here.

Then take the rope that was to the left at the bottom of the ramp to find a Mime. It's been a while since we last fought this enemy but the moveset is exactly the same. You will receive a haircut and outfit for Maelle. Loot the Colour of Lumina to the left of where the Mime was and then take the rope back up. Now take the only remaining path, opposite the ramp we came down originally. Follow this path over several grapples and eventually you will reach a cutscene. When back in control, loot 3,128x Chroma to the left of the new balloon and then take it to the next area.

Rest at the flag if needed and then take the path forward. You will soon reach solid ground again. Turn around here and take the path back the way you came for the "Protecting Tint" pictos. In this foggy area, head to the left and the path will split. Keep to the left and follow this path downhill, eventually taking a left again. Head forward now until you see a rope ahead and loot the Colour of Lumina to the left of it. Take the rope down to find a merchant. Defeat him to unlock access to a weapon for Verso. Note that he also sells the "Anti-Blight" pictos which you should definitely pick up as it makes enemies in this area and others much easier.

Now take the hot air balloon to the right of the merchant. Defeat the enemies ahead and then loot the 3,128x Chroma they were guarding. Turn left and grapple across, then grapple again and take the rope down. Loot the "Healing Boon" pictos from the dead enemy here and then drop down. Immediately on your right as you land, is a door to the Manor. Enter and loot [Journal #32/49 - Unknown]. Leave the manor and look to your left. Take the ramp going up and then take the saw acting as a ramp to go up again. Take the third ramp ahead and continue straight on here to arrive back at a flag. Fast travel to the "Foggy Area".

Make your way back to the area with the hill and where the path splits. Take the right path this time, running past the enemies if you can as the big guy is a pain to fight. If you do end up fighting him, every attack he does that hits you will give you blight stacks. If you use free aim and hit his lantern, you will remove ALL blight from the character using aim. As far as I can tell there is no way to avoid the blight wave attack so you either want to have the anti-blight pictos from the merchant we just visited OR destroy the lantern periodically to remove blight from some of your characters.

Whether you defeat the enemy or not, carry on down this path and look to the right to see another rope. Opposite the rope is 3,128x Chroma. Take two ropes up and at the top loot a Colour of Lumina directly ahead. Go back past the rope and grapple across and loot another 6,255x Chroma from the end of the path ahead. We are now back at the top of the hill in this area. Look around as there may be another of the big enemies patrolling. Provided the coast is clear, drop off this ledge and go left until you spot another hot air balloon. You should see [Journal #33/49 - Expedition 61] just to the left of it. Now take the balloon to the next section, we're nearly there now.

Rest at the new flag and then take the grapple ahead. Turn left at the top, essentially turning back on yourself and loot 3,128x Chroma. You can take more grapples here to land on a platform with a Chromatic boss.
Jump Combo - This is a simple jump counter followed by a very telegraphed smash from above.
steps.heading: Chromatic Braseleur - Attacks

steps.text: Hammer Combo - This is a multi-hit combo but again, is easily telegraphed
Fire Orbs - The orbs will intermittently shoot at a random party member. Parry when they pulse for an easy counter.

Don't ever bother destroying the orbs as the boss will resummon them. The shooting orbs give you plenty of opportunities for counter damage. The only threatening ability is the hammer combo just because it has so many hits. It's totally fine to just dodge this over parrying if not confident, the orbs will give you lots of chances for parries anyway. The boss will heal if you use fire attacks so any Maelle enjoyers may want to swap her out or just focus on using non-fire based attacks. If you successfully parry the orbs, they will continually fire so it is possible to defeat the boss without it ever attacking other than the opening moves. My Maelle was doing nearly 200k per counter and the boss kept targeting her with the orbs so I killed him in about 6 turns. This is the way to go.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Grapple back across the platforms and continue on the main path to reach another flag. Rest and check pictos for Maelle as the following battle will be a 1v1 where you will have to play as her no matter what. When ready, head forwards for a cutscene followed by a boss battle.
I did not list the attacks for Alicia as they are all multi hit sword combos and it felt moot trying to describe the differences between them.
steps.heading: Alicia - Attacks

steps.text: This fight can be very tough or very easy depending on how much damage you manage to dish out fast. At 75% and 25% health, Alicia will cast "Powerful" then "Rush" on herself but if you are doing enough damage you will not give her time to make much use of this. She gets a lot of moves in a row, especially with "Rush" so you need to try and dish out as much as you can through counters as you will be limited with what you can do on your own turn, especially if you have to heal. For reference, my first counter on Alicia dealt 234k damage and took her down to half health. It's still very possible to beat her just through dodges as this is what I did my first time through, but you are elongating the fight substantially.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Up until 50% health, Alicia will just do Sword Ballet or Virtuoso Strike so you will have a lot of time getting used to those moves first and foremost. Maelle's Medalum weapon is very powerful in general but will start you in Virtuoso Stance so is worth looking into for this fight also. Once Alicia gains "Rush", she will start casting Fleuret Flurry and Phantom Strike also. Fleuret Flurry has a lot of bait moves so don't fall for it. It's the slowest attack she does, wait for each hit. Phantom strike is the most erratic and ends with a gradient counter. Another valid tactic is try and stack burn on her as she will take damage in between turns and with painted power on, this will melt through her health whilst you focus on evading. It all comes down to how comfortable you are with parrying really. Just take it step by step, learning each combo she does.

When back in control after the cutscenes, you can exit this area by walking to Esquie nearby. You will automatically go to camp and dialogue will start with Maelle, after which you will reach relationship rank 6. Now speak to Maelle again and choose to spend time with her. MISSABLE - VERY IMPORTANT. This is the missable Maelle dialogue that has been mentioned for a while. During your time with Maelle, you will get the chance to lie or tell the truth. You MUST tell the TRUTH to advance the relationship. If you choose to lie, the relationship will not advance and you will not be able to get Maelle's relationship maxed on this playthrough. You can still load an earlier save if need be but the game autosaves over itself so don't leave this too late if you choose to see what happens for lying.

Once you have pressed TRUTH, go through the rest of the dialogue to reach relationship level 7 with Maelle. This will unlock her incredibly powerful level 3 gradient attack "Gommage" as well as the below achievement for maxing her relationship:

We just have Lune and Monoco's relationships left now and they both consist of fighting a boss rather than trudging through a giant area like the Reacher. I chose Lune first, so speak to her to learn that she wants to find a record of her parent's expedition. Rest at the fire to return to the continent and then look for Siréne's island on the world map. There will be a red objective marker on the east side. Land here and enter the Siréne's Dress area.

Head forward for a flag and then proceed to the large door. Choose to "look around" and then "play music" to open it. There is another flag ahead. Lune does not have to be in your party for the boss ahead but you may have her there from the recent cutscene so make sure to check and set up. When ready, head forwards and a giant snake will appear. This is a chromatic boss but one you must fight for Lune's quest.
steps.heading: Siréne's Dress

steps.text: Tail Slam - A multi-hit combo where the boss slams its tail down. Easily telegraphed, just parry before each hit.
steps.heading: Chromatic Glissando - Attacks

steps.text: Blind - This looks identical to the tail slam but is just one attack. If it connects, it will affect all characters with "Dizzy" which affects free aim.
Head Smash - A 2 hit combo that is quite delayed where the snake smashes its head into the whole party.
Swallow - The boss swallows a dead party member, healing for around 100k health.

You can Free aim attack the tail to destroy it but the boss will grow it back and I didn't notice anything being "easier" with the tail gone. The swallow move essentially means you can't risk having people die as you won't get them back outside of a stun and the heal is huge. The worst move for me was just the tail slam as it's a big multi-hit combo that does a large amount of damage if multiple hits connect.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: I ended up parrying the first two hits and then dodging the rest and got consistent with this. Outside of this, the boss doesn't have many moves that cause issue. Just be over-cautious with healing if people are low as you likely won't get a chance to use a revive before the boss eats them. Note that towards the end of the fight, the tail combo seems to become longer. I'm unsure what causes this other than just getting boss to a certain point.

Similarly, the head smash becomes a 1 hit move that stuns with a much longer delay. It could be that destroying the tail stops these moves from happening but as the boss grows the tail back I'm not sure when would be best to do it. Be careful sub 50% and assume that the moves will be the enhanced versions. Destroying the tail stops the enhanced attacks but means you're spending AP on free aim over actual attacks so it's kind of up to you how to go. The boss later enrages and attacks twice just for more fun.

When you finally get the boss health to 0, three ballet enemies appear. Do not lose focus now as it sucks big time to fail here and have to start from scratch. Note that you can now revive people without penalty of being eaten if necessary. Focus on one enemy at a time. The enemies will cast blight at you. After the 2nd "pulse", parry it. The window seems quite forgiving. This should one-shot the enemy. Do this three times and all enemies will be dead, ending the fight.

With the fight out of the way, head to the back of this area and across the bridge to finally loot [Journal #34/49 - Expedition 46]. Now leave the area and you will again automatically go to camp, reaching relationship level 6 after the dialogue. You will automatically obtain [Record #17/34 - Lune]. Speak to Lune again and spend time with her. Go through the dialogue and at the end you will unlock her final gradient attack as well as the below achievement for maxing her relationship:

That just leaves Monoco. Spend time with him now and you will get another new objective, to visit the Sacred River. I had to spend time with him twice first as my relationship level was only level 4. Before you rest at camp, check pictos and gear on Monoco and Verso as the next boss fight will be just these two characters. When ready, rest at camp and when back on the Continent, look at the world map for the red marker near the snowy area on the map, south of where we are now.
On landing here there will be a merchant. Buy the record from him for [Record #18/34 - Children of Lumiére]. Now head into the swirling portal.

Head forward the only way you can and interact with the giant crystal Gestral. Following the cutscene, you will be in a boss battle. This fight is also a good chance to get the achievement for using a level 3 gradient attack if you haven't done so yet. The boss has a lot of health, even with Painted Power. Simply use as many AP attacks as you can until you have 3/3 gradient charges. Then use Verso's "Angel Eyes" ability. This will also give you a free revive on Verso if he dies, which is useful in this fight as there are only two of you. Using the level 3 gradient will unlock the below achievement:
steps.heading: Sacred River

steps.text: Impressive Combo - A 4 hit attack. The first 3 hits come in semi-fast, with a slight delay before the 4th.
steps.heading: Golgra - Attacks

steps.text: Dancing Around - An easily predicted attack that requires a gradient counter.
Swift Combo - A 3 hit attack with each hit having a slight delay between it.
Fast Combo - A 3-hit combo where the first two attacks are back to back and there is a short delay before the third.
Anger - At 50% health, Golgra becomes angry, gaining both powerful and rush.
Crazy Combo - Sub 50% only. A 6 hit combo that is pretty fast with minimal delays.
Long Combo - Sub 50% only. A 6 hit combo that is slower, with more delays between attacks.
Earth Shake - An easy jump counter followed by a gradient counter.

The first half of the fight you will want to hope for lots of easy gradient counters and the impressive combo. Post 50%, Golgra gets angry and uses new moves combined with her old ones. In all of my attempts I only saw the crazy combo a couple of times but the long combo constantly. It is good and bad, as not seeing it for a while can throw off your practice but also means you get more practice on other moves. All in all, this felt like a fun fight to me. It can take a few goes for the names of the different combo's to click but it shouldn't give you too much trouble.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Following the cutscene, leave this area to be returned once again to the camp automatically. After some dialogue, you will reach relationship level 6 as well as obtain [Record #19/34 - Monoco]. Spend time with Monoco again now to reach the max relationship level with Monoco. You will unlock Monoco's level 3 gradient attack as well as the below achievement:

With all the relationship levels maxed, I decided to tackle some of the bosses now in order to tick off a couple more achievements. My party was around level 56-58 at this point. Go to the below location and you will find a metallic figure stood in the water. Approach it to engage in battle.
Stage 1 - Strike - A one hit attack where Sprong slams down onto the party. If this connects, it marks them. As the boss health gets lower, this will increase to a 2 hit and then a 3 hit combo.
steps.heading: Sprong - Attacks

steps.text: Stage 2 - Sabotage - Following immediately from stage 1, this attack fires 4 lasers at different party members. This has the usual timing for laser attacks where you look at the pulse. If the lasers hit, they cause various effects such as exhaust. As the boss health lowers, more lasers will be added to this attack.
Stage 3 - Combo - There is a little delay before the first hit, then two hits quickly and a delay before the 4th. As the boss's health goes down, this increases to 5 hits and then 7 hits.
Stage 4 - Extermination - Sprong charges up and doesn't do anything.
Stage 5 - Extermination Beam - Sprong fires the beam. This is a very simple 2 hit laser attack. Every time it pulses, parry.

The boss will cast the above moves in order, sometimes two at a time and then repeat. Assuming you are around my level or possibly higher, this fight will be a breeze with painted power. Given his location on the map, I assume he was probably meant to be fought earlier. Keep an eye on the boss's health and as he gets lower, prepare for there to be more hits to each combo. For stage 1 and 3, the popup will say the hit numbers but stage 2 doesn't so be prepared for more lasers. The extermination beam will always be 2 hits so don't worry about that one.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: You will receive the "Cheater" pictos for defeating Sprong which I'd advise equipping on a character straight away for learning as it allows you play twice in a row. You also unlock the below achievement for defeating the boss:

With the pictos equipped, we are now going to do some collectible gathering. You should have 34/49 journals and 19/34 records. With all of the map open we can go now and grab almost all of the rest both from the overworld and from side areas. Along the way we will naturally increase the party level through fighting enemies which beats grinding it. First go to the location below:
Here you will find [Journal #35/49 - Expedition 47]. Now go to the location below, way back in this Act I area for [Journal #36/49 - Expedition 64].

Now head to the location below and enter the spiral portal here to enter the side area, "The Fountain". Don't worry about it saying "Danger", it just means we are under-leveled for the area but we are only dipping in now for the journal.

On entering, head down the path just to the left past the flag. You will see a creepy Nevron ahead. Ignore it and go down the path to its right. You will quickly find [Journal #37/49 - Expedition 84]. That's it! Return to the Continent.

We will visit a few more side-areas to get quick journals, rather than fully exploring them. You are free to explore these areas as you wish, the majority of them I won't be coming back to. Head to the location below and enter the portal for "The Crows" side area.
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: Look to the left in here to see the flag, and next to it is [Journal #38/49 - Expedition 34]. If interested, you can shoot all the crows in this area with free aim to trigger a boss. The boss is just a chromatic enemy that drops the usual upgrade materials, a weapon for Sciel and the "Shielding Death" pictos which gives other party members 3 shields each when you die. I didn't personally feel it was worth doing but you can decide for yourself.
Back on the Continent, head to the below location:

Loot [Journal #39/49 - Julie] from the tents here and then look to the right. At the back of this area, guarded by enemies is [Journal #40/49 - Verso]. Anti-blight is good here as the enemy group features one of the nasty enemies we fought in the Reacher area. The next journal is a two-step process. First, head to the area below and enter "The Canvas".

Take the only path you can here until find a familiar painting. Interact with it and choose to remove the portrait. We will use this later when we visit the Manor. It's time to head to a side-area now as it has a journal, a record and an entrance to the Manor we can use. Head to the below location and enter the "Falling Leaves" area.

This is a large area but we are just going to beeline for the collectibles and then defeat the boss as it rewards a record. You will be over-leveled for here really but it's still worth fighting enemies to train pictos. Head forwards, under the log and over the bridge. You will see a rope to the right as you approach the flag. After resting, go ahead and turn right, wrapping back around on yourself. Loot the 4,010x Chroma you pass and then take the rope down, followed by another rope. Continue forward into the large cavern and look to the left for a door to the Manor. Ignore the giant figure hanging from the ceiling for now and enter the Manor.
steps.heading: Falling Leaves

steps.text: Loot [Record #20/34 - Alicia] from the desk ahead and then take the door to the right. Make your way to the entrance of the manor but don't leave yet. With the flag behind you, climb the center stairs and then look at the empty picture frame above the right set. Interact with this to use the portrait we obtained earlier. Go through the door that opened at the end of the center passage and loot [Journal #41/49 - Unknown 3] from the middle of the floor here. Now you can leave the manor.

Retrace your steps back to the ropes and take them back up to the level the flag was on. Head straight ahead now, past the flag to the left and grapple across the gap. Follow this path the only way you can, stopping to fight the merchant on the right on the way if you wish. Climb the small ledge past the merchant and then take the next two grapples. Interact with the shortcut at the end of this path and take the rope down. In the clearing ahead, look to the left and loot [Journal #42/49 - Expedition 35]. There is a Chromatic boss battle just beyond the journal if you wish.

Make your way back to the flag at the start of this area, and with it behind you and the rope we took to the right, head forwards until you reach a gate. Speak with the NPC here and then take the ropes back down to the giant thing hanging from the ceiling. Cycle through its dialogue and then speak with the boy again. Take the now open gate behind the boy and follow the path, climbing the handholds to the top. At the top turn left and go straight, taking the path between the rocks to another rope. Loot [Journal #43/49 - Expedition 49] and then take the stairs up.

Rest at the flag and then take the stairs up for a boss. You should be over-leveled for this area so I didn't feel there was a need to include a section for this boss. Even if the boss does get a turn off, and you fail to dodge, the damage will be minimal. Return to the boy by the gate and speak to him for [Record #21/34 - Until Next Life]. We're done here so return to the Continent.

We are getting there with the collectibles now. We have a few more journals and records to obtain and then it's essentially going to be a few side-areas to level up until we are over level 70 and can start tackling the final areas. Head to the area below and enter the side-area entitled "White Tree".
steps.heading: The Continent

steps.text: There is nothing to do here other than to loot [Record #22/34 - Honeymoon in Lumiére] and [Journal #44/49 - Expedition 36]. Return to the Continent and then head to the location below entitled "Crushing Cavern".

This is another short side-area. Head past the flag, through the tunnel and you will eventually fall down. The weird face in front of you is actually a boss. Again, I'm not writing a section for this boss as at this point in the game, I killed it in two moves. You will more than likely not even see it attack. Take the passage behind the boss and climb the rope up. There will be a split in the path. Go left to loot the Colour of Lumina and look left from this to see the journal. Loot [Journal #45/49 - Expedition 45]. Take the right path now and you will eventually drop down back at the entrance. Leave this area and return to the Continent.
Head to the location below entitled "Stone Waves Cliff Cave".

Again, there isn't too much to do here. Take the path down past the flag and as you move down the path, you will see a crystal enemy in the distance. Loot the Colour of Lumina as you go. To the right of this is a crawlspace with a paint cage if you want that gives a Chroma Elixir Shard. Continue down to the enemy. You can loot the journal without fighting it if you wish. Either way, loot [Journal #46/49 - Expedition 54]. You can also loot a pictos from this area if you wish. Fighting the boss will give you the "Energising Revive" pictos and as with the boss in the previous area, you are over-leveled to the point it won't get a turn. When you are done, leave through the swirling portal here to return to the Continent.
Head to the location below entitled "Stone Quarry".

There is a Nevron ahead we will speak to shortly for his quest. Before that though, go behind him and loot [Journal #47/49 - Expedition 48]. Now speak to the Nevron and you will eventually end up in a mini-game of sorts where the Nevron will play music and you must either get hit by the attack or parry. Look at the pattern the Nevron does and then make sure to parry the red notes but let the green ones hit you. There are three rounds of this and it may take some time to get the timing down.

Once all rounds are complete, speak to the Nevron again for a pictos. Go through his dialogue once more to make sure you have seen everything. As always DO NOT ATTACK. This completes [Nevron Quest #5/10]. Return to the Continent. We now only have two journals left. One is locked behind the final super-boss and one is in the area we are going to next. I was around level 60 at this point and the next area we are going to is good for grinding out some levels. Head to the location below entitled "The Carousel".

Head past the flag here, sticking to the left side. Keeping looking left and a short way in, you will see the purple item. Loot it for [Record #23/34 - Le Grand Café de Lumiére]. Now leave and head to the location below to enter the area entitled "Frozen Hearts".

As mentioned, this is a lengthier side area. When this area is done, you will be higher level and we will then clear up most of the records, just like we did with the journals. I will be treating this area like the areas in the story and going into a bit more detail here. It is definitely worth fighting as much as you can for XP, as it just saves time grinding out levels later.
steps.heading: Frozen Hearts

steps.text: Continue forward and up the stairs into a larger area. You will see the flag ahead. Instead of taking the tracks across the bridge, head further right and loot a Colour of Lumina from the broken section. Now cross properly and look immediately left. On the end of a stuck out train carriage is another Colour of Lumina. Now look ahead for the track bending around to the right. As it bends, look ahead and take the path here. There is a giant door embedded in the ice to the right and at its feet, is [Journal #48/49 - Expedition 51]. You should now have all but one journal and you won't get it for a while. If you're behind the current count, you can check what you are missing on the collectible page.

With the journal behind you, head towards the right of this area and hug the train to the left that is elevated. Loot the Colour of Lumina at the end and then drop down to be back where you crossed the bridge. Go to the right, slightly uphill and look to the right, past the building glowing red inside, to find a narrower path. Follow this and take a left at the end into a cave, taking a rope up at the end. There is another flag straight ahead here. Before heading to it, take a left and look left again to spot some stairs. Follow the track left to the end and loot a Colour of Lumina.

You will see some enemies below you. This is [Nevron Quest #6/10]. You are also only allowed to use Lune, a character I had mostly neglected so far. As is hinted at in the dialogue, you can only beat this enemy through parrying. It may take a few goes and feel like it doesn't end, but it does. Keep patient and with enough parries, the battle will be over. Cycle through the dialogue afterwards, again being sure not to attack.
Take the rope back up and return to the stairs. Cross straight ahead and loot another Colour of Lumina. Now head to the flag we skipped.

From the flag, you can see a rope in the distance. Take the left path to it and before going up, look in the left corner to find a Grandiose Chroma Catalyst. Now take the rope up and follow the left edge round for some Chroma. Defeat the enemies ahead and loot some more Chroma from behind them. You are now above where we just were. Follow the ledge to the left and grapple over the gap, before using the handholds to climb.

When the handholds split, take the right path. Grapple over to the train here from the edge of the area and then release a rope from the lower end of the train. Take it down and loot the "Burn Affinity" pictos. Do NOT fall off the train. Turn around and follow it into an open area. The big enemy here is a chromatic version of the lamp/blight enemies you've fought before. It can be skipped if you wish. It drops the usual slew of upgrade materials and the "Energising Burn" pictos that gives 1AP on applying burn. You should be well used to this enemy by now and it is made significantly easier if you equip anti-blight pictos on everyone.

Whether you defeat the enemy or not, look for the door to the Manor in this area. Just behind it you can loot a Grandiose Chroma Catalyst. Enter the Manor and loot [Record #24/34 - Clea Don't Pull Your Sister's Hair]. Leave the manor and you will be back in the large cavern. With the manor door behind you, wrap around to the right and move forward. You will see a white item pickup to your left as you go. Loot this for some Chroma and then defeat the enemies ahead. Follow the path the only way you can and you will be back outside.

The left path ends with a paint cage. The three targets are all nearby and are pretty easy to spot. The first is directly above the cage itself, on the side of the building. The second is on the arm of the crane like structure nearby, and the third is amongst some ice spikes that border the edge of the path you came from. Destroy them all and loot the "Anti-Freeze" pictos, which is very useful for some bosses later. Now take the remaining path and you will eventually find a rope to release. Do so, and take it down. You can drop down to the left here for some Chroma.

Take the other rope here to find yourself back at the start. We now want to get back to the handholds and not take the right path this time. From the top of the rope go straight ahead to the red tinted building and then right down the narrow path. Turn left into the cave, take the rope up and then take the rope up again in the next area to eventually find yourself back at the handholds. Go straight up this time. Make your way into the opening at the top of the area to find a flag. There are other goodies you can grab in this area if you wish, including a paint cage which contains a Revive Tint Shard and a Petank near the piano at the top. Personally, I felt I had enough of these so skipped it and when straight for the top of the area.
Maelle hit level 66 for me here whilst fighting the enemies, unlocking:

You shouldn't be too far off yourself so don't stress if you don't have it. I was aiming for level 70 across the party by the time I was done with this area. From the flag, follow the left edge around to a Colour of Lumina and then climb up the trains opposite the flag and take several grapples until you have a choice of taking one to the left or ahead. Taking the left path leads to a merchant that offers a couple of outfits and that's it. Continue to the right past the merchant and in the back left corner here, amongst some crates, is a Colour of Lumina. Continue to follow this path around and behind some pillars is a Grandiose Chroma Catalyst, as well as a Mime that can be defeated for a haircut for Lune.

Carry on past where the mime was, and in some more crates here is another Grandiose Chroma Catalyst. Now return to the grapple junction and take the grapples all the way to the top. Once at the top, defeat the enemy you see here and then grapple from where it was to reach the next flag. You will see the boss of this area ahead. Whilst you are still likely a little over-leveled for this area, the attacks can still quickly kill party members. This boss is as far as I can tell, pretty identical to the version you fight inside the monolith in Act II so I have not written another section for it here.

With the boss defeated, we are now done with this area and you can return to the Continent through the nearby portal. We are nearing the end now and will focus our attention on the remaining collectibles we can get on the next page.

sections.title: 10. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Post Game - Part 2

steps.text: With all but one journal left, we now repeat the process with records. You should be on 24 records. We will go around the map picking some up and will be left with only one that is in one of the last areas we have to visit. After this, we then go and take out two boss achievements before heading for the final remaining areas. First of all, head to the location below entitled "Boat Graveyard", and enter it for [Record #25/34 - Alicia's Birthday Party].
steps.heading: Postgame Part II

steps.text: Now head to the image below and enter the area entitled "White Sands", looting [Record #26/34 - Aline] from the end of the path.
Head to the image below where you will find a door to the Manor.
Enter the Manor and open the cabinet on the right. Pass through and loot [Record #27/34 - Forlorn] from in here. Exit the Manor and head to the location in the image below to find a merchant.
Buy [Record #28/34 - Lost Voice] from the merchant. Now go to the location in the image below for another merchant, where you can buy [Record #29/34 - Linen and Cotton].
Nearly done! Head to the location below and enter the area entitled "The Meadows". Inside, loot [Record #30/34 - Our Painted Family].
Head to the location below and enter the side area entitled "Blades Graveyard", looting [Record #31/34 - Reverence].

Finally, for the last record we are going to get for now, head to the location below, and enter the "Flying Casino". Take the path the only way you can until you reach the casino. Head round to the right of it and loot [Record #32/34 - Reveries dan Paris].

That wraps up the records for now. The only ones left are in end game areas we have yet to explore. Our list for postgame is narrowing. Assuming you've been following the guide from the beginning, you should have completed 6/10 Nevron quests, so we will finish off the last four now to unlock another achievement. Provided you haven't killed any of the Nevron quest NPCs so far either, the final one will give you a whopping 100 Lumina points. If you have killed any, don't stress! The achievement can still be earned, you just won't get the Lumina points.
Head to the location below and enter the "Esoteric Ruins".

Once inside, head the only way you can, until you see a strange orb in the middle of the area. This is our next Nevron. Speak to it and cycle through the dialogue. Afterwards, climb the handholds beyond to the top, and then take the rope up. Take the sharp right at the top and follow the path down to the bottom. There is a paint cage here also if you wish. At the bottom, you will see a yellow orb ahead. The idea is that you shoot the orbs here to open the path ahead, it's essentially a light maze.
steps.heading: Esoteric Ruins

steps.text: Shoot the orb ahead and enter the room on the left. Turn around and shoot the first orb again, and then shoot the orb you are now stood next to. Head into the room ahead and then into the one on the right here, heading straight through it into another room ahead. Now turn around and shoot the orb in the "middle" room that you just passed by. The way out is now clear. Head through the remaining open doorways and loot the purple item at the end for the "Wood Boards". There is another purple item to the right here that you can loot for a Colour of Lumina. Grapple out of this area, follow the balcony to the left and climb up. Grapple the only way you can and you will end up back by the paint cage.

Head back to the blue orb and speak to it to give it the "Wood Boards". Cycle through the dialogue carefully, being careful not to attack it. This completes [Nevron Quest #7/10]. Return to the continent and head to the next location below, entitled "Floating Cemetery".

This is one is quick and simple. On entering, head to the left and speak to the Nevron. It doesn't matter which weapon you choose here. Head inside the nearby building and win the fight, which should be over very quickly at this level. With the battle done, the Nevron will give you a choice, if you want the Lumina points at the end and haven't killed any Nevrons so far, then choose to spare him. This completes [Nevron Quest #8/10]. Return to the Continent and head to the location below, entitled "Red Woods".
steps.heading: Floating Cemetery

steps.text: This is another quick and easy quest. Run to the bubbling well ahead and interact with it. You will be prompted to donate Chroma. Do this four times for a total of 90,000 total Chroma. Cycle through the extra dialogue at the end, being sure not to attack. This completes [Nevron Quest #9/10]. From here, return to the Continent and fly west to the "Fountain" area that we briefly entered earlier whilst journal hunting. This time speak to the creepy Nevron. Provided you have not killed any of the Nevron Quest NPC's, this Nevron will give you 100 Lumina points, completing [Nevron Quest #10/10] and unlocking:
steps.heading: Red Woods

steps.name: Aiding the Enemy
steps.description: Finish all of the Nevron quests.

steps.text: If you did kill Nevrons, you will have to fight this Nevron instead. Defeating it will unlock the achievement.

Note that now it is kind of up to you what you tackle next and there is merit in going back and forth between different end-game areas to see what you can do. I found myself starting with the Endless Tower below and then, when reaching a harder part, moving over to somewhere else. It is non-linear and entirely up to you. The guide is written in the assumed order most players will go in but if/when you struggle somewhere, it's good to try out another area, gain some more levels and come back. For example, I started the Endless Tower around level 68. I reached roughly halfway through it at around level 75 and just could not get anywhere. I left and went to the Flying Manor, clearing up to the final boss there and then came back.

Note that for most battles from here on out, if you want to "cheese" to a certain extent, you need only live long enough to get 3 gradient charges and then Maelle's "Gommage".
