This will probably kill any enemy left. The "Stendhal" ability found in the top middle row of Maelle's skill tree is also insanely powerful. Personally, I tried to refrain from using these abilities but as you will see below, there are a couple of fights where I felt I had to. Your mileage may vary with this depending on difficulty also. I also put Monoco in my party as you fight a lot of enemies you've seen throughout the game and it's a good way to gain skills. I will highlight what skills I personally got but your own mileage may vary if you haven't been using Monoco more or less than me. The Collectibles page has a full list of all abilities so you can see what you are missing. Head to the giant C on the west side of the map and locate the entrance.

Head forward and rest at the flag in the next area if needed. This area is essentially just battles one after another, with no exploration so I will list what Monoco skills I learnt here but won't include much otherwise as most of this is just enemies you've fought before, including bosses albeit beefed up. Ahead you will see a canvas, with an NPC to its right. Speak to her for some context and then interact with the canvas here. There will only be one option to start with and you will instantly begin a fight. You can rest at the flag after each battle so make sure to do so to upgrade characters as you go. You will get a lot of Grandiose Chroma Catalysts from this area. The spoiler tag contains the stages where I learnt skills.
steps.heading: Endless Tower

steps.text: Stage 1 - Trial 1: [Monoco Skill - Ramasseur Bonk] + [Monoco Skill - Gault Fury]
Stage 1 - Trial 2: [Monoco Skill - Potier Energy]
Stage 1 - Trial 3: [Monoco Skill - Duallist Storm]
Stage 2 - Trial 3: [Monoco Skill - Lampmaster Light]
Stage 4 - Trial 1: [Monoco Skill - Orphelin Cheers]
Stage 4 - Trial 2: [Monoco Skill - Jar Lampstorm] + [Monoco Skill - Rocher Hammering]
Stage 5 - Trial 2: [Monoco Skill - Sapling Absorption]
Stage 6 - Trial 2: [Monoco Skill - Glaise Earhquakes]
Stage 11 - Trial 2: [Monoco Skill - Creation Void]

During my time in the tower, I had been leveling up Maelle's Medalum weapon and at this point got it to level 32. I still had the Perfect Chroma Catalyst from when we found it in the story, so I upgraded it to level 33 here and unlocked:

No stress if you don't have it yet. If you've been leveling a weapon consistently, you will almost certainly get it done by the end of this area, provided you looted the aforementioned Perfect Chroma Catalyst. After reaching Stage 7, I left and started the Flying Manor area below. If you are having no issues then feel free to continue on in the tower the whole way or until you do struggle. There is no penalty or missable for going back and forth to different areas.
For winning the final battle you will automatically obtain [Record #33/34 - Clea] and as this is also the end of the tower, you will unlock the achievement below for finishing it:

steps.name: “Endless”
steps.description: Reach the top of the Endless Tower.

steps.text: You should have every Monoco skill now, bar one. So let's go and get the final one! Head to the location below where you will find an enemy called Gross Tete.

At this level and with end-game abilities, you should make short work of the boss, it's nothing special at this point. On defeating the boss, you will receive your final [Monoco Skill - Gross Tete Whack]. Assuming this is your last skill, you will unlock:
If you are missing any skills, you can check Monoco's skill tree and then compare with the listed skills on the collectible page.

When you have finished with the tower, or if you have leveled up and fancy a break, it's time for another end-game area, the Flying Manor. Head to the location below and enter. It may still say "Danger!" if you are at a certain level but this is with regards to the boss at the end, you should be able to clear up to that point if coming here earlier.

Take the path ahead the only way you can until you reach a large island with display cases in the middle. There is a flag here and an NPC. Speak to the NPC to learn that to open the door to "her", you need to return the colour to the paintings in the display cases. Head to the flag and go past it to what looks like four ropes. This is actually a lift. Take it up and again, follow the path. You will see two statues ahead. Go behind the one on the left for a Colour of Lumina. Continue on and grapple over the gap. This is a crossroads, with a path left, ahead and to the right, as well as some large enemies. Loot another Colour of Lumina here and then take the left path, defeating the enemy in the way.
steps.heading: Flying Manor

steps.text: There is a merchant here you can fight to unlock a whole host of level 28 pictos. I won't list them all here but the merchant himself is no different to other merchant fights other than he may one-shot you depending on your level. He also sells a few level 28 weapons. Crawl under the gap past the merchant and loot the Grandiose Chroma Catalyst from back here. Now return to the crossroads and take the path to the left, again defeating the enemy on the way.

Take the path to the right and continue until you grapple across a couple of platforms. On the other side, you will fight Goblu, a boss you may have already fought recently in the Endless Tower. That is the "gimmick" of this area essentially. Each display cabinet in the plaza is a boss you must defeat in order to reach the end boss of this area. I won't repeat the tactics for Goblu but if you need a refresher, his moves can be found in Act I of the WT.

With Goblu defeated, loot the "Energising Shots" pictos from the back left of this area and then speak to the NPC here to return to the main hub of this area. Rest at the flag if you need to and then head to the center of the area where the display cases are. Find the archway with a long set of stairs leading down and take the rope at the end. There is another lift ahead that will take you even further down. Take more stairs until you reach a large open area with some big enemies. Pan the camera to the right to see a large enemy that we have fought a few times before. Go to and defeat it, and then take the rope it was guarding. Take the path up, following the lamps and you will fight the Lampmaster again. As with Goblu, this fight has the same moves as the Act I fight, it's just beefed up to a higher level.

Note that this boss drops a Perfect Chroma Catalyst so if you did not loot the one mentioned in the story, you can now use this to upgrade someone's weapon to level 33 and unlock the corresponding achievement. Speak with the boy to again return to the main hub. Rest at the flag if you need to and then look towards the back of this area, where the grapple point to the end boss is. Looking this way, turn right and go to the edge of the main hub. There is a large picture frame here that you can drop onto. Do so and then head for the corner straight ahead. You will see a grapple point you can use.

Run along the next frame, grapple again and then drop down through the gap in the balcony. The large enemy ahead is Eveque, one of the first bosses you fought in the game and the third in this area. You actually fight three variants together here but they all have the same moves. There is nothing too fancy honestly. This boss also drops another Perfect Chroma Catalyst. As usual, speak to the boy after the battle to return once more to the main hub.

For the final path, head past the area with the lift, keeping the lift on your right hand side. You will see a narrow ramp leading up. At the top of the ramp, you will see a purple item across the gap that you can't reach at the moment, and some handholds to your right. Take the handholds and grapple across the gap to the top. Defeat or skip the enemies here and head straight on, up the steps to face Dualliste once more. This guy was one-shotting me with most attacks at level 80 so I did end up spamming Stendhal and revives here a little but your mileage may vary. He drops yet another Perfect Chroma Catalyst when defeated. Speak to the boy and return to the main hub for the last time.

You can now challenge the boss in this area. Personally, this is one of the last things I did as both this boss and another end-game boss are quite tricky. I will include the fight details below now as you will have to fight her eventually for one of the remaining achievements.

The "Anti-Stun" pictos is a godsend for this fight. I would highly recommend getting it and equipping to all of your characters before fighting this boss. It is obtained from defeating the Chromatic Petank, which is covered further down in the guide. Defeating the Petank is very simple at higher levels and unlocks an achievement anyway so I would urge you to at least do that and then come back. "Anti-Freeze" is also useful. You may have it already, but if not, it is found in the paint cage located in the Frozen Hearts area.
steps.heading: ??? - General Info

steps.text: I put the notes part first with this fight only as it's pivotal to understand from the off how the fight works. Every time you fail to parry an attack, the boss will heal a large amount. This amount does vary by difficulty and on higher difficulties it is basically a full heal. The boss herself doesn't fight you directly. Instead, she summons different types of Nevrons that perform attacks against you that must be parried. The pop-up will tell you which type of Nevron is next and you will have to learn each moveset and parry accordingly to succeed.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Don't worry about damage until you are confident about what attacks do what and how to parry them as if the boss gets one heal off, any damage you've done will almost certainly be for nothing anyway. Just take it easy and learn it a step at a time. Gommage followed by Stendhal will deal crazy damage as well but it won't help you as much as you might think given the healing the boss does. You really do just need to learn this one.

Musical Nevrons - A 5 hit attack. This is quite fast but easy to learn once you've seen it a couple of times. There will be four of the trumpet Nevrons back to back that "fire" at you, followed by a slower wind-up attack at the end.
steps.heading: Abilities

steps.text: Creepy Nevrons - A 4 hit attack. The Nevrons appear close and swipe at you. I found this one harder to parry because of the Nevrons proximity to you and because their attacks aren't the easiest to see. If the large enemy at the end gets a hit off, it will stun the character. This is especially bad as I often found my stunned character would get chain stunned, stopping you from parrying for a good few turns. This can get very frustrating.

Powerful Nevrons - This is one of the easier ones. An enemy will lunge from the left, another from ahead and then a big enemy will jump from the sky. If the attacks connect they will stun you if you don't have Anti-Stun.

Agile Nevrons - This first appears below 75% health. It's a 7 hit combo. The big enemy behind will twirl around a bit but is only the final two hits of the combo, do not get distracted by him. The other 6 hits all come from the smaller enemy jabbing at you.

Violent Nevrons - Another move that appears below 75% health. This is a long, 7 hit combo that alternates between a parryable hit and a jump counter. I find this really hard to see. Don't forget about the final hit at the end that has a slow wind-up. The alternating attacks are very fast, you have to hit the parry straight away after the jump, other than the final hit.

Nevrons from the Deep - There are two variants to this. The first time it is cast, a giant enemy appears that swallows a character. As with the versions of this you've fought before, the character is gone for now and there is no way to stop this. The second time onwards, this is a long combo that I found mega confusing as it consists of multiple different enemies swiping at you.
You will receive the below achievement for defeating the boss:

I now chose to tackle the Painting Workshop, another high-level area with an achievement tied to it. This does require a bit of legwork (literally) before you can get it done but it's not as bad as some of the platforming you've done by now. First off, head slightly east, to the image below and enter. This is one of 3 painting workshops you will have to traverse,

Inside, there is a platforming puzzle of sorts where you must work your down to the giant picture below where you will find the Fading Boy. Speak to him and then choose "we will". From here you must now work your way down further until you reach a larger area with statues. Annoyingly if you fall off, you will return to the entrance. I found these not so bad as the game has no fall damage so you can skip large chunks of the platforming simply by landing further down. Once on the large platform, approach the statue of the Lampmaster and interact with it to place the lamp. The boss becomes accessible when all three lamps are placed. Head behind the statue and look to the right for a portal which will return you to the Continent. Now head to the second Painting Workshop location below:

Repeat the process. Platform down to the boy, speak to him to receive the quest item and then platform down further to the statue. Place the lamp and then leave via the portal behind. Finally, head to the location below, note that it is in the air, on a small island.

Repeat the process again only this time, instead of leaving behind the statue, continue on to the end. The enemy is yet again...the Lampmaster. This is just another beefed up version with the same moves as its other iterations. The boss does hit hard but equally at this level you will do a lot of damage back, particularly if you counter. Abilities like Stendhal in virtuoso stance will do the work here if you prefer that route. The only move you really need to worry about is the "massive sword of light" as it will wipe your group entirely if it hits. I just focused on dodging this and parrying everything else. Stendhal can hit for anywhere up to 3million+ with roulette. For defeating the boss, you will obtain various pictos and other items, as well as unlocking the below achievement:

Now it's time to take out a world boss or two and tick off some more achievements. Find the Flying Casino on your map and head just north of it to find a purple worm thing in the sky. Fly into it to start a battle with the Serpenphare.
Tail Swipe - The boss will swipe its tail from left to right. Parry just before it hits and then be ready to jump counter. It can do this 2, 4 or 6 times as the fight goes on.
steps.heading: Serpenphare - Attacks

steps.text: Laser Attack - The popup will say "the boss attacks". This is an easy attack that pulses to indicate a parry. It can be done in 3,5 or 7 hits and the last will always be a gradient counter.

Head Slam - The boss slams its head into the whole group. This can happen as 2, 4 or 6 hits. The boss always does this two hits at a time. Wait till just before it slams its head to parry the first, then be ready to parry again.
AP Absorb - The boss will intermittently drain all AP from party members.
Shield + Speed - The boss increases its speed and gives itself shields
Freeze Beam - Similar to laser attack but with more delayed timing, the boss will attempt to freeze each party member in turn. Wait for the 2 pulses, then parry.
Silencing attack - This is very animated but easy to dodge. Dodge just before each of the three comets hits you.

Explosion - If the boss absorbs too much AP in one turn, it will do this attack. The boss will pulse a few times, getting quicker each time until it explodes. If you don't dodge or parry, it will wipe your group.

This boss can probably be done much sooner but I found it kind of annoying so saved it till I was more leveled. There is no way to avoid the AP drain. Making sure each character has the "Cheater" pictos equipped will allow them to play twice in a row. Provided you defeated Sprong on the previous page, you will have this pictos. Having two goes at once is good for using energy tints to get off powerful attacks such as Stendhal.
steps.heading: Additional Information

steps.text: Additionally, Maelle's shield break ability gives her 1 AP for every shield broken so using this will give her full AP. I preferred leaving the shields until Maelle's turn for this purpose. As usual, you will get a good chunk of damage through counters. Make sure to read the popup with regards to how many times the boss attacks as it does change. I tried to always use my AP and avoid the explosion attack entirely. If you do get it, I'd advise dodging rather than trying to go for the parry as it will more than likely take out your whole party if it hits. Avoiding it will break and stun the boss so this is a valid tactic if you can repeatedly evade the explosion.
With the boss defeated, you will obtain a nice pictos, a Perfect Chroma Catalyst and unlock the below achievement:
Now for another world boss which at your current level you should have no issue with. Head to the location below, where you will find a Petank.

This is a Chromatic Petank and, like the many you've seen throughout the game, must be herded to its pad before it can be fought. It's a bit of a long path to herd it along but it's also easier to cut it off and manipulate the direction as you are flying. From where you find it, you want to guide it south on the map, through the river and then around and up to the pad. The area itself has limited paths so it shouldn't take you long to find it. Once on the pad, fight the enemy.

Assuming you are high level, you will have no issue here. The boss will call other petanks to help but just focus on doing damage to the boss itself. At high level you will defeat it in no time with little chance for it to attack. If you fail or if the boss defeats you, you will need to enter any area in the game and then return to the Continent in order for the Petank to respawn at its original location. For defeating the Petank, you will unlock the below achievement:
This boss also drops the "Anti-Stun" pictos which is mentioned above as a key item for fighting the boss in the Flying Manor.

At this point we have very little left to do. The only achievements you should have left now are for beating the final super-boss, reaching level 99, and if you missed a record, the achievement for this as well as any character specific achievements that you haven't picked up through natural play. You might think that the final super-boss requires level 99 but it really doesn't as the fight is more reliant on mechanics over characters being level capped. However, as mentioned at the start of the post-game, you do want ALL of your characters are a decent level and with good skills equipped as they will have fight time on the last boss.

If some of your B team is lacking a bit, you need to get to level 99 anyway so there is no harm in grinding some levels now until you feel comfortable, challenging the final boss and then finishing the grind. The way I've tackled this is that I go to the area that leads to the super-boss now, collecting the final unique record along the way before challenging the boss. I've also included grinding spots after the super-boss to get to level 99. These can be used now or after the boss, it's entirely up to you. Head to the location in the image below to enter this end-game area. Note that you should level up a bit naturally here anyway as you make your way through. The enemies are challenging and give good XP anyway.

Take the path down from the flag and at the bottom take the sharp left. Use the grapple point to reach the top of the building with the faces on and take the slope down. Look to the right for a purple item. Loot it for [Record #34/34 - Endless Light]. If you didn't pop it earlier, and provided you haven't missed both of the missable records, you should now unlock:
steps.heading: Renoir's Drafts

steps.text: If you defeat the enemies nearby here, you can loot the "Quick Break" pictos. Return to the start of the area and take the other path this time, defeating the group of enemies here and then following the path the only way you can, defeating another set of enemies after climbing a low ledge. Then follow the ramp up. You can speak to the Fading Man on the right. Equip the Anti-Blight pictos if you don't have it on and then engage the enemies ahead.

Take the path to the right and defeat the enemies here, looting the Grandiose Chroma Catalyst they were guarding, before taking the ramp down to the right. There is another Grandiose Catalyst under the ramp you just went down. There are two paths ahead but the one we want is the straight forward path with the two Creation enemies. Yes, this area does the repeat enemies thing also I'm afraid. Defeat the creations and then loot another Grandiose Catalyst from behind the statue straight ahead.

Facing the statue in the middle, take a right turn and you will see another Creation ahead. You can slip past this if you like or fight it. To continue towards the final super-boss take the tight right turn back up a ramp to find a flag. You can explore more of the area if you wish. When ready, head upwards and take the swirling portal to enter...

This is it. There is nothing here but the final super-boss. There are various different ways to beat what is coming up. As usual, I have put the actual fight information in spoilers. For full disclosure, I fought him on the easiest difficulty as I did not want to cheese with super-builds and that kind of thing. It's entirely up to you how you fight him. I will be detailing the mechanics he does and such so that you can fight him normally and learn his patterns if you wish but there are a plethora of cheese videos and guides available also if you want to go down that route. When ready, follow the tunnel and drop off the end of the path.
steps.heading: The Abyss

steps.text: There is a flag here you can rest at to tinker with builds and such. When ready, approach the figure for a cutscene.

As with the boss above, I put some general info here first as it's pivotal to know this before fighting Simon. This is a 3 phase fight where in the 3rd phase, Simon will wipe out your party, forcing your "spare" characters to come in. Because of this, you actually want to fight the first two phases with the two members of your B team so that you have the main 3 characters coming in at the end of the fight. This is why I mentioned leveling them up as you will learn the bulk of this fight with them.
steps.heading: Simon - General Information

steps.text: Outside of this and the amount of damage Simon does, the attacks he does are very fast and can be immensely frustrating to learn. A lot of people find this fight frustrating and unfun and there are lots of cheese build guides available that will allow you to decimate the boss with little issue. If you choose to learn the boss, it is no different than anything else in the game and just requires time and learning parries.

The moves mostly stay the same throughout the fight in that phase 1 introduces you to the short, long and powerful combos that exist in all 3 phases. Phase 2 introduces the light speed and sword of Lumiére moves. At around 40% of health remaining in phase 2, Simon will remove your current team from the battle. Assuming this is your two B team members, this will allow you to bring in the heavy hitters for Phase 3.

In Phase 2, Simon's combos essentially become double hits. For every hit he does, another sword will hit as well. To get around this you need to learn to double parry, essentially hitting the button once for Simon and immediately again for the follow-up. This is then made more complicated in phase 3 where each hit has two additional follow-ups requiring 3 parries. If you don't use a cheese build, it could well be worth at least watching a video of the later phases once you've made it there so that you have a better idea of what each attack looks like but it's of course up to you.

Levels don't really matter at this point but you can eek out some stats by reaching 99 if you wish. If Simon hits you it will likely kill you regardless, with this being a certainty if multiple attacks connect. Focus on parrying and learning the fight for the first few attempts and build on that knowledge as the fight goes on.
Remove Dead - If any party member dies, Simon will remove them from the fight. Note that if you get a turn before his next one, you can revive.
steps.heading: Simon - Phase One - Attacks

steps.text: Sword Plant - The popup says that Simon plants his sword in the ground. He then performs a 5 hit punching combo. This is well telegraphed and quite easily parried.
Gather Chroma - If this hits, it will reduce you to 1 HP.
Powerful Combo - A slow 3 hit combo with the sword
Long Combo - A slow 6 hit combo
Short Combo - A 3 hit combo. There is a slow first parry, a jump counter and then another parry.
Note that everything in this phase is faster and essentially requires you to hit parry twice to reasonably parry in time. Most of the moves are the same as P1 but with more hits added
steps.heading: Phase Two - Attacks

steps.text: Powerful Combo - This is now a 6 hit combo. Each hit from Simon is immediately followed by another hit. This is essentially 2x2x2 hits. Remember to double parry by hitting the parry button twice.
Long Combo - This is now a 12 hit combo and a total mess to explain. Every hit has another hit after it but not necessarily immediately.
Short Combo - Again, this is the same move but with an extra hit after each attack.

Light Speed - This is very hard to describe and really requires seeing first, either on your own or via a video. It's a 10 hit combo that is very erratic. However, it does have a rhythm to it that you can learn like almost everything else in the game.
Sword of Lumiére - A 7 hit combo. Again, this looks quite daunting but at this stage in the game it's just committing and learning. It is well telegraphed so with time, you will learn it.
At the start of this phase, Simon will remove all members of your current group. This should ideally still be your two B team members. You now have your best 3 team members in for the last phase.
steps.heading: Phase Three - Attacks

steps.text: This is just a more souped up version of Phase 2. His three combo moves now have a hit followed by 2 follow up hits. For example, the short combo is now 9 hits. The light speed and sword abilities remain the same.
Once Simon is defeated, you will unlock the below achievement:
You can also loot the final journal from this area, [Journal #49/49 - Simon] which will unlock:

steps.name: Follow The Trail
steps.description: Find all of the journals from prior expeditions.

steps.text: Outside of miscellaneous character achievements, all that you should have left now is getting to level 99. I have outlined one possible grinding spot below. It is boring and takes a while but it's the final hurdle and then you're done. You can try mixing up grinding spots to keep it fresh or you can also start NG+ at any flag. I'm unsure what the XP gain is like in NG+ but if you're planning another run at the game anyway, it might be better than grinding. Just make sure you have absolutely everything done before doing this as I believe most things do not transfer over. There are plenty of different grinding methods that can be found online too so it may be worth experimenting to see what personally works for you.
For one possible grinding spot, head to the location below and enter "Dark Shores".

This is actually the beach from the opening cutscenes. There is nothing fancy or technical to this. The enemies here give good amounts of XP and there is a flag nearby to rest and reset. I fought the 3 packs of enemies closest to the flag and then reset and went again. Any end-game areas that give XP are viable but this has good XP in proximity to a flag. Note that you only need one character to hit level 99 to get the achievement. Note that without the no dmg xp bonus, this is slow...very slow. The enemies are basic but have a tonne of health. Once you learn their patterns, it's a good farm but it's frustrating at first. I mixed this up with other methods myself to keep it fresh.
steps.heading: Dark Shores

steps.text: Once your first character hits level 99, you will unlock:

Outside of a few miscellaneous or character achievements, you should now be done! All of the character achievements can be found on the next page with explanations for each. The collectibles page details the whereabouts of all collectibles if you are missing any. If this was your last achievement then I hope you enjoyed the game and that the WT was helpful!

This page details how to unlock any miscellaneous character achievements you may be missing. It is highly unlikely you finish everything else and still have all of these locked but you may need a couple depending on which characters you play more of. I did not cover the character specific achievements in the guide outside of the Prologue as I felt that most would be unlocked through natural play. They are therefore listed here to be finished off for those who need them.
steps.heading: Character Achievements

steps.name: Overcharge
steps.description: With Gustave, use a fully charged Overcharge that Breaks an enemy.
steps.heading: Gustave

steps.text: This achievement can be unlocked in the prologue when you fight the Mime. Simply use abilities with Gustave until your Overcharge is full and then attack the Mime. The attack should break it, unlocking the achievement. You can also get this with most enemies throughout Act I.

steps.name: Perfect Flow
steps.description: With Lune, consume Stains 4 turns in a row.
steps.heading: Lune

steps.text: Lune's abilities work by generating and spending stains. When looking at Lune's skills in battle, the icons to the left of the AP amount will be the stains generated. As an example, one of Lune's first skills, "Immolation", generates one fire/red stain when cast and will consume an ice/blue stain if present. The idea of this achievement is to consume one stain every turn for 4 turns in a row. The endless tower is perfect for any endgame miscellaneous achievements as you can simply turn on the enemy health modifier and there is no risk of the enemies dying too quickly.

There are many ways this can be done but an easy way to follow along with uses the "Electrify" and "Earth Rising" abilities. Use "Electrify" twice to generate 4 electric/yellow stains and then use "Earth Rising" 4 times. Each use of "Earth Rising" will consume on electric stain. When all 4 electric stains are consumed, the achievement will pop.

steps.name: Synergy
steps.description: With Maelle, use Percée on a Marked enemy while in Virtuose Stance.
steps.heading: Maelle

steps.text: This is a very quick and simple achievement, assuming you picked up Maelle's Medalum weapon back in the Gestral Village. Make sure Maelle is not first in the turn order, which can be changed by adding/removing party members. I did this with Sciel but any ability that puts mark on an enemy works too. Make sure Maelle has the "Percée" ability equipped and that Sciel has "Marking Card". Go into battle with just these two so there is no messing around skipping turns. Use "Marking Card" on an enemy with Sciel and then use "Percée" on Maelle's turn to unlock the achievement. As the Medalum weapon starts Maelle in Virtuoso stance, that is all there is to it.

If you don't have Medalum, there are a couple more steps but the achievement is still easy. A quick way to get Maelle into Virtuoso stance is to apply the burn effect either with Maelle herself with abilities like "Rain of Fire", "Pyrolyse" or "Spark". Then use "Swift Stride" to trigger Virtuoso on her next turn and go from there.

steps.name: Wheel Control
steps.description: With Monoco, cast an Upgraded Skill 4 turns in a row.
steps.heading: Monoco

steps.text: This achievement is best done with the more skills for Monoco you have. At the very least you will need one of each skill (Heavy, Caster, Agile and Balanced). Each turn Monoco has, his wheel will correspond with one of these masks. The idea of the achievement is to always use a skill that matches the wheel. Matching the wheel results in an upgraded version of that skill. If the wheel is on Almighty, ANY of the masks can be used, it does not have to be an almighty mask but you can also equip an almighty skill if you wish.

Ideally you want to go for low AP cost skills as the wheel is random and will not do one after the other. Unlike some of the other character achievements, I would recommend starting the battle with all 3 characters as the other characters you use can spend energy tints on Monoco to keep him topped. The lowest AP cost abilities of each mask are as follows:
Agile Mask - Ramasseur Bonk, Lancelier Impale or Abbest Wind (2 AP)
Caster Mask - Demineur Thunder or Ballet Charm (2 AP)
Balanced Mask - Sakapatate Estoc or Gault Furty (3 AP)
Heavy Mask - Rocher Hammering, Cultist Blood or Boucheclier Fortify (3 AP)
Almighty Mask - Lampmaster Light (5 AP) - Again not necessary as any can be used as Almighty, but if you want to be sure, it's here.

Once you have the skills set up, I'd again advise either turning the enemy health modifier on or going into endgame battles where they won't die easily. Keep Monoco topped up with energy tints from the other characters. This, combined with a spread of low AP abilities on each mask, should make it quite easy to match the wheel four times. Once 4 upgraded/matched abilities have been used, the achievement will unlock.

steps.name: Maximisation
steps.description: With Sciel, consume 20 Foretell on a single target during Twilight.
steps.heading: Sciel

steps.text: For this achievement I'd recommend starting a battle with all 3 characters so that they can use energy tints on Sciel if needed to help. Some of Sciel's abilities apply Foretell and others consume it. Outside of Twilight, Sciel can only apply up to 10 Foretell on an enemy, with this number raising to 20 when Twilight is active. The aim of the achievement is to consume all 20 Foretell on an enemy whilst twilight is active.

When the battle starts, use "Focused Foretell" to immediately apply 5/10 Foretell. Then use "Searing Bond" on the next turn to apply another 5. This caps us at 10/10 Foretell. We will get the other 10 Foretell needed in Twilight mode, but not quite yet. First use other sun abilities like "Rush" to get enough for one gradient charge. Other sun abilities or AP abilities from other characters are fine as long as the enemy doesn't die and as long as you don't consume Foretell. Just don't use any moon abilities yet. Once you have the one gradient charge, use moon abilities like "Twilight Slash" to get into Twilight mode. Once in Twilight mode, use Sciel's basic gradient charge attack, "Shadow Bringer". This hits 10 times and applies 1 Foretell per hit which will result in you reaching the 20 Foretell.

On the next turn, provided you are still in Twilight mode, use any ability which consumes ALL Foretell such as "Harvest" or "Phantom Blade" etc. Consuming all 20 Foretell at once will unlock the achievement. If you are no longer in Twilight mode, don't worry. The Foretell stacks will not time out. Just use a combination of sun and moon abilities, making sure not to consume any Foretell until you re-enter Twilight mode. Then use the consuming ability next time around.

This achievement is either one you will find easy or one that is more difficult depending how you are with parrying. Verso works on a grading system, a bit like games like DMC where the better you fight, the higher your grade goes. Getting hit by abilities will drop your grade so you need to repeatedly parry to raise your grade to S. There are some things which help make this easier though. One is to drop the difficulty to "Story" if not already as this makes the parry window much bigger. Secondly is to use the "Gaulteram" weapon as instead of losing a full rank on being hit, you will only lose a little bit. The weapon is obtained by defeating the giant Bourgeon enemy near the Stone Wave Cliffs in act I. You can also buy it from a vendor in the post-game at a higher rank, though for this you only need it to be at least level 4.

There are a couple of ways you can go about obtaining the achievement. The simplest is just to go into battle with Verso alone and parry until you reach S rank. Another is to make sure you have the "Perfect Break" ability. This ability automatically switches you to S rank once an enemy is broken. There is no specific enemy to use this on but I would recommend trying a few fights in the endless tower early on or out in the open world. The ability can sometimes break an enemy regardless of their current break status so it is worth just using the ability and seeing also. Whichever way you choose to do it, once Verso hits rank S in battle, the achievement will unlock.
